Manoş said they want Abdullah Öcalan to be granted physical freedom as soon as possible and for his status to be recognized.


Condolences to the families of the martyrs


Manoş conveyed, on behalf of the group, his condolences to the families of the Kurdistan Freedom Guerrillas following the reported deaths.

author: groundxero
title: Artificial Intelligence: Private Ownership, Collective Risks
content:
Just as capitalism destroys the environment in pursuit of profit, it is today destroying the human mind through an artificial intelligence subject to the logic of competition, profit and domination.


 


Rezgar Akrawi


Via

Globetrotter


 


On 8 September 2026 the researcher

Jacob Coxon resigned

 from Anthropic, declaring that the two largest companies in the field are ‘gambling with our lives,’ and the people building these systems ‘earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.’


 


His concern was not an isolated one. Tens of thousands of people, among them leading scientists, have signed

an international statement

 demanding a ban on the development of ‘superintelligence’ until there is scientific consensus that it is safe.

The International AI Safety Report

 warned of the growing ability of models to dodge evaluation and get around the tests.


 


And the danger is not entirely hypothetical.

The UK AI Security Institute

 revealed that during a controlled security evaluation artificial intelligence agents carried out 19 unauthorized actions targeting real people and organizations, with no actual harm recorded. Anthropic, in

its September security report

, documents the automation of an entire attack chain directed at various companies.


 


On 12 September the digital capitalist corporations broke their silence. Dario Amodei published an essay titled

‘We Must Pace the Frontier’

, calling on his industry to slow the AI development race. Within hours

Sam Altman

 announced that he was adopting the same step, Elon Musk wrote ‘Dario is right,’ and Demis Hassabis of Google DeepMind joined them.

The three companies revealed

 that they had been in talks on this question for weeks.


 


This position reveals a fundamental contradiction. The companies are aware of the risks, yet they operate inside a competition that pushes every one of them to keep racing for fear of losing its place. In my view, calls for a slowdown are liable to remain limited or merely formal unless they turn into binding rules and independent oversight. Two days later

Mark Zuckerberg and Jensen Huang rejected

 any coordinated slowdown, and Huang held that ‘the market forces are already there, we don’t need any new laws.’


 


The response of the US administration came quickly. On 14 September

Donald Trump described

 these warnings as a ‘hoax’ and a ‘sick conspiracy’ and wrote ‘Don’t kill the Golden Goose,’ while his vice president JD Vance called the companies’ demand for regulation a ‘Trojan horse.’


 


This comes within a wider struggle over the relationship between the far right and digital capital. It runs from Elon Musk, who places the X platform at the service of right-wing forces worldwide, to Peter Thiel and

the Palantir manifesto

, which I have treated as an expression of a new fascism in its digital form. On the same day a completely different position came from

the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights

, insisting that ‘no company should be able to decide by itself which risks the world must accept.’


 


When Artificial Intelligence Becomes a Weapon of Mass Destruction


 


What we are witnessing now is a stark model of digital control, in which algorithms decide what reaches individuals and what is kept from them, and are designed to serve

the logic of the capitalist model

. Their effect on consciousness is no longer a hypothesis.

A study published in the journal Science

, covering some 77,000 participants, found that conversation with these models can shift political positions, and showed their capacity to persuade and to influence consciousness.


 


What makes this control more dangerous is its voluntary character, since individuals are pushed into

‘

digital servitude’

 without direct coercion and under the illusion of control and choice.


 


Here a fundamental difference emerges between the concept of freedom on the left and its concept in neoliberalism. The neoliberal view tends to reduce freedom to individual choice among the digital options available on the market. The left sees it instead as an actual capacity to control the conditions of life, work and knowledge, and to take part in building the digital options that shape the life of the individual and of society. A freedom whose conditions are not owned or controlled by the person exercising it is therefore not a complete freedom, since it remains a choice among what capital has …

author: Agatha Hazel Rabino
title: Pagtanggal ng pangil sa mapangahas na buhay ng isang rebolusyonaryo
content:
Sa mahabang kasaysayan ng kilusang kabataang estudyante, hindi na bago sa pandinig ang pangalang Edgar “Edjop” Jopson. Batikang lider-estudyante at tagapangulo ng National Union of Students of the Philippines (NUSP), kalaunan ay organisador ng mga manggagawa sa makasaysayang welga ng La Tondeña, at sa huli’y organisador sa komunidad at kanayunan sa Mindanao. Hindi alintanang tinahak niya ang masalimuot na buhay ng isang rebolusyonaryo noong kasagsagan ng Batas Militar.

Waring naimortalisa na ang hindi matatawarang ambag ni Edjop sa pambansa-demokratikong pakikibaka ng sambayanang Pilipino. Hindi normal na landas ang mangahas na baguhin ang lipunan sa radikal na pamamaraan. Sa pagbaybay sa maikli ngunit makabuluhang buhay ni Edjop, maaaninag ang pagkamulat ng isang nakaaalwan at ideyalistang estudyante mula sa Ateneo tungo sa isang lider-masang pinanday ng kampanya at pakikibaka para sa pambansang demokrasya. Na ito ay isang desisyong inanak mula sa sakripisyo at literal na dugo at pawis. “Buhay man ay ialay”, tulad ng madalas na panata ng mga aktibista’t rebolusyonaryo.

Marahil ito ang thesis na nais palitawin ng pelikulang Edjop ni Katski Flores. Isang biopic na humalaw ng inspirasyon sa tunay na kasaysayan ng buhay ni Edgar Jopson, sinikap isabuhay ng pelikula ang tao sa likod ng pigurang si Edjop. Subalit sa kabuuang daloy ng pelikula, hindi rin mapigilang paglimian kung epektibo bang gamitin ang punto-de-bista ni Joyette, ang anak na literal na tinakbuhan ang legasiya ng kanyang ama?

Isang creative choice na nga siguro ang paggamit sa lente ni Joyette (Jodi Sta. Maria) upang makilala at maunawaan ang kanyang “tats” na si Edjop (Elijah Canlas). Sa pagbaybay sa pelikula, na nahahati sa flashbacks ng buhay ni Edjop at buhay ni Joyette, nakikita ang kontradiksyon ng anak na kilalanin ang ama. Paano nga naman niya kikilalanin ang ama na hindi niya maalala nang hindi nakukulayan ng hinanakit o pagkadismaya sa mga naging desisyon niya sa kanyang buhay? Sa mata ni Joyette, marami mang bersyon ng Edjop, ang nangingibabaw sa kanya ay ang Edjop na wala na.

Isinabuhay sa pelikula ang matagal na proseso ni Joyette sa pag-unawa sa legasiya ng kanyang ama. Marahil, ang pagiging atleta ang pamamaraan para mapagdugtong ang pagkakapareho ng mag-ama: ang ambisyon na mag-ambag ng legasiya sa bayan. Marahil, si Joyette ang ginamit na punto-de-bista ng direktor para maging relatable ang pagkilatis sa isang pigura ng aktibismo, dahil hindi niya direktang nakasalamuha ang ama at mas “obhetibo” ang pagkilala niya kay Edjop bilang isang indibidwal.

Kung ito man ang intensyon, lumabas na hindi rin epektibong nagamit na behikulo si Joyette, dahil may bahid na ng prejudice ang pagkakasulat sa karakter na ito. Sa buong pelikula, waring tinatakbuhan ni Joyette ang katotohanan na rebolusyonaryo ang kanyang ama. Hindi rin malinaw sa pelikula kung paano nabagtas ni Joyette ang pagkilala sa buhay at pakikibaka ni Edjop, liban na lang sa huling minuto ng pelikula na inamin niyang para sa kanya, isang “konsepto” ang kanyang ama at kalauna’y kinilala niya ang sakripisyo at pagmamahal ni Edjop para sa kanyang pamilya at bayan.

Sa ganitong treatment sa subject ng biopic, lumitaw ang disjoint sa pagitan ni Edjop at Joyette. Waring nakukulayan ng cynical point of view ni Joyette ang sequences ng buhay ni Edjop. Habang pinapanood ang pelikula, hindi ko maiwasang tanungin ang sarili, ito ba ay tungkol kay Edjop o tungkol sa pagkilala ni Joyette kay Edjop?

Bagaman mahusay ang paggampan ng pangunahing mga aktor, kapos ang karakterisasyon ng script para i-humanize ang “konseptong” si Edjop. Bagaman inilahad ang mga mahahalagang pangyayari sa buhay ni Edjop, nananatiling surface–level at palaisipan ang katauhan ni Edjop sa pelikula. Pinapakita man ang kanyang pagkamulat, hindi napalalim ang araw-araw niyang pakikibaka at sakripisyo sa lahat ng mga responsibilidad na tinanganan niya.

Hindi ako dinala ng pelikula na lubos na yakapin ang kanyang mga adhikain, kahit sa mga eksenang nagpapahayag siya ng kanyang pagtindig para sa karapatan ng karaniwang tao. Lapses sa script or dahil si Joyette ang frame of reference at ito ang kanyang appreciation sa buhay at pakikibaka ng kanyang ama? Ano man sa dalawa, litaw na ito ang malaking kahinaan ng pelikula para sa akin.

Sa filmmaking, lalo ng mga biopic, hindi maiwasang lagyan ng artistic license ang subject ng pelikula para sa entertainment factor. Kaiba sa paggawa ng dokumentaryo, tunay namang may kalayaan …

author: James Plested
title: Victorian Socialists’ election campaign in full swing
content:
The Victorian state election will take place in just over two months, on Saturday 28 November. The Victorian Socialists’ campaign is now in full swing, with local campaign activity taking place daily across Melbourne and regional Victoria.

The scale of the campaign—with VS candidates set to run in all 88 lower house seats and all eight upper house regions across Victoria—is beyond anything the socialist left in Australia has attempted for generations (if ever). Even just a few years ago, a statewide campaign like this would have been unthinkable. That it’s happening at all is something of a breakthrough.

Between 1 June and 19 September, VS volunteers knocked on more than 80,000 doors, already well on track to reach the 2022 campaign total of around 190,000. The party received around 2,000 requests for campaign signs to be put on front fences and in yards, eclipsing the 2022 total of 1,000, with hundreds of orders a week still coming in. More than 2,400 people donated to the campaign, and almost 1,800 registered for a party event. 

New branches are springing up everywhere. Wherever they do, we’re finding people who want to get involved. VS events in places like Pakenham, a suburb on the far south-eastern fringe of Melbourne—more than 50 kilometres from the CBD—are attracting many new faces. And we now have active branches in regional centres including Geelong, Warrnambool, Ballarat and Bendigo, and the beginnings of branches in Shepparton, Wodonga and Warragul. 

We’re accustomed to being almost completely overlooked by the mainstream media, but the sheer size of our campaign this time means we’re increasingly difficult to ignore.

ABC News reported

 on the VS campaign launch on 1 August, and Channel 9 reported on our “all-in” Footscray doorknock on Sunday 16 August, which was attended by more than 350 volunteers. VS candidate for the Northern Metro upper house region Omar Hassan has become something of a regular fixture on talkback radio 3AW’s morning show with Tom Elliot—most recently on the topic

“what is socialism?”

VS candidates in the regions are attracting particular attention.

Hera Sheppard,

 in the seat of

South-West Coast

 (comprising Warrnambool, Port Fairy, Portland and surrounds), has been featured in several articles in the

Warrnambool Standard

, including the front cover. An

article at ABC News

 and an appearance on ABC Radio followed—the latter

drawing the ire

 of Australia’s richest billionaire Gina Rinehart, who objected to Hera’s claim that she was pushing for Australians to work for $2 a day (in the 2012 quote Hera referenced, Rinehart worried about Australia’s competitiveness when “Africans want to work, and its workers are willing to work for less than $2 per day”). It certainly helps that, at 18, Hera is one of the youngest candidates ever to run for parliament in Australia, but regional media in general have shown a keen interest in VS candidates everywhere. 

Signs also suggest the campaign is resonating. In Footscray, where VS volunteers have already knocked on around 17,000 doors, and the campaign has put up more than 200 yard signs, a steady trickle of people have turned up to volunteer at the campaign office after receiving VS material.

There’s no escaping the fact that politics in Victoria has shifted decisively to the right, and it’s likely either a Liberal or a Liberal-One Nation Coalition government will be elected on 28 November. But there’s no shortage of people who are horrified by the rise of One Nation and who are relieved to find, when visited by a VS volunteer, that there’s a party offering a genuinely anti-establishment alternative on the left. 

Hassan tells the story of Mary, an 82-year-old he met while doorknocking in the outer northern suburb of Thomastown. A long-time Labor voter, Mary told Omar that she wouldn’t vote for the ALP this time because “they’ve completely lost their way”. He later recounted:

“Unsure where things might go, I raised Pauline Hanson and her racist attempt to blame migrants for all our problems. She shook her head. ‘It’s very sad, very wrong’, she said, before explaining that she grew up in Reefton, where her father worked building the Upper Yarra Dam alongside thousands of migrants from around the world. She described playing with all the Italian and Yugoslav kids, going to each other’s houses and having great fun. ‘It made life richer, having all the different cultures, growing up together’.

author: Pip Hinman
title: We need to stand up against genocide
content:
Cathy Eatock gave the following speech to the International Day of Peace rally on September 20 on Gadigal Country, organised by Sydney Anti-AUKUS Coalition and Stop the War on Palestine.

AUKUS ties us irrevocably to the United States war machine.

Australia has previously blindly followed the US into the war on terror which led to the deaths of an estimated 4.7 million people in Iraq, Syria and Libya.

Now the Anthony Albanese government has, astoundingly, followed Scott Morrison into AUKUS, without question or public discussion. The obscene cost of $368 billion over 30 years means hospitals, aged care homes, housing, education, the National Disability Support Scheme, dental and mental health services, and Aboriginal communities won’t receive the funding we need.

With each submarine having its own nuclear reactor, its radioactive waste will need to be stored here.

But Aboriginal people have repeatedly rejected even low-grade medical uranium waste being stored on their lands. The Aboriginal communities of Maralinga, Emu plain and Montebello Islands have already borne the brunt of nuclear testing.

Pacific peoples in the Marshall Islands, Christmas Island, French Polynesia and Kiribati have endured 315 nuclear weapons tests. It is the Pacific and Aboriginal communities that continues to suffer that legacy.

As well as the initial deaths, blindness, radiation sickness, there are continuing high rates of cancers, miscarriages and birth defects. These tests have made the lands uninhabitable, and they continue to poison the food and water sources these communities rely on.

The government has recognised the obvious danger of nuclear-powered submarines, requiring Perth’s hospitals to stock iodine tablets in case of an emergency.

AUKUS is a clear breach of the Treaty of Rarotonga, which establishes the South Pacific as a Nuclear Free Zone, and which Australia helped develop under a previous Labor government.

The chance of the US going to war with China is only increasing. Roughly 60% of the US public believes a major military conflict with China is “possible”; 26% view it as “likely”; and 11% consider it “inevitable”.

Tying Australia to the US industrial-military complex directly threatens Australia. Does anybody really think we will have sovereignty of where those submarines go and what they do? It’s insanity!

The Albanese government has continued to place the US and Israel’s interests ahead of its own citizens. Australia has been shamed by its lack of action against the horrific genocide and decimation of Gaza, and the violent illegal settlements in the West Bank.

The failure to respond has meant that bombings and the blocking of medical aid, food, water and building materials continue. This lack of response has only fed Israeli and US impunity and led to the invasion of Lebanon and war on Iran.

Australia has welcomed the president of the genocidal Israeli state that, according to Francesca Albanese, has slaughtered more than 680,000 people in Gaza.

The Israeli Occupation Force has left newborn babies to die in their hospital cribs; it has targeted the shooting of babes in arms and children in the head and groin.

We’ve seen 335 shots fired into the car where a five-year-old was waiting for help, only for the targeted murder of paramedics seeking to save her.

Australia has failed to act when the Australian aid worker, Zomi Frankcom, was murdered, along with six other aid workers from World Central Kitchen, which had previous approval for its travel route.

We’ve then seen Israeli Defense Forces soldiers who have participated in this genocide be welcomed to Australia for a running race.

The murders continue, condoned by a lack of action to stop the genocide.

Yet, it was Gareth Evans, a former Labor MP, who developed the UN’s Responsibility to Protect. Adopted by the United Nations in 2005, it obliges states to intervene and prevent mass atrocities, including genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity.

Australia has a responsibility to respond to such atrocities and work with other middle powers to intervene and ensure states abide by international law.

Yet Australia has failed to join 11 other nations to sanction Israel’s illegal settlements, even though that is mostly a symbolic gesture.

Australians do not condone this slaughter of children and unarmed people. The Australian government must meets its international obligations and not drag us into a major regional war.

author: AWSM
title: Why I Won’t Vote ~ A SYMPOSIUM #1
content:
Anarchy 37, March 1964, Why I Won’t Vote

Voting : “The instrument and symbol of a freeman’s power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country”

The saying that ” only a fool would put a loaded gun into the hands of an idiot ” is an especially apt analogy of government. An idiot (usually well-meaning) considers himself clever enough to run the affairs of a large number of people by taking a seat in parliament. A large number of people, acting like fools, vote for his party’s policy then spend the next few years grumbling about the results. The error in approach is that the voter thinks that he will get what he voted for. If he could vote for those who in fact control the country, say the Governors of the Bank of England, the directors of the industrial corporations and those behind the ministries, the illusion of democracy would be more understandable.

The real centres of power lie far beyond the people’s influence at elections. These remain constant whatever Party is ” in power “. In the terms of centralised ” democracy ” the only possible argument to justify voting is that marginal benefits may be gained. The state only incidentally attends to the well-being of its subjects. Its main concern is its power relation to other states, of which the most perfect expression is in war.

I am on the side of people anywhere who are prepared neither to live nor die for something that in the long run can only militate against survival and the conditions that make life worth living. Our immediate action must, by its nature, be to oppose that pathetic gesture, voting. It must be direct and direction. We can learn to live as free men and women only by organising against the condition we are in.

The Tenants Association, Consumers Association, and Direct Action in industry all provide opportunities for people to experience directing their own lives in positive ways towards positive ends.

Only by direct involvement in society can the individual hope to transform himself and his world. Freedom cannot be given, it must be taken; and the free society can only grow from experiments in the problems (ethical and organisational) of community.

Voting does not, and cannot, mean government by consent. By voting, one acts on the assumptions that certain men are fit to govern, and that a majority is necessarily right. Also should the state, acting in the name of a (frequently fictitious) majority, declare war, the individual loses the right to live, if he ever had it.

To me, voting is complicity with the State and a negative action, therefore I do not vote.

author: Tom Bramble
title: What’s the deal with productivity?
content:
The bosses are trying to convince workers that lower corporate taxes, fewer regulations and workers’ rights, and less union power would be good for real wages. What they really want is more profits at the expense of the working class.

For years, business lobby groups have decried what they call Australia’s “productivity crisis”. They don’t say workers are producing less than they used to; they say they aren’t increasing production as quickly as before and aren’t keeping pace with overseas productivity growth.

It’s true: growth in workers’ hourly output has slowed over the past decade, and Australian workers don’t produce as much value for the bosses as American workers. But the bosses argue that this means living standards are held back, and prices rise more than they otherwise would, contributing to the cost-of-living crisis.

They say that government regulations (rules about wages, hours of work, health and safety standards, construction standards, environmental protections and professional and occupational registration requirements) and trade unions are preventing business investment. Their solution is “deregulation”, “slashing red tape”, “more competition”. These are simply code words for attacking the working class.

Let’s break this down. First, what is productivity? The simplest definition is “output per hour”. For BlueScope Steel, it could be tonnes of steel produced per hour per worker. For a childcare centre operator, it could be the number of children in care per worker per day. Lift those and productivity rises.

But who benefits? Does the steel worker or childcare worker see their wage rise automatically if they get more done? Of course not. In the first instance, all the money made from extra production by every group of workers goes to the capitalists, not the workers. Workers’ standard of living depends on how much they fight for. And that applies across the whole economy.

The bosses say some of the additional money coming in from workers’ extra effort will come back through higher wages and maybe more jobs. They argue: “a rising tide lifts all boats”. Is that true, though?

First, productivity in Australia may have slowed in the past couple of decades, but it has still risen. Yet household living standards are no higher than they were in 2012. There is no indication that workers are seeing any of the higher value they produce in the form of higher real wages.

A starker example is the United States, which bosses always point to as the high-productivity benchmark, where output per worker is higher and rising faster. In that country, workers’ share of national income is now at its lowest since World War Two—the productivity gains have gone to the capitalists, who have grown ever wealthier at workers’ expense.

Take things down another level. Even if bosses shared a cut of the higher revenue from increased productivity with workers, or unions successfully struck to extract a higher wage, bosses would still be ripping off workers.

All wealth ultimately comes either from the world’s natural resources or from human labour. You only have to see what happens when workers go on strike to see the truth of this—nothing gets produced, not a wheel turns, the childcare centres lie empty. All the machinery, all the factories, all the railway lines can only be put to good use if workers labour on them. And these in turn are the product of previous generations of workers’ labour.

What the capitalists call productivity should really be called exploitation: the extraction of value from the worker over and above the cost of their reproduction, i.e. what is necessary to get them to come to work each day in the form of wages. They call it profit; in fact, it’s theft from the worker.

This theft lies at the heart of capitalism. It explains why the workers labour their whole lives and have not much more than their home to hand on to their kids, and often not even that. While their employer has significantly expanded their operations at the workers’ expense. Some of the bosses may blow the money on a more self-indulgent lifestyle, but personal greed doesn’t get to the heart of it.

Every boss is driven to extract more from their workers, i.e. to lift productivity, because if they don’t, their rivals will, and they will be undercut and go out of business. The winner is the boss who can exploit their workers the most. That’s why every boss in every country demands that governments make it easier for them to rip off their …

author: AWSM
title: Errico Malatesta – Vote? What For?
content:
George: This beer’s not too bad, is it?

Jack: Yes, it’s alright, but what a price!

George: Shocking – especially when you remember what things used to cost. Still, you can’t wonder with all these taxes. It costs you twice as much to live as it used to. They put up the price of some things, and say you can do without them. But you can’t do without bread, and food, and clothes – you have to pay the rent all the same, and then there are the taxes on this and the rates – on our wages too! What a life! And it’s our own fault! If we wanted to we could alter things. The working class has the remedy in its own hands.

George: Easy enough! You’ve got a vote?

Jack: What’s that got to do with it?

George: Have you, or haven’t you?

Jack: Well, I’m entitled to a vote – but I never make use of it.

George: There you are! You’ve got a vote, but you just won’t take the trouble to use it, and then you wonder why things are so bad. You deserve all you get, honestly! People like you are responsible for all the trouble in the world!

Jack: Alright, alright, keep your hair on! Just tell me what’s the good of voting?

George: It’s obvious. Who makes the laws? The M.P.’s. Elect good M.P.’s and you get good laws.

Jack: Good councillors and good M.P.’s? We’ve heard that for a long time. But you’d have to be deaf, dumb, and blind not to notice it’s the same stooges that always get in. Oh, it’s wonderful to hear them when they’re after votes at election time. They pat you on the back, ask after the wife and kids, kiss the baby, promise you railways, bridges, work, cheap bread, less taxes, higher wages, protection – absolutely everything! And once they get in, they’re no better than anyone else. Goodbye promises! The wife and kids may starve, there’s no more or less work than before, the whole town can be falling to pieces for all they care. They’ve other things to think about than your troubles! Then a few years later they start the ballyhoo again. It doesn’t matter what colour the party is: they’re all the same. As soon as they’re elected, they forget all about you. They’re in their clubs and at their select dinners, and they don’t even trouble to come and have a look at you until the next election.

George: That’s correct! But why elect the rich? Don’t you know that the rich only live on the work of the masses? So how do you expect them to worry about the masses? All they think of is getting as much out of the ordinary man as they can.

Jack: Now you’re talking! But it’s not only the rich. There’s the other type, who want to get elected so they can become rich.

George: That’s true. So don’t let’s vote for them. Let’s elect workers, experienced friends of ours, as you might say, and then we won’t be fooled.

Jack: Oh, we’ve got some of your “experienced friends” in now, and they’re no different from our acknowledged enemies! Anyhow, what do you mean, “let’s elect – let’s elect.” As if we – you and me – could do as we like!

George: But it’s not only us two. If each one of us tried to convert other people and they would do the same, labour would have a majority, and we could elect whoever we liked. And that’s when we could form a government of the workers, and then . . .

Jack: And then it would be a paradise – I mean for those who were in Parliament! You’re arranging things a bit too quickly! Those in command always have the majority. The rich are always in power. Just imagine a poor worker, perhaps with an ill wife and four hungry kids, and you tell him to risk his job and get thrown out of his house to starve; just to give his vote to a candidate his master doesn’t like. Just try and convince those poor devils who can be thrown out of work by their boss whenever he likes. They’re never free; if they want to be free, they don’t want to waste their time voting – just take what they need.

George: But if we didn’t do that, no-one would vote. We couldn’t go to the workers and ask them to vote for our party, and say at the same time that votes were useless.

Jack: That’s just it! And on top of that you have to make election promises you know you can’t keep. And then you have to stand in with the Government, and mix with the well-to-do, and all the rest of it. As soon as any of your men are elected they have to kow-tow to the people you admit are the opponents of the workers. So why the hell talk about propaganda when the first thing you do is to counteract propaganda?

George: But you must admit, it’s an advantage to have our own men with …

author: Emma Black
title: Strangulation: How did attempted murder become normal?
content:
A 16-year-old woman from Sydney’s northern beaches died in hospital in late August after reportedly being strangled during consensual sex with her partner. The tragedy has sparked a long-overdue reckoning with the consequences for young women of the pornification of sex and the normalisation of sexual violence that has come with it.

In recent years, sexual strangulation has gone from being a relatively marginal phenomenon to an everyday sexual practice. In Australia, 61 percent of young women report having been strangled during sex, according to a

2024 survey

 of thousands of 18- to 35-year-olds. Men are most likely to be the stranglers. There is no safe way to strangle someone. According to David Corlett and Marie Crabbe, founders of anti-strangulation advocacy group Breathless:

“Potential 

consequences

 [of strangulation]

range from

 neck pain to loss of bladder and bowel control, headaches, memory loss, seizures, brain damage, stroke and, as seems to be the case with the young woman from the northern beaches, death. The risks and consequences are cumulative, so the more someone is strangled, the more likely they are to suffer harm.”

Only a tiny percentage of middle-aged and older adults have engaged in sexual strangulation, but among young people it’s become commonplace. Maree Crabbe, who is also the director of

It’s Time We Talked

, says strangulation wasn’t an issue before about 2019. But things have changed dramatically since then. “In recent years, we’ve been hearing it’s become normal for young people of all backgrounds, socioeconomic groups, cultures, sexual orientations”, she recently told the

Sydney Morning Herald

.

So how did a potentially deadly act become a normal sexual practice?

The main driver is pornography.

Recent research

 found more than 60 percent of 18- to 35-year-olds had encountered sexual strangulation depicted in pornography. One study comparing the content in the most popular pornography across the two and a half decades to 2024 found that sexual strangulation has gone from almost non-existent to featuring in 15 percent of scenes.

Pornography has become the de facto sex education system for millions of young people. And strangulation is just the latest trend in an industry that maximises profits by selling more extreme depictions of violent and degrading treatment of women.

A landmark 2010 study of best-selling pornographic videos, published in the journal

Violence Against Women

, found that 88 percent contained physical aggression, while 49 percent of scenes contained verbal aggression. Perpetrators were usually male, whereas targets were overwhelmingly female. Targets most often showed pleasure or responded neutrally to the aggression.

So the vast majority of mainstream pornography, whether it depicts strangulation or not, reinforces the idea that violence and humiliation are not only permissible, but pleasurable for women. The pornography industry has “blood on its hands” for propagating this sort of violent content, according to Chanel Contos, founder of

Teach Us Consent

.

An example of how normalised strangulation during sex has become came from this year’s Eurovision song contest.

Romania’s 2026 song entry

 “Choke Me” repeats the words “choke me” 30 times in three minutes. The song also contains the lyrics “It’s hard to breathe in” and “make my lungs explode”.

Many mainstream commentators

emphasise

 the importance of avoiding “kink-shaming” when addressing the issue of sexual strangulation with young people. This dresses up the prioritisation of men’s sexual gratification over women’s safety as sex-positive open-mindedness. And it wilfully ignores the fact that sexual desires and practices are not simply a matter of individual preference; they are shaped and constructed in a society where women are not equal to men, and enormous profit can be made from sex by companies competing for market share.

The reality is that people’s sexual inclinations have not radically changed on their own over the last 50 years, such that the majority of men now enjoy inflicting harm on women. Market forces have pushed things in this direction. In an attempt to be more sensational and attract market share, pornography companies have taken the male-dominant trope that underpins the construction of mainstream heterosexuality and pumped it up to a new extreme. This has shaped attitudes to sex and sexual desire, which in turn further reinforces the business model. And …

author: Susan Price
title: ‘Ecological crisis creates a challenge and an opportunity for the left’
content:
Ayesha Ahmad, a Pakistani socialist-feminist activist, researcher, educator, and labour rights practitioner with the Haqooq-e-Khalq Party, was one of the guest speakers at the Ecosocialism 2026 conference in Magan-djin/Brisbane, September 11–13. She spoke to Green Left’s Peter Boyle about the impact of the mounting global ecological crisis on politics in Pakistan.

The catastrophic flash floods in Nepal as a result of global warming and the melting of the Himalayan glaciers were a warning to the world, but does it have a special significance for Pakistan, which also borders the Himalayas?

The catastrophic flash floods in Nepal are a profound warning for Pakistan. For years, Pakistan has been among the countries most exposed to the climate crisis in South Asia, and we have already witnessed what a warming Himalaya can do — from the catastrophic 2022 floods, to increasingly frequent glacial lake outburst floods in Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Nepal disaster tells us that we may be entering an even more dangerous phase of the Himalayan climate crisis.

But for me, there is a much deeper question here. South Asia shares a history. We share the history of colonial extraction, of loot and plunder, of resources being taken from our lands to build wealth elsewhere. Political decolonisation did not necessarily mean economic decolonisation. The geography of extraction has changed, the language has changed, but the underlying relationship can remain remarkably familiar.

Today, we are being told that the answer is development, investment, critical minerals, energy security and even the green transition. But we have to ask: whose development, whose energy security and whose transition?

Climate change cannot be reduced to mining alone. But it would be deeply irresponsible to pursue accelerated extraction in an already climate-vulnerable Himalayan region without asking what extraction does to fragile ecosystems, watersheds, communities and the cumulative resilience of the region.

And this is where the history of colonialism matters. We cannot keep repeating the old colonial bargain under a new vocabulary: our mountains provide the minerals, our communities bear the ecological and social costs and the value is extracted into global markets elsewhere.

If the Global North needs minerals for its energy transition, then the question must be: Who owns them? Who decides? Who benefits? Who bears the environmental costs? And what happens to the people and ecosystems from which these resources are extracted?

We cannot continue with an economic model that treats our mountains, minerals, rivers and land as commodities.

We cannot call it a green transition if the transition is built on another round of extraction from the Global South. We cannot decolonise our politics while continuing to colonise our resources. And we cannot keep asking the people of Pakistan to pay the climate price for a development model from which they receive so little of the wealth.

For Pakistan, the lesson from Nepal is therefore not simply to prepare better for floods.

If extraction continues without ecological limits, democratic control and justice — and if the old unequal relationship between the Global North and resource-rich countries of the Global South continues under the language of “green development” — then the next disaster will not be a surprise. It will be a consequence of choices we already made.

Many years ago, we took part in an international campaign for the release of Baba Jan from Gilgit-Baltistan, who was dubbed the “first climate justice political prisoner”. How does the mounting ecological crisis impact repression and human rights?

The struggle is not only about environmental protection, but about who has the right to speak, whose land is protected, whose losses are recognised, and whether climate-affected communities are allowed to demand justice.

For me, the story of Baba Jan is one of the clearest examples of what climate politics looks like in Pakistan when it becomes a question of justice, rather than simply a question of climate change. And this tells us something very important about the space available to the left in Pakistan.

We are allowed to talk about climate change. We are allowed to talk about floods, melting glaciers, carbon emissions and resilience. But when we start talking about climate justice — about land, ownership, displacement, workers’ rights, resource extraction, reparations and who is …

author: Lucy Chapman-Kelly
title: ‘Rig your own stages!’: Melbourne theatre workers strike
content:
Fans of Macy Gray were met by hundreds of Arts Centre Melbourne staff on strike for the first time in the institution’s history on 11 September. More than 95 percent of union members

 voted

 in favour of the 24-hour strike, rejecting management’s 3 percent offer and instead demanding an above-inflation pay rise, back pay from last October, and increased government funding for the arts.

According to the

unions

 covering the workers—the Media, Entertainment and Arts Alliance and the Communications and Public Sector Union—Arts Centre staff wages have gone backwards in real terms by 10 percent since 2022, and almost 40 percent of the workforce is paid at the minimum award rate. Management’s 3 percent pay rise offer amounts to a further cut in real wages.

Nearly half the workforce is casual, and contact between workers is limited. Workers serving drinks at the bar, for example, might never interact with the ushers who seat people. The high turnover characteristic of casual work also means people don’t work with the same people consistently. This creates barriers to organising the workforce, and highlights why the strike, and the broader campaign for a better agreement, is a significant achievement.

For many of the workers, it was their first experience of an industrial campaign. Many brought handmade signs and gave impromptu speeches, with several pointing out that without the work of hundreds of workers like them, shows would not happen. One stage management worker started a chorus: “Pay us better wages, or rig your own damn stages!”

Arts Centre managers say they can’t afford to increase wages because of the lack of government funding for the arts. Public funding is a real issue, with Victoria’s state funding cut by more than $20 million since 2022. Yet the Arts Centre CEO, Karen Quinlan, earns around $450,000 per year,

according to their most recent Annual Report

.

Much of the Arts Centre’s funding comes from private donors, including

shopping centre owner John Gandel

, who is worth nearly $5 billion, and the parents of

Visy owner Anthony Pratt

, whose net worth is more than double Gandel’s.

Socialists want a world in which

artists are not censored based on the interests of corporate donors

, and artistic institutions that enrich the lives of the majority, like public museums, galleries and theatres, are properly funded and those who work in and contribute to them are able to live a decent life.

Lucy Chapman is a union member working at the Arts Centre.

title: Eğitim Sen’den Gebze’de çağrı: Okullarda şiddete karşı somut adımlar atılsın
content:
Kocaeli – Eğitim Sen Kocaeli 2 No’lu Şube, Manisa’nın Turgutlu ilçesinde öğrencilerin hedef alındığı silahlı saldırının ardından Gebze Kent Meydanı’nda basın açıklaması yaptı. Gebze Sendikalar Birliği ile Gebze Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri’nin destek verdiği açıklamayı şube yöneticisi Hatice Oral okudu.

İnci Üzmez Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi önündeki saldırıda 11 öğrencinin yaralandığını belirten Oral, “Okullarda her geçen gün tırmanan şiddet olayları ve öğrencilerin yaşam hakkını tehdit eden saldırılar, artık münferit vakalarla geçiştirilebilecek basit bir asayiş sorunu olarak görülemez” dedi.

Millî Eğitim Bakanlığı’na (MEB) seslenen Oral, Bakanlığın öğrencilerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin güvenliği yerine önlük ve giyim kuşam gibi konularla meşgul olduğunu söyledi. Oral, “Okullarda öğrenciler saldırıların hedefi olurken, eğitim emekçileri her gün şiddet riskiyle yüz yüze çalışırken, Bakanlığın eğitimin asıl ve hayati sorunu olan ‘güvenli okul güvenli gelecek’ talebini görmezden gelmesi kabul edilemez” ifadelerini kullandı.

Okulların yalnızca güvenlikçi yöntemlerle güvenli hâle getirilemeyeceğini vurgulayan Oral, “Kalıcı çözüm, okulları sadece güvenlikçi bir anlayışa teslim etmekte değil; Psikolojik Danışmanlık ve Rehberlik (PDR) hizmetleri ile Sosyal Hizmet uzmanlarını eğitim sürecinin tam merkezine koymakta yatmaktadır” dedi.

Açıklamada, psikolojik danışman, rehber öğretmen ve sosyal hizmet uzmanlarının okulların ihtiyaçlarına göre görevlendirilmesi, kalabalık sınıfların azaltılması ve müfredatın akran zorbalığıyla mücadele, kültür, sanat ve sporla desteklenmesi istendi. Eğitim Sen, yeni saldırıların önüne geçmek için öğrencilerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin can güvenliğini sağlayacak önlemlerin gecikmeden alınması çağrısında bulundu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Pro-Palestine Activist ‘Close to Death’ on Hunger Strike in Tunisian Prison
content:
The leader of the Global Sumud Flotilla is in a semi-comatose condition and close to death as he enters the 39th day of his hunger strike inside Tunisia’s Mornaguia Prison, the organisation has confirmed to Novara Media.


Wael Naouar, a father of two who was detained in March alongside three other Flotilla organisers, Ghassan Henchiri, Ghassan Boughdiri and Nabil Chennoufi, initiated his hunger strike in protest of the prolonged detention the Sumud 4 have endured without trial. 


In a press release shared on Tuesday, the Global Sumud Flotilla said Naouar is facing organ failure, and experiencing hallucinations and severe heart, chest and stomach pain. He is described as barely able to see or hear, and “wishes to lose consciousness only to escape the agony”.


After a visit to his son this week, Naouar’s father said: “Wael is on the brink of death.”


Henchiri, Boughdiri and Chennoufi also began their hunger strikes a little over two weeks ago. The Flotilla described Henchiri as “bedridden, in severe pain and denied basic medical care”.


The activists were initially arrested over allegations of financial violations in March. This triggered an investigation into each of the men, and they have remained imprisoned by Tunisian authorities while they await trial. 


A trial date has yet to be set, and their pre-trial detention was

extended by four months

on 11 September. 


Hundreds of protestors took to the streets in Tunis this weekend demanding freedom for the Sumud 4. 

Around

15 people were reportedly arrested

 after the march, a move condemned by two Tunisian political parties and the Tunisian League for Human Rights which called for the immediate release of those detained. 


The Global Sumud Flotilla slammed the Tunisian government for holding the Sumud 4 on “fabricated financial charges designed to criminalise their solidarity” with “no credible evidence” and said it holds state authorities fully responsible for their fate. 


It is calling for the activists’ immediate release, all charges against them to be dropped, emergency hospital care for the hunger strikers, and the release of “every activist detained for standing with them”. 


During their six months incarcerated, the Sumud 4 have endured brutal prison conditions including extreme heat, water shortages and a denial of healthcare, according to the Flotilla.

author: cnt.es
title: Solidaridad con “los 15 de Minnesota”
content:
El Comité Antirrepresivo «15 de Minnesota» busca el apoyo de la clase trabajadora de todo el mundo. Se trata de un grupo de activistas de Minneapolis y St. Paul, en Minnesota (EE. UU.), que se enfrentan a cargos federales por su participación en protestas en contra de ICE, la policía migratoria de Estados Unidos, durante la operación Metro Surge, de este cuerpo represivo. Varias de las personas acusadas pertenecen al movimiento anarquista, mientras que ocho de ellas son militantes sindicales de base y muchas desempeñaron un papel fundamental en la organización de la huelga general de Minnesota del 23 de enero. Uno de los acusados es miembro desde hace mucho tiempo de Industrial Workers of the World (IWW).


Queremos crear una red internacional de contactos para coordinar las iniciativas de solidaridad. La red que pretendemos crear es un frente unido que incluya a sindicatos, organizaciones defensoras de migrantes y solicitantes de asilo, redes de apoyo mutuo, grupos religiosos, estudiantiles y comunitarios, etc.


A través de nuestra red, estamos creando comités de solidaridad en diversas ciudades de Norteamérica y de todo el mundo. Estos comités están integrados por personas de la clase trabajadora de diversos ámbitos de la sociedad y por organizaciones que ayuden en conjunto a defender a «los 15 de Minnesota», además de coordinarse contra la represión estatal en general.


Nuestro comité desarrollará su actividad de apoyo en cuatro ámbitos.


Declaraciones de solidaridad por parte de organizaciones, entre las que se incluyen sindicatos, iniciativas sindicales, colectivos políticos, organizaciones comunitarias, etc.


Recaudación de fondos, incluyendo donaciones directas de asociaciones e individualidades, iniciativas para compartir nuestro enlace en redes sociales y la organización de eventos para recaudar fondos. Se pueden hacer aportaciones en:

https://chuffed.org/project/186570-minnesota-15-legal-defense-fund


Ayudar a difundir la voz de las personas encausadas y de quienes integran el comité, mediante contactos con periodistas, creadores y creadoras de contenido (en podcast o en vídeo), además de organizar eventos y charlas.


Acciones a nivel local, acordes a los objetivos que se persiguen y en la medida de las posibilidades.


Si quieres participar, ponte en contacto con:

Sоlidarity@minnesоta15.оrg.


Puedes obtener más información sobre el caso en nuestra página web,

Minnesota15.org

.


Gracias y ¡viva la solidaridad internacional!


El Comité Antirrepresivo de “los 15 de Minnesota”


La entrada

Solidaridad con “los 15 de Minnesota”

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

title: Akın Gürlek’i bekleyenler var
content:
AKP kadroları bir süredir iktidar yorgunluğu yaşıyor. Toplumsal rıza üretememeleri durumuna anayasa ve yasalar çerçevesinde toplumu yönetememek de eklendi. Devletin merkez ve yerel organlarıyla beraber, kamuda ve özelde hukuksal, kurumsal normlar büyük ölçüde erozyona uğradı, hatta yer yer kalmadı bile. Şirketler dar gelirlilerin tabiri caizse üç kuruşluk yatırımlarına devlet-hükümet yetkililerinin gözü önünde el koyup, yurt dışına kaçırıyor. Patronlar işçilerin kazanılmış ücretlerini, kıdem tazminatlarını bakanlara söz verdikleri halde ödememekte ısrar ediyorlar. Bir süredir Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı ile Adalet Bakanlığı önünde haklarını arayan işçi ve sendika yöneticileriyle, mahkemelerden sonuç alamayan depremzedelerin nöbet eylemleri yaygınlaştı. Çeyrek asırlık iktidarları boyunca depremin felakete dönüşmesini engellemek için gerekenleri yapmayanlar can kayıplarının karşısında mahkemelerin işlevsizliği konusunda sessiz. Bu hafta, son olarak Adalet Bakanlığı önündeki nöbet eylemi nedeniyle dünya ölçeğinde bile “felaket” olarak adlandırılan Şubat 2023 depremlerinden sonra bile unutulan acılar ve yapılmayanların bir nebze olsun anımsanabilmesi için yazmayı tercih ettim.


Litosfer-taşküre


Günümüzden 4,55 milyar yıl önce oluştuğu ve 4,1 milyar yıl önce de üzerinde yaşamın başladığı tahmin edilen dünya, bizlerin de diğer canlıların da ortak “evi”. Yaşayabilmek için kendisine “mecbur olduğumuz” dünyanın en dış katmanı taşküre (litosfer) olarak adlandırılıyor. Jeoloji ve jeofizik bilim dallarının araştırmalarına göre okyanuslar ve kıtaların yer aldığı taşküre, 70-100 km kalınlığında ve milyonlarca yıldır hareket halinde olan levhalardan oluşuyor. Bu levhalar zaman zaman kırılıp parçalar birbirinden uzaklaşıyor ya da üst üste biniyor. Başka bir ifadeyle, taşküre milyonlarca yıldır “yerleşmeye” çalışıyor. Söz konusu bu “yerleşme”ler gerçekleşirken de sarsıntılar/titreşimler-depremler ortaya çıkıyor. Konunun uzmanlarının çok daha ayrıntılı olarak anlatacakları bilgiler ışığında; biz insanların yalnızca “ne zaman” olacağını bilemediği bu “yerleşme”lerin neden olduğu sarsıntılara/titreşimlere-depremlere karşı gerekli hazırlıkları yapmadığımız yerlerde, olayın gerçekleştiği taşkürenin üzerindeki hemen her şeyi beraberinde kırıp, yıktığını yaşayarak da olsa biliyoruz.


Japonya’da da deprem oluyor ama…


Ancak, bu sarsıntıları/titreşimleri dikkate alıp, gerekli önlemler hayata geçirilerek hazırlıklı olduğumuz bölgelerde bu levhaların üzerinde yaşayabilmemiz pekâlâ mümkün. Onu da biliyoruz, gözlemliyoruz. Türkiye’de yaygın olarak bilinen bir ülke örneği olarak Japonya’da olduğu gibi. 11 Mart 2011 tarihinde gerçekleşen

Tōhoku bölgesindeki “yerleşme” sırasında ortaya çıkan 9,1 büyüklüğündeki

sarsıntı/titreşim-deprem sonrasında 15 bin 700 kişinin hayatını kaybettiği, 4 bin 600 kişinin kaybolduğu ve 5 bin 300 kişinin de yaralandığı kamuoyu ile paylaşılmıştı. 91 ay sonra, 17 Ekim 2018’de gerçekleşen Osaka’daki “yerleşme”de

ortaya çıkan

depremin büyüklüğünün 6,1 olduğu, yalnızca dört kişinin hayatını kaybettiği ve 400 kişinin de yaralandığı rapor edilmişti. Yine Japonya’da son olarak, 16 Mart 2022’de Fukuşima’da gerçekleşen “yerleşme”de ortaya çıkan 7,3 büyüklüğündeki depremin üç kişinin hayatını kaybetmesine, 198 kişinin de yaralanmasına neden olduğu açıklanmıştı.


Öyle ki Japonya’da “dünya yerleşirken” ortaya çıkan deprem sırasında insanlara ölmemeleri-yaralanmamaları için “en güvenli yer olarak” binaları terk etmemeleri, eğer dışardalarsa da binalara girmeleri tavsiye ediliyor. Oysa Türkiye’de hâlâ insanların ölmemesi için deprem sonrasında binaların bir an önce terk edilmesi ve artçı depremler bitene kadar da binalara girilmemesi öneriliyor. Tabii ki binalardan çıkabilecek gerekli zamanı, olanağı bulabilirlerse. Unutmadan ekleyelim, 12 Nisan 2007’de Endonezya’da gerçekleşen Sumatra’daki “yerleşme”de 8,4 büyüklüğünde deprem meydana geldiği, 20 bin binanın hasar görmesine karşın, 25 kişinin hayatını kaybettiği, 161 kişinin de yaralandığı bildirilmişti.


Türkiye’de “Şubat 2023 depremleri”-felaketler


Türkiye, dünyanın “yerleşme”sinin en sıklıkla gerçekleşmekte olduğu jeolojik bir bölgede yer alıyor. Bu nedenle, geçmişte olduğu gibi, gelecekte de taşküreyi oluşturan bu levhalardaki kırılmaları ve bunun neden olduğu depremleri sıklıkla yaşayacağız. Deprem Bölgeleri Haritası’na göre, Türkiye’nin yüzde 92’sinin bu “yerleşme” bölgeleri içerisinde olduğu, nüfusunun da yüzde 95’inin “yerleşme” bölgeleri üzerinde ya da …

author: winter oak
title: Anti-Fascist Always
content:
This is the fourth in a selection of chapters from the book 

King of the Squatters

 by jaybo which we are delighted to be able to share on Winter Oak. The whole text can be found as a pdf

here

.


Here we are again in 2015.


Fascism was defined by the Italian dictator, Mussolini, as the merging of governments and corporations. When prime ministers like Tony Blair and politicians started also working in top positions at big companies, creeping fascism began.


In the height of a glorious summer, we started receiving fascist threats, directly against the entire camp, but also, astonishingly, a national extreme right-wing organization began threatening the entire city of Liverpool. Liverpool has always traditionally been left wing and anti-fascist. For example, Ken Loach had chosen a scouse girl to read her grandfather’s letters from Spain, written whilst he had been fighting fascists in the Spanish Civil War, in his film ‘Land and Freedom’ (

pictured)

. Approximately two thousand brave souls from Liverpool went to Barcelona and beyond to fight with the anarchists and socialists against Franco and the fascists in 1936. Those men and women were called the ‘international brigades’, which George Orwell also joined and wrote about in his book

Homage to Catalonia

.


The threats directed at the camp initially came from a local idiot, not shy about his shallow beliefs or violent threats. He had several German shepherd dogs which he sometimes walked around the camp with, but he began threatening to drive his car over our tents whilst we slept. I doubt I was the only one who lost a lot of sleep at that time. Thankfully, none of his threats ever materialised.


The threats against the entire city were something altogether different. They were still made by idiots, but those idiots were more organised and committed, and they were a group, not an individual. I forget the name of the group, possibly the ‘English Defence League’ (EDL) who had some support at that time. The

Liverpool Echo

 newspaper informed the people of Liverpool that a right-wing group had told them they were coming to the city to burn it down and only bullets would stop them! Many of us could not believe either the balls, or the stupidity, of those people.


At our camp, the atmosphere became electrified. Most of our guys were not activists, far from it. Politics was meaningless bullshit for them, irrelevant to their direct lives. They could sound sexist, racist, homophobic or ageist; they could sound right-wing themselves just regurgitating sound bites from the right-wing mainstream media. But for me, that situation catalysed their real, unadulterated feelings and beliefs. They were spoiling for a fight for sure, and they were right at the front of the queue waiting in Lime Street train station for the representatives of the master race to greet them.


In what must surely be one of the great moments in Liverpool’s history, fifty racist nut cases pulled up in a train to discover that about one thousand five hundred people had brought the city centre and train station to a grinding halt, waiting to say hello, antifa style. Quite fabulously, the police decided that the only solution to prevent carnage was to lock the fascists in the train station’s left-luggage room, for their own safety!


After a few hours of being locked in with the luggage, the fascist leader actually convinced the police to let him out and give a little speech. He was immediately subjected to flying bottles, and Jed managed to punch him. Media were everywhere, and this could have easily resulted in two of our guys going straight back to Walton prison. Thankfully, it did not.


All of the guys from the camp had been so eager to meet the fascists that no-one kept to our agreed plan, that we needed at least six people to stay on site at the LA/UOTH camp. I was concerned that our local fascist might see an opportunity to do us harm, combined with the fact that the national fascist group had found out about our camp and said that they would attack it, so I remained alone at the camp. Marianne checked in on me, as did another wonderful female supporter. I pleased to see all of our guys return home safely. I pretended I had not been scared. They were jubilant.


That day, together with the daily organising of our own lives, voluntarily and co-operatively, was enormously politicising and empowering for all the young homeless girls and guys. Some were just teenagers when their parents had …

author: By Devon Cupery, Hannes Brunner, and Scott Russell, Contributors
title: Canadian Oil Giant Enbridge Builds Unauthorized Pipeline Bypass Following 1.3 Million Gallon Spill
content:
Saxon, WI – The Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR) repeatedly requested Enbridge keep its

Line 5

 pipeline shut down following the largest oil and gas spill in state history on Aug. 25. Enbridge defied the requests. Without receiving the required permits, it built a new pipeline to bypass the rupture and restarted Line 5’s operations.


Enbridge’s actions raise serious questions about the state’s ability to regulate large, multinational corporations and its willingness to enforce its permits.


Bad River Tribal Chair Liz Arbuckle asked DNR officials if the permits meant anything at all: “What are the consequences if they are violated?”


Arbuckle said the DNR representatives gave evasive responses. They told tribal leaders they are continuing to work with Enbridge in the permitting process. The DNR would not answer whether they would issue Enbridge retroactive permits for the bypass work.


DNR Sec. Karen Hyun and Wisconsin Governor Tony Evers have criticized Enbridge’s conduct, but so far they have stopped short of meaningful enforcement action, such as revoking permits or taking legal action. 


Aerial view of Enbridge’s unauthorized pipeline bypass and the Aug. 25 spill location in Saxon, WI. The site is four miles south of Lake Superior. Photo contributed by Devon Cupery.


In a Sept. 9

letter to Enbridge

, Hyun said that Enbridge has a growing list of environmental harms and permit violations, “demonstrating disregard for the environment, human health, and the statutory authority of the department.” Hyun said Enbridge’s Line 5 reroute permit violations have caused “continued frustration and profound unease” for state officials and the people of Wisconsin. 


Sept. 14 aerial image of the Line 5 excavation pit where the pipeline spill occurred in Saxon, WI. Photo contributed by Devon Cupery.


Enbridge contractors remove semi truck at the excavation pit where the spill occurred. Photo contributed by Devon Cupery.


People living near the pipeline have been unsatisfied with the DNR’s construction oversight. Bad River Tribal Member Joe Bates and others have taken it upon themselves to keep an eye on things and make sure that spills and violations are promptly reported. It is worth noting that Bates’

drone footage

 of the spill made international headlines.


Enbridge’s spill site bypass required state permits to cross streams and wetlands. The DNR did not approve the work. Enbridge blocked state officials from accessing the rupture site for weeks, citing safety concerns. When the DNR got access to the site, the bypass was under construction.


The federal government imposed a no-fly zone for 20 days, preventing independent monitors from recording drone footage of the spill site. During this information blackout, the DNR and the community at-large were dependent on Enbridge’s self-reporting about spill impacts. The no-fly zone was lifted on Sept. 14, the day Enbridge restarted the flow of oil through Line 5. 


Line 5 released more than 1.3 million gallons of toxic gas liquids when an Enbridge contractor truck struck the pipeline at an excavation site on Aug. 25. Photo contributed by River Akemann.


Beth Wallace of the National Wildlife Federation criticized Enbridge’s lack of transparency at a recent press briefing. “Enbridge claims to have learned from the 2010 Kalamazoo oil spill, but [their recent actions show] that they have only escalated the ways in which they shut out local communities, and that is making communities less safe.”


Wallace urged Wisconsin officials and residents to take the issue seriously, calling attention to Enbridge’s “alarming escalation of federal preemption.” She referenced a federal case currently playing out in Michigan where “Enbridge is trying to destroy state rights to regulate [projects] of this nature.”


Enbridge has received strong criticism from other state and Tribal leaders.


Enbridge’s Line 3 construction in Minnesota

ruptured several artesian aquifers

. The company withheld information from the state about its first breach for months. Minnesota DNR Commissioner Sarah Strommen

said

 in a media release that “Enbridge’s actions are clear violations of state law and also of public trust.”


On Sept. 9, Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer renewed her call for a Line 5 shutdown in the Straits of Mackinac, calling the pipeline a “ticking time bomb in the heart of the Great Lakes.” Whitmer urged outgoing Enbridge CEO Gregory Ebel to shut it down “within …

author: CNT Santander
title: Comunicado Anti-Galerna Fest
content:
El fin de semana del 25 y 26 de septiembre tendrá lugar en Santander un festival de música de ideología neofascista, organizado por la Asociación Alfonso I. Las bandas anunciadas tienen causas abiertas en diferentes países europeos por la presencia de homofobia, xenofobia, racismo y violencia en sus letras. Un año más se celebrará sin que el Gobierno de Cantabria lo impida, estando avisado con mucho tiempo de antelación, año tras año.


Desde CNT Santander,

reclamamos que se garantice el cumplimiento de la legislación vigente

, especialmente en materia de igualdad, prevención de la discriminación, seguridad y protección de los derechos fundamentales, y que actúen dentro de sus competencias ante cualquier conducta que pudiera vulnerarla.


Desde CNT Santander, mostramos

nuestra total oposición a la realización de este festival

, ya que consideramos que la normalización y la difusión de ideologías que promueven el odio, la discriminación y la exclusión de determinados colectivos son incompatibles con una sociedad democrática y con los principios de igualdad y dignidad que nosotras defendemos como sindicato de clase.


Esta celebración lo único que genera es más oleadas de racismo, odio y violencia en nuestras calles. Por ello,

no podemos permanecer indiferentes

 ante iniciativas que utilicen la música y los espacios como vehículo de propaganda de ideologías totalitarias y de odio.


Como personas que rechazan cualquier tipo de discriminación y violencia sobre cualquier ser humano no podemos quedarnos calladas frente a esta impunidad de actuación que poseen este tipo de grupúsculos y núcleos. No se pueden ni se deben normalizar los discursos que promulgan estas asociaciones y bandas europeas con ideología de extrema derecha.


Desde CNT Santander,

reivindicamos que los espacios de ocio sean lugares de encuentro, libertad y convivencia entre todas las personas

 y no plataformas para la difusión de mensajes que puedan incitar a la discriminación y a la violencia.


Nuestra oposición a la celebración del festival Galerna no supone un rechazo a la libertad de expresión o a la cultura musical, como muchas personas vitorean. Precisamente porque

defendemos una sociedad libre, plural y diversa, consideramos necesario establecer unas líneas rojas frente a la propaganda de odio y frente a cualquier intento de convertir la intolerancia en algo socialmente aceptable

. Hay líneas que no pueden ni deben traspasarse. Cuando se vulneran los derechos humanos de todas las personas hay acciones y opiniones que dejan de ser aceptables, y es algo que como sociedad deberíamos tener muy presente.


Como dijo Buenaventura Durruti:

¡Al fascismo no se le discute, se le destruye!

, y todas

juntas debemos destruirlo, alzando la voz y no permaneciendo impasibles

. Tenemos que gritar bien alto que no permitiremos que campen a sus anchas con sus ideas racistas y fascistas entre nuestros barrios. Cantabria es, y será siempre, antifascista. Queremos paz y libertad en nuestras calles y que cualquier persona pueda habitarlas sin miedo a ocupar los espacios.


Desde CNT Santander, hacemos un llamamiento a la

unidad de clase, a la solidaridad, al apoyo mutuo y a la convivencia

, y animamos a la ciudadanía y a las organizaciones sociales y sindicales a expresar de manera pacífica su oposición a la normalización de la ideología nazi y fascista.


Tomaremos las calles en la manifestación creada por Cantabria Antifascista que se celebrará el 26 de septiembre a las 12:00 horas en la plaza de los «Derechos Humanos», (C/Alta) de Santander.


¡¡No permitiremos ni el odio ni la discriminación!!


¡Solidaridad, fraternidad, salud y libertad!

 se publicó primero en

CNT Santander

.

author: C.J. Polychroniou
title: This Rising Leftist Party Hopes to Turn Back Germany’s Fascist Wave
content:
The leftist Die Linke party won the most votes in Berlin, even as the far right AfD won a state election in the north.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Germany is now facing the same systemic crisis that its leaders once diagnosed in other European countries, such as Greece, Portugal, and Spain, in the early 2010s. Economic woes and anti-immigrant sentiment have given rise to anti-establishment politics, which in turn is reshaping the country’s political landscape. Indeed, after the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party achieved a historic result in the Saxony-Anhalt state in eastern Germany, the fascists have just won another state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and also made significant gains in the election held in the city-state of Berlin. But it was the radical left Die Linke (the Left), the successor to the ruling Socialist Unity Party (SED) of the former German Democratic Republic, that won the most votes in Berlin.

In the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural state in Germany’s former communist east where unemployment stands at nearly 8 percent, well above the national average, the AfD took first place by winning 38.2 percent of the vote on September 20, while the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) came second with 35.5 percent. Chancellor Merz’s center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) got routed as it failed to cross the 5 percent threshold, thus not winning a single seat in the state parliament for the first time anywhere in Germany. Merz described the result as “a disaster” for his party but vowed to stay in office and press ahead with his unpopular reforms to the German economy, which consist of imposing austerity measures and do not touch the rich. The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) also failed to clear the 5 percent threshold, while Die Linke took just 6.5 percent and the Greens took 5.7 percent.

The state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania was another resounding victory for the AfD and represented something of a rebuke of the SPD-Die Linke coalition that has governed in the state capital of Schwerin for the past five years. Indeed, what is most unexpected about the result in this German state election is that, unlike Saxony-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania was not considered an AfD stronghold. Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania has the lowest proportion of immigrants among all of Germany’s 16 federal states.

In the Berlin state election, Die Linke finished first with 25.3 percent of the vote, ahead of the CDU which got 19 percent, while the AfD won 16 percent, up 6.9 points from the last election.

Die Linke more than doubled the vote percentage it received in the previous Berlin state election in 2023, when it won 12.2 percent of the vote. The party cannot form a government alone, but is clearly in a position to lead a coalition government with the Social Democrats and the Greens and could see its mayoral candidate Elif Eralp become the first leftist mayor of Berlin.

Housing was at the center of the Berlin election and is undoubtedly the key factor behind Die Linke’s surge in popularity. Led by the charismatic 45-year-old Eralp — the daughter of Turkish exiles and a human rights advocate who has served in the Berlin House of Representatives since 2021 and is often called “Berlin’s Mamdani” — Die Linke focused its campaign on rent controls and more social housing, including support for implementing Berlin’s 2021 housing referendum, in which nearly 60 percent of voters backed a legal process to expropriate properties from big landlords. In Berlin, major housing and financial corporations own hundreds of thousands of apartments and thus have major influence over rents in the neighborhoods in which they own properties.

Bringing large private housing stocks under public ownership is a truly radical solution to the housing problem facing Berlin. The 2021 referendum is not legally binding but has nonetheless found massive support among the young people of Berlin in particular, who voted overwhelmingly for Die Linke. Yet, it could potentially become law if the parties in control of the Berlin Senate choose to make it so, although such a move would face various judicial challenges. A far less radical measure, a Berlin rent cap law, was declared unlawful by the German Federal Constitutional Court.

title: El fascismo en el Estado español: un genocidio de clase que no se puede maquillar
content:
El príncipe Juan Carlos de Bourbon y el dictador Francisco Franco en Madrid, Reino de España. Fuente: Wikimedia


Un genocidio ideológico y de clase.


El fascismo, o falangismo, en España significó un genocidio ideológico y de clase. Fueron asesinados y torturados hombres, mujeres y niños inocentes. Fue un castigo a quienes defendieron la legalidad vigente, a quienes se atrevieron a soñar con un mundo mejor, a pensar y a cuestionar los privilegios de la oligarquía. No fue un exceso ni un error: fue un proyecto para aplastar al pueblo trabajador y devolverle el poder a quien nunca lo quiso soltar.


Un golpe de Estado traidor y cobarde.


La República sufrió un golpe de Estado, un golpe traidor y cobarde. Se convirtió en guerra civil porque el pueblo resistió. Y ese pueblo trabajador, con las manos y con la dignidad, tuvo que plantar cara a unos golpistas que contaron con la ayuda necesaria del nazismo alemán y del fascismo italiano para vencer esa resistencia. Conviene no olvidarlo: no se ganó aquella guerra con razones; se ganó con aviones extranjeros y con terror.


Quien piensa diferente no es fascista.


Quien piensa diferente y defiende su postura con argumentos, que podemos compartir o no, no es un fascista. El fascismo no utiliza argumentos porque no los tiene. Su argumento es la mentira, la fuerza y la violencia. Llamar fascista a cualquiera que discrepe es un error, pero mucho peor es lo contrario: blanquear lo que fue el fascismo real, el que fusiló, encarceló y torturó.


Ni comparaciones interesadas ni olvido.


Quienes comparan el fascismo español con el comunismo lo hacen por ignorancia o, peor, de forma intencionada, para lanzar bulos y prostituir la historia. Y quien lo compara con los defensores de la independencia, del derecho de autodeterminación de los pueblos o de otro modelo de Estado se equivoca, casi siempre a propósito y otras veces ejerciendo de mamporrero del poder. Defender que un pueblo decida su futuro es un derecho democrático, no una ideología del odio.


Memoria para no repetir.


Mirar hacia atrás no es quedarse anclado en el pasado. Es entender por qué hoy la ultraderecha avanza con la bandera falsa de lo antisistema, cuando nadie es más sistémico que ella. Es entender por qué no podremos construir una sociedad más justa sin superar el régimen del 78, que se edificó sin ajustar cuentas con aquel pasado. Y es entender que la respuesta a los herederos de aquel golpe no está en la moderación ni en las medias tintas, sino en la unidad de la clase trabajadora.


Porque la memoria es también una herramienta de lucha. Quien olvida quién asesinó a nuestros abuelos acaba aceptando que los nietos de los verdugos sigan mandando.


Até a vitoria sempre!


André Abeledo Fernández


La entrada

El fascismo en el Estado español: un genocidio de clase que no se puede maquillar

 se publicó primero en

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

author: dev
title: Le sacrifice du ciel
content:
Le philosophe Mohamed Amer Meziane publie son troisième livre,

Le Sacrifice du ciel. Une autre histoire de la raison

, qui vient rouvrir, reprendre et poursuivre le cycle ouvert par

Des empires sous la terre

 (2021) et

Au bord des mondes

 (2023).


Le thème du « sacrifice du ciel » fait écho à ceux de la sécularisation, de la mort de Dieu et du « désenchantement du monde ». Ces lieux communs, au sein de l'attirail des pensées critiques, ressemblent à des enjeux à la fois familiers et méconnus.


À voir lundi 21 septembre à partir de 20h


Les « statuaires de la pensée », expression du livre renvoyant au panthéon fatigué des « grands auteurs » européens, ne nous ont légué que peu d'outils pour y faire face. Il se pourrait, en plus, que ces thèmes « biens connus » (c'est-à-dire peut-être totalement impensés) aient obscurci la compréhension qu'on a de ces grands auteurs eux-mêmes. C'est la conséquence d'un des points principaux du livre : l'

orientalisme

, sous la forme de la critique historique des textes sacrés, a joué un rôle matriciel pour la production du savoir occidentalisé.


À partir de là, l'enquête donne lieu à une autre histoire de la philosophie : au prisme de l'orientalisme, Spinoza, Kant et Hegel apparaissent sous un autre jour. Leurs façons de penser la religion, ses rapports à la pensée et à la politique, est très loin cependant de s'être cantonnée au seul domaine de la philosophie. Elles participent de mouvements qui les précèdent et leur survivent, et qui constituent le sol sur lequel se sont déployées les sciences humaines et sociales « modernes ». Un ensemble de mythes vivaces s'ancrent dans cette histoire : le christianisme comme seule religion de la sortie de la religion, le protestantisme comme religion du monde moderne, le monothéisme comme origine de la violence, le fanatisme comme caractéristique des « religions de la Loi »…


Le Sacrifice du ciel

 se présente comme une critique des savoirs, une « histoire souterraine » de la connaissance. Celle-ci ne se contente pas d'en exhumer les marges, mais entend ressaisir l'héritage d'un centre occulté en montrant que la raison n'est pas « occidentale ». Se pose alors une question simple, mais trop souvent ignorée (y compris par la critique décoloniale) : comment les « orientaux » ont-ils eux-mêmes pensé l'orientalisme ? La philosophie d'Afghāni et la « métaphysique insurrectionnelle » de l'émir Abdelkader ont été les lieux d'une résistance formulée au nom du savoir et d'une « critique traditionnelle de la tradition », et deviennent ici ceux de l'élaboration d'une « pensée-autre » (comme le disait Abdelkébir Khatibi, en partant de Fanon).


« La tâche de cet anti-impérialisme philosophique a surtout été de montrer la profonde irrationalité de tout ce système militaro-fossile qui, avec un fracas et une morgue confinant à la folie, s'est targué d'être la seule Raison qui soit. »


Pour aller plus loin (ou revenir quelques crans en arrière), nous renvoyons à nos deux précédents entretiens avec Mohamed Amer Meziane

autour de

Des empires sous la terre

Au bord des mondes

.
