title: ‘Philippines not for sale,’  groups tell investors
content:
Tensions flared outside the venue of the investors’ forum at the posh Bonifacio Global City between the activists and the police where 29 activists sustained injuries after they were dispersed by the police. Photo courtesy of Altermidya

The groups rejected the Luzon Economic Corridor, calling it a “massive sellout” of Philippine patrimony.

MANILA – “The Philippines is not for sale!”

Progressive groups led by the Bagong Alvansang Makabayan (Bayan) and International League of Peoples Struggle (ILPS) Philippines on Thursday expressed their strong condemnation as the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) Investment Forum inaugurated on Thursday, September 10 at the Grand Hyatt Hotel at the Bonifacio Global City, Taguig City.

The group said the initiative is a threat to Philippine sovereignty and a vehicle for foreign control over the country’s resources.

In a joint statement, the groups rejected the LEC, calling it a “massive sellout” of Philippine patrimony, and accused the government of allowing foreign interests to shape the country’s infrastructure and economic development agenda.

Sponsored by the U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA), the event brought together about 600 international investors, industry leaders, project developers, and government officials to discuss investment opportunities within the Subic-Clark-Manila-Batangas corridor.

Bayan and ILPS argued that the corridor would not lead to genuine industrialization but instead create profit opportunities for foreign companies and local business interests. The groups questioned the prominent role of the U.S. government in promoting the initiative, noting that the USTDA is sponsoring and organizing the investment forum

According to the USTDA, the LEC is a trilateral initiative involving the Philippines, the United States, and Japan aimed at mobilizing investments in transportation, logistics, energy, digital infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing. The agency said the corridor seeks to strengthen connectivity and economic growth across Luzon

The groups also cited the proposed 232-kilometer Subic-Clark-Manila-Batangas Freight Railway, which they said would primarily serve foreign commercial interests. Corridor documents identify the freight railway as a key transport project linking major economic hubs in Luzon.

Among the projects criticized by the groups was the proposed Pax Silica Economic Security Zone, which they claimed could accelerate critical mineral extraction and affect Indigenous and agricultural communities.

Bayan and ILPS further alleged that the corridor forms part of a broader U.S. strategy in the Indo-Pacific and raised concerns over what they described as the possible dual-use nature of infrastructure projects located near strategic transportation and military facilities.

The groups said several corridor projects could support both commercial and defense-related activities, citing developments in Subic and other strategic locations. Corridor materials show that the LEC connects key economic centers, ports, airports, and transport networks across Subic, Clark, Manila, and Batangas.

Bayan and ILPS urged the public to reject the corridor, arguing that national development should remain under Filipino control and not be driven by foreign governments or investors. The groups also criticized recent government policies that they said were designed to attract more foreign investment and expand critical mineral projects associated with the corridor.

“Do not sell the Philippines to foreigners. The Philippines belongs to Filipinos. If the government is to undertake projects or programs for industrialization, these should be geared toward national industrialization by Filipinos and for Filipinos, not for foreign interests.,” said former Bayan Muna Rep. Teddy Casino, now chairperson of Bayan, during the protest.

For Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP), the LEC is being presented as “economic development” by Ferdinand Marcos administration, but in reality, the group said it is “really a corridor for imperialist profit and war.”

“Filipino land, resources and infrastructure are being prepared to serve foreign corporations, global supply chains and the strategic military interests of the United States,” said KMP Chairperson Danilo ‘Ka Daning’ Ramos in a statement.

Ramos further said that the ports, airports, railways, fuel facilities and telecommunications infrastructure being built under the LEC are not simply economic facilities.

author: Editors
title: 9/11: How the US turned tragedy into barbarity
content:
Twenty-five years ago, the world changed irrevocably. Not because terrorists from the al-Qaeda network attacked the United States, bringing down the World Trade Center’s Twin Towers in New York, hitting the Pentagon in Virginia and killing nearly 3,000 people. It changed because of US imperialism’s response.

The day after 9/11, the editors of

Socialist Alternative

 magazine, one of the precursor publications of

Red Flag

, warned: “The real threat to people around the world is not terrorism, but the racism, militarism, repression and nationalism that has been unleashed in the wake of the terrorist attacks”.

A week later, President George W. Bush, in an address to a joint session of Congress, announced his so-called War on Terror: “Every nation, in every region, now has a decision to make. Either you are with us, or you are with the terrorists”. His administration rode the wave of outrage over al-Qaeda’s assault to open a new era of imperialist aggression that has cost millions of people’s lives. 

First came Afghanistan in October. It didn’t matter that the ruling Taliban

offered to hand over Osama bin Laden

, the alleged mastermind of the terrorist attacks, to a neutral country to face trial. The US was interested only in war. Condoleezza Rice, then Bush’s national security adviser, admitted as much to the

New Yorker

’s Nicholas Lemann several months later. In the wake of the 9/11 attacks, she had asked senior national security staff to think about how to “capitalise on these opportunities”. 

The Bush administration soon began making a public case for invading Iraq—which had no ties to 9/11—declaring the country part of an “axis of evil” with Iran and North Korea. Undersecretary of State John Bolton soon expanded the axis list to include Cuba, Libya and Syria. The bombs started raining down on Baghdad in March 2003.

These invasions would have been followed by more had the resistance in Iraq not bogged down the US military in an intractable counterinsurgency. Nevertheless, Brown University’s

Costs of War research

 estimates the direct death toll from US military operations in the post-9-11 era in Iraq, Afghanistan, Syria, Yemen and Pakistan to be close to 1 million people. It estimates a further 3.6 to 3.8 million “indirect” deaths resulting from the “destruction of economies, healthcare systems, infrastructure and the environment”. 

The US also set up a global kidnapping network, which it termed “extraordinary rendition”, and a series of “black sites” in which prisoners were held without charge and tortured.

The Open Society Foundation estimates

 that 54 governments collaborated in the program. Then there is the notorious

Guantánamo Bay torture camp

, used since 2002 and still holding ageing prisoners from the War on Terror. This all served as notice that the US empire would stop at nothing to maintain its global domination.

A more enduring legacy of this era of “forever wars” has been the construction of vast internal security and surveillance states, which have trampled civil and democratic rights. 

More than 140 governments have adopted “counterterrorism” legislation since 9/11, beginning with the USA PATRIOT Act, which green-lit mass surveillance and delayed-notice search warrants and bolstered spy agency resources. Mega-departments, such as Homeland Security in the US and Home Affairs in Australia, were established as Western states have become more authoritarian.

Indeed, Australia is one of the worst offenders. “No other nation can match the volume of Australia’s counter-terrorism laws”, wrote legal academics Rebecca Ananian-Welsh and Keiran Hardy in

a 2021 piece for the University of Queensland’s

Contact

 magazine

. They describe the scope of the laws as “staggering”, “unprecedented” and “extreme”, noting that they go beyond even “historical wartime powers”.

They include control orders, preventive detention, and compulsory retention of all telecommunication and online data of every resident. The

Surveillance Legislation Amendment (Identify and Disrupt) Act

 of 2021 gave law enforcement agencies the power to take control of a person’s individual online accounts, modify or delete their data and even take over entire networks. That is, they can legally alter a person’s text messages.

Death and destruction abroad and authoritarianism at home: such is the “rules-based order”, the purported demise of which we are supposed to lament. This post-9/11 era normalised authoritarianism …

title: Συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης, Τετάρτη 23/9 στα δικαστήρια
content:
>για την υπόθεση εκκένωσης της κατειλημμένης πρυτανείας ΕΜΠ, 9:00 Δικαστήρια Ευελπίδων.


>για τη Μ., 9:00 Δικαστήρια Θεσσαλονίκης.


>για τους 4 που διώκονται για την υπόθεση εμπρηστικής επίθεσης στο υπουργείο πληροφοριακών συστημάτων, 10:00 Δικαστήρια Ευελπίδων.


ΑΘΗΝΑ – ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΤΗΡΙΞΗΣ ΣΤΗ ΔΙΚΗ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΥΠΟΘΕΣΗ ΕΚΚΕΝΩΣΗΣ ΤΗΣ ΚΑΤΕΙΛΗΜΜΕΝΗΣ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΑΣ ΕΜΠ ΤΟΝ ΝΟΕΜΒΡΗ 2020


Ενόψει της επερχόμενης δικάσιμου της υπόθεσης εκκένωσης της κατειλημμένης Πρυτανείας ΕΜΠ, το Νοέμβρη του 2020, καλούμε στα

δικαστήρια Ευελπίδων, την Τετάρτη 23/9/2026, ώρα 9:00 π.μ, κτίριο 9, αίθουσα 12.

 Η εκκένωση αυτή αποτελεί την πρώτη οργανωμένη κατασταλτική επίθεση εντός πανεπιστημιακού χώρου, μετά την κατάργηση του πανεπιστημιακού ασύλου, με στόχο την σύλληψη φοιτητ(ρι)ών και εργαζομένων.


Λίγα λόγια για το χρονικό της κατάληψης: Στις 12/11/2020 και εν μέσω πανδημίας, πραγματοποιήθηκε κατάληψη της πρυτανείας του ΕΜΠ στην πολυτεχνειούπολη από φοιτητικά και εστιακά σχήματα, στέκια και αλληλέγγυο κόσμο, ως αντανακλαστικό στην απόφαση της τότε διοίκησης για lock out του κάτω Πολυτεχνείου. Η κατάληψη έγινε αφενός λόγω της τότε επετείου της εξέγερσης του ’73 και αφετέρου ως ένδειξη αλληλεγγύης στην παράλληλη συγκέντρωση φοιτητριών, εργαζομένων, ανέργων και αγωνιστριών στο κάτω Πολυτεχνείο που είχε σκοπό να κρατηθεί ανοιχτός ο ιστορικός χώρος του Πολυτεχνείου και να διασφαλιστεί η διεξαγωγή των εκδηλώσεων του τριημέρου. Η κατειλημμένη πρυτανεία το μεσημέρι της 13/11, αποτελούσε χώρο ανοιχτό για όσα επιθυμούσαμε να στηρίξουμε τον παραπάνω πολιτικό σκοπό, συμμετέχοντας στις συνελεύσεις, ετοιμάζοντας πανό και ζωντανεύοντας την αποκλεισμένη πολυτεχνειούπολη. Εκείνη την ώρα, και τα δύο εγχειρήματα εκκενώθηκαν ταυτόχρονα, από πάνοπλες αστυνομικές δυνάμεις όλων των ειδών (ΕΚΑΜ, ΜΑΤ, ΟΠΚΕ, ΔΕΛΤΑ, κρατική ασφάλεια), σημειώνοντας το εντυπωσιακό ρεκόρ των 92 ταυτόχρονων συλλήψεων σε πανεπιστημιακούς χώρους. Συγκεκριμενα για την πολυτεχνειούπολη, οι δυνάμεις καταστολής περικύκλωσαν και εισέβαλαν στο κτίριο, σπάζοντας πόρτες και παράθυρα και προκαλώντας φθορές όσο τα άτομα που βρισκόμασταν στο χώρο συγκεντρωθήκαμε αντανακλαστικά στο προαύλιο του κτιρίου. Χαρακτηριστικό της βιαιότητας της επιχείρησης ήταν πως σύμφωνα με μαρτυρίες, ο “έλεγχος” στο κτήριο συνεχίστηκε με ήχους σπασιμάτων έως και 2 ώρες μετά την εκκένωση (

http://yd.ntua.gr/2020/11/13/καταγγελία-του-σ…

), με σκοπό το στήσιμο ενός πιο επιβαρυντικού/αναβαθμισμένου κατηγορητηρίου. Οι κατηγορίες που αντιμετωπίζουμε περιλαμβάνουν φθορά ξένης περιουσίας, παρακώλυση δημόσιας υπηρεσίας, παραβίαση των μέτρων για την πρόληψη ασθενειών, προσβολή εθνικού συμβόλου, απείθεια και άλλες πλημμεληματικού βαθμού.


Επιπλέον λίγους μήνες μετά, 13 από τους συλληφθέντες, καθώς και άλλος ένας σύντροφος που ταυτοποιήθηκε αποτύπωμα του, άρχισαν να λαμβάνουν κλήσεις για λήψη γενετικού υλικού και ανάλυση DNA. Η συγκεκριμένη κλήση αναφέρει ότι υπάρχει ταύτιση ανδρικού γενετικού υλικού μεταξύ κινητού αντικειμένου (άδειου μπουκαλιού) που βρέθηκε εντός της κατειλημμένης πρυτανείας, με κάποια χαρτιά με αίμα που εντοπίστηκαν επί της οδού Σπύρου Τρικούπη στα Εξάρχεια στις 7/12/2014, μέρα που είχε γίνει και επίθεση κατά δελτάδων με μολότοφ. Η δικογραφία των γεγονότων του 2014 ήταν κακουργηματικού χαρακτήρα, και μάλιστα σαθρή από μόνη της λόγω της σύνδεσης μιας ματωμένης χαρτοπετσέτας με επίθεση σε μπάτσους. Η συσχέτιση των δύο αυτών υποθέσεων με 6 χρόνια απόστασης μεταξύ τους, καθιστά εμφανή την πρόθεση της ΕΛ.ΑΣ. για γενετικό φακέλωμα και κατασκευή σκευωρίας εις βάρος αγωνιστών. Σημειωτέο ότι οι περισσότεροι από τους κληθέντες ήταν το 2014 περίπου 13 ετών, ενώ ορισμένοι δεν διέμεναν καν στην Αθήνα. Η χρήση γενετικού υλικού ή αποτυπωμάτων (ιδίως πάνω σε κινητά αντικείμενα) με σκοπό την αυθαίρετη σύνδεση υποθέσεων και την ενοχοποίηση αγωνιστών, αποτελεί μια πάγια εκδικητική και επικοινωνιακή πρακτική του κράτους. Μερικά μόνο παραδείγματα είναι οι υποθέσεις της Ηριάννας και η πρόσφατη των Αμπελοκήπων, όπου οι μπάτσοι για να δημιουργήσουν κατηγορητήριο χρησιμοποιούν μοναδικό στοιχείο τις σχέσεις ή την πολιτική ταυτότητα και δράση των κατηγορούμενων.


Από τον Νοέμβριο του ’20 έως και σήμερα, βλέπουμε στα πανεπιστήμια μια ολοένα αυξανόμενη ποινικοποίηση της συνδικαλιστικής και πολιτικής δράσης, με σκοπό τελικά την αποστείρωσή τους. Αυτό αποτελεί προϋπόθεση για να καταστήσει τα πανεπιστήμια ασφαλής πόλους επενδύσεων, κάτι που ξέρουμε πολύ καλά πως με την πρόφαση της «ανάπτυξης» σημαίνει συμμόρφωση με εργασιακούς όρους που …

content:

„

Vor 10 Jahren erweiterte sich der Raum der europäischen Arbeitnehmerfreizügigkeit auf Rumänien und Bulgarien. Heute leben etwa 1,3 Mio. Doch oft wird die Migration aus diesen beiden Ländern noch immer als Armutszuwanderung stigmatisiert. author: Steven Methven
title: How Zohran Mamdani Helped Germany’s Left Party Win in Berlin
content:
In Berlin’s state elections, Germany’s most leftwing party Die Linke has won a significant victory – the biggest in its

recent

 history. It could also mean that the city gets its first mayor from the party since the fall of the Berlin wall.


That’s partly due to the apparently infinite influence of New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose team helped supercharge the German left with the infectious positivity he’s world famous for. But it’s also down to policy – and in particular a long-standing pledge to expropriate housing from the private sector for public supply in a city where rents have

soared by 70%

 in the last decade. 


Die Linke’s Elif Eralp, a human rights advocate

sporting a ‘rent cap’ necklace

, may well become Berlin’s first anti-capitalist mayor since reunification. The daughter of Turkish immigrants, she led the party to a clear victory in Berlin’s Sunday election, taking 26% of the vote – several points over what the polls predicted, by running on a platform squarely targeted at Berliners’ cost of living. 


It all came with a little help from some friends. According to the Washington Post, in the weeks leading up to the race, Die Linke

sent a delegation to New York

 to meet with advisers to Mamdani. “The success of a democratic socialist in New York, the heartland of capitalism, is a huge achievement,” Eralp

said last week.

 “We’ve exchanged a lot of ideas.”


Die Linke, which has more than doubled its membership since 2024, was an early adopter of some of Mamdani’s techniques, not least of all

a massive ground game

 and

lashings of social media flare

 in last year’s federal election. In Berlin, they took another leaf from his policy rule book: keep it simple and keep it real.


Simple and real the campaign was, with a laser focus on

Berlin’s mounting housing crisis

.


Throw a stone in Europe, and you’ll hit a major city in a housing emergency. Crippling rents, gobbling Pac-Man-like one steadily increasing chunk of your paycheck after another, are increasingly the complaint not just of the under-30s, but many of those knocking up against midlife. And Berlin, a city where

84% of the population rent

, and more than half from private landlords, is no exception.


The monthly extortion that is the city’s rental market has been blamed for any number of social ills. Last year, Berlin’s

birth rate dropped

 by 5% on 2024. At the same time, some 160,000 people (a growing trend) are thought to have

left the city

, many for cheaper housing elsewhere. 10% of Berliners

live in housing poverty

. 


It’s a problem that’s been long-brewing. A 2021 referendum saw Berlin’s residents vote in favour of the city’s government

seizing privately-owned flats

 from large corporate landlords. While it wasn’t binding, what it proposed appeared legal, with Germany’s 1949 constitution – the Basic Law – giving the state the right to

bring private property into public ownership

 in exchange for appropriate compensation to former owners.  


Late last year, a

law drafted by political supporters

 inched the referendum towards a concrete reality. Enacting that law and forcibly buying back 220,000 flats from

multinationals like Vonovia

 at around 60% of market value was a major plank in Die Linke’s pitch. Another was rent caps. And that – no duh – seems to have worked. 


The result puts Die Linke far ahead of their nearest challenger, the centre-right Christian Democrats (CDU). That’s the party of Germany’s

beleaguered chancellor Friedrich Merz

. But in order to govern, it’ll

need to enter a three-way coalition

. 


Treachery aside, it’ll include the German Greens, who came fourth in this election also on a commitment to push the property law through. Die Linke will need the support of the centre-left too, in the form of the market-friendly Social Democrats (SPD), whose collapse in support has pushed them to a distant fifth. They previously ran the city in coalition with the CDU. Surprise, surprise, the party’s lead candidate in the city has already said

he’s against expropriation

. 


I predict Sturm und Drang ahead. 


Germany’s far-right party, Alternativ für Deutschland (AfD) also did better than expected in Berlin on 16% of the vote, with its leader bitterly claiming that

Die Linke wants to shoot the rich

. It also won –

though very narrowly

 – another state election on Sunday. In north-eastern Germany’s Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, it grew its voteshare by a stonking 21%. It …

author: Randi Beers
title: A case for rent control in Nunavut
content:
As temperatures drop and we start to prepare for another fall, we’re reminded of one of Nunavut’s most urgent problems: housing.


Andrew Morrison


We don’t need another study to make us aware of the crisis. We see it every day not only on the streets of Iqaluit, but in other, more hidden ways: students coming home with nowhere to live, families crammed into relatives’ homes and long-time Iqalummiut losing their staff housing when they retire. Too many people face various forms of homelessness in their own homeland.


The numbers back this up. The Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp. reports that Iqaluit’s rental vacancy rate was just 0.3 per cent in 2025 — six empty units out of nearly 2,000. That leaves tenants with almost no alternatives and lets rents climb far beyond what many can afford.


Nunavut should freeze rents.


Rent control won’t solve the whole housing crisis. It won’t build the homes we badly need, and it won’t house everyone who is currently without shelter. But a rent freeze will help address staggering rental rates that seem to be going up every time we blink. 


Rent control won’t lower today’s already high rates, but it would limit how fast they can rise in future. Right now, Nunavut’s Residential Tenancies Act allows landlords to raise rent once every 12 months, with three months’ written notice — but sets no limit on the size of the increase.


For example, a landlord could raise rent on a one-bedroom apartment from $2,500 to $5,000 a month, as long as the notice requirements are met. There’s no cap. In a territory where buying a house seems more and more like a distant dream (or nightmare) and government staff housing regimes inflate the rental market, local tenants simply have nowhere else to go.


A freeze on rent can also have other positive impacts on tenant rights. Following New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s election on a rent-freeze platform, reports suggest New York landlords became more responsive to tenants’ repair requests, potentially reflecting the benefits of prioritizing tenants’ rights.


The path forward is clear. The minister of justice can amend the Residential Tenancies Act to let municipalities set their own rent-control rules, within territory-wide minimum standards. Iqaluit could adopt protections suited to its pressures, while Igloolik would remain free to choose its own approach.


We have a rental officer who hears landlord-tenant disputes. That office should be given authority to investigate unlawful rent increases, order repayment and enforce the rules.


Any new rules should cover all new rental units and should apply to housing paid for by governments and Inuit organizations. Rent control is also in the interest of the Nunavut government, Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. and other institutions facing steep staff-housing cost increases over the past 15 years.


Of all the housing problems we face, this one has a straightforward fix. The GN, NTI, and the City of Iqaluit should push for that authority — and use it.


Nunavummiut deserve stronger tenant rights and the security of knowing their homes will stay within reach.


Andrew Morrison is a lawyer and musician who lives in Iqaluit.


Nunatsiaq News invites readers to submit letters to the editor for publication. They must be less than 500 words and signed by the writer. Please send them to 

editors@nunatsiaq.com

.

author: Anneke Demanuele
title: Albo is proud to be a houso—will anyone else get the chance?
content:
“I’m proud to be a houso, and I’m proud of the community in which I grew up.” These were the words of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, spoken with a quivering top lip, after One Nation leader Pauline Hanson attacked his mother, Maryanne Albanese, for living most of her life in a public housing unit.

“Housing commission houses should not be there for people to live in them for 30, 40 [years]”, Hanson said. “And he said his mother lived in the same one she was born in for 65 years.”

Albanese may be proud to be a houso, but his party is ensuring that very few others will be able to access the level of housing security he and his mother did. Across the country, public housing is being eroded and depleted—homes and buildings left in disrepair, demolished or sold off to private developers. The idea that the government should build and provide long-term public housing to those who need it has been almost entirely destroyed.

In Victoria, public housing has been decimated. Walk-up estates have been bulldozed to make way for luxury developments, and 44 apartment towers are scheduled for demolition. The UN special rapporteur on adequate housing, Koldo Casla, has condemned the slated demolition of the 44 towers. In his letter to the Australian government, Casla writes:

“I am concerned that affected residents have primarily been treated as occupants of public property rather than as rights-holders entitled to participate in decisions fundamentally affecting their homes and communities.”

Demolishing housing will force residents out of homes meant to be permanent, out of their communities and away from vital services and infrastructure they depend on. All in the middle of a housing crisis.

According to the Victorian Housing Peaks Alliance, Victoria needs 377,000 more social housing dwellings by 2051 to accommodate everyone who needs low-cost housing. Instead of demolishing public housing and handing over public land to private developers, the government should refurbish existing stock and build new homes.

“It must be reasonably feared that the destruction of 44 public housing towers in central locations or the city will rather amplify these problems and not be a suitable measure to address these preexisting violations of the right to adequate housing”, Casla notes.

The Victorian Labor government says that the total number of dwellings will increase. But it will cut public housing unit numbers significantly. They will be replaced by a mix of community housing, run by not-for-profit agencies, and private dwellings sold at market rates. Tenants have fewer rights, face higher costs, enjoy less long-term housing security and are more easily evicted from community housing as compared to public housing. Data from the Australian Institute of Housing and Welfare in 2023, for instance, shows that when comparing public and community housing tenure length, the proportion of public housing residents that have lived in their homes for more than a decade is twice that of the community housing sector.

Residents in inner-city suburbs will and have been shunted off to outer suburbs, far from the schools, kindergartens and other services they rely on and that connect them with others. Many won’t be able to return to public housing at all.

This adds to the general erosion of the idea that housing is a human right that should be guaranteed to all. Instead of being an option for working-class people to live in, raise their families and build their communities over a lifetime, public housing is increasingly seen as a temporary option for only the most desperate—those living in extreme poverty and for whatever reason unable to participate in the labour market. Today, it is being deliberately run down to make its demolition or sell-off inevitable.

Public housing in Australia has always fallen below the standard of Britain and Western Europe. Writing in the

Marxist Left Review

, Jordan Humphreys details the limitations: “Access to public housing would be restricted to those on very low incomes, so it would be put aside only for the very poorest of the poor. If not enough of the poor could be found, then the Housing Commissions were encouraged to sell off ‘excess’ housing stock”. By the 1960s, two-thirds of British people lived in public housing, compared to only 4.2 percent of Australians (today it is about 2.6 percent).

The Victorian government’s housing strategy document describes public housing as a “legacy”, and what remains is intended …

author: Amira El-Fekki
title: Clashes flare around Warraq with tensions high as island residents campaign for housing guarantees
content:
Warraq Island residents clashed with security forces deployed intensively on and around the Nile island this week, with tensions flaring as authorities are yet to respond to the residents’ demands for clear answers and guarantees regarding the fate of their homes and lands.


The new chapter in talks between residents and authorities comes as families in Warraq take action to disrupt the government’s ongoing development project and seek firm guarantees that officials will support them to stay in their homes and lands.


Security forces set up on Tuesday metal mesh barriers at the entrance to the Qolaly ferry crossing that connects the island to the Nile bank, and, on Wednesday, more barriers were added in the vicinity of the crossing, according to a resident of the island who spoke to Mada Masr.


The measures, they said, add to a series of existing restrictions already imposed on the residents’ movement and access to key goods and services.


The new barriers appear intended to protect security personnel, after stones were thrown during clashes with residents near the ferry crossing in the preceding days, the resident said.


The latest of these took place at Qolaly on Sunday and Monday, with several residents injured as a result, including a young man whose skull was fractured in the clashes, they added.


To protest the security response to the Qolaly clashes, several residents also gathered at a demonstration on Monday evening near a security forces deployment stationed beneath the Tahya Misr Bridge that runs through the island.


The gathering ended in further

clashes

, according to two residents who were present. The confrontations were visible in footage posted by Warraq residents on social media.


As the ban on construction materials entering the island continues, the Qolaly ferry crossing, the main entry point to Warraq from Giza, has been a flashpoint of near-daily confrontations between residents and security forces for around nine years. One resident said to Mada Masr that the friction around the entry of materials to the island arises mainly between security forces and residents who work to deliver construction supplies to the island — but the clashes it triggers spill over to other residents in the area around the ferry.


The clashes come in parallel to a campaign to remain the island that residents have pursued since August. A large number of island residents have begun organizing as part of a group called Staying on Warraq, pushing for firm guarantees from authorities regarding the fate of their land and homes, according to several residents who have spoken to Mada Masr in recent weeks, particularly as circulating reports and unofficial maps of the government’s development project appear to include parts of the residents’ lands.


For years, residents have watched the development project unfold, waiting to learn what would happen to them, while their access to basic services on the island — like healthcare and education — has deteriorated due to state restrictions, leaving residents to establish replacements or alternatives themselves. Their efforts have included spending around LE400,000 to prepare schools for the current academic year.


They have now concluded that waiting has brought no solutions, as the state continues to carry out the project after

acquiring

most of the island’s land, the residents have said.


As part of this campaign, residents attempted on Sunday to obstruct the state’s road construction work on the island, blocking the way of transportation trucks involved in the state development project. The following day, they

held

a protest outside the New Warraq City Development Authority, where they vowed to escalate until their demands are met.


“People went out and stood outside the authority because the state is now building the roads, and they found out that the roads are getting close to residents’ homes. What impact will this have in terms of demolitions?” a lawyer from the island told Mada Masr.


“The state doesn’t solve anything. It wants to suffocate people so that they get fed up and leave,” one of the two residents who witnessed Monday’s clashes said. They said residents planned to continue disrupting the construction work being carried out by the state. “God willing, all the work will stop,” they said.

author: winter oak
title: The Love Activists
content:
This is the third in a selection of chapters from the book 

King of the Squatters

 by jaybo which we are delighted to be able to share on Winter Oak. The whole text can be found as a pdf

here

.


Here we are in 2015.


I do not recall my last night in Ireland, at all. I was extremely upset to leave Amy and all of our new friends behind. They got me very drunk to deal with the situation. When I arrived back in Liverpool, the Love Activists (LAs) had achieved support and notoriety in the city, after squatting six different high-profile places in a few months. The LAs had started out in London, declaring themselves to be anarchists driven, by love, to help house and feed the homeless and bring down the evil bankers and their corrupt system.


One LA known as ‘Grandad’ described the LAs eviction from the Bank of England to me. He said that they had been kept on lock-down, a prison term for everyone being locked up in their cells, for two long weeks by the police. The police had erected a tall steel fence which completely surrounded the bank and a cordon of cops then stood completely surrounding the fence all day and night. Upon witnessing this action local people spontaneously formed their own human chain surrounding the police and also maintained a 24/7 presence. Supporters cheekily threw many crucial supplies right over the polices heads to grateful activists who caught them on window balconies!


He said, “Almost everybody who entered the bank respected the building. Only a few made some graffiti on walls, and that could have easily been painted over. But the police did not respect the building cutting through those amazing doors.” Grandad also told me, with great pride, “The fire bobbies were called to the eviction. When they arrived, they talked and quickly decided that they were employed to save lives, not evict homeless people. They fucked off, to cheers from the crowd of hundreds surrounding the police. Ha Ha!”


Having been unceremoniously evicted from the Bank of England on Castle Street in the spring, the LAs had blazed a trail of six squats from the city centre, south, ending up on Sefton Park meadows. They had set up camp “right outside fat Joe’s new offices”, fat Joe being the name many of our people in the city used to describe the deeply unpopular

mayor of Liverpool

. The LAs had squatted a Georgian terraced block of houses in the city centre, and they did a sit-down protest on the road at the entrance to the Mersey car tunnel, closing the tunnel down completely. They had stormed the city, which had not seen any squatting in the previous twenty years, and received the support and admiration of thousands of ordinary people across the region.


As I approached the LAs camp on Sefton Meadows for the first time, it warmed my heart to see the anarchist flag that had hung from the Bank of England flying high, together with a Bob Marley flag. As I got closer, I saw a big banner at the side of the kitchen, next to the camp’s entrance, which read in large letters, ‘Uprising of the Homeless’. I never expected to read such an audacious banner and was utterly intrigued.


The LAs and Uprising of the Homeless (UOTH) camp was right on my old doorstep. Situated just across Princes Park to Sefton Park on the meadows beyond. A lovely, open site that had been left to the people of Liverpool, two hundred years previously, in perpetuity, i.e. forever, as a green haven in an industrial city. Sefton Park was one of Liverpool’s biggest and best parks, just a short walk from the city centre and the River Mersey. There were huge, magnificent, old trees surrounding the meadows, and about twenty-five raggle-taggle tents had been erected in the middle, surrounded by a rope border.


On a beautiful early summer’s afternoon, with everything I owned in my backpack, I slowly walked across the meadows towards the camp, full of anticipation. There was a group of mostly men sitting around a small fire. I saw Jed and Grandad first. They both gave me a huge smile as I got closer. Then I saw Lisa Love, looking like a futuristic steam punk. She also gave me a huge smile and had a very powerful energy. She seemed to have all of the men’s respect. Then I saw Biggy, and he gave me possibly the cheekiest smile I had ever seen. I knew immediately that I would be fine with the LAs and UOTH. I was definitely in the right place.


Most of the guys that I met at the camp considered themselves to be both LAs and UOTH. I asked about the Bank of …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Neuquén: la provincia le dio la personería jurídica a la comunidad Melo pero sigue la amenaza de desalojo
content:
En Neuquén el gobierno provincial acaba de reconocer la personería jurídica a la Lof Melo. Lo paradójico de esta situación es que la reconoce la personería jurídica como comunidad, sin embargo la amenaza de desalojo no retrocede.


Escuchá el reporte de Maitén Cañicul desde la FM Che.


Julieta Melo, werquen de la Lof Melo, expresó al respecto: “El gobierno nos otorgó la personería jurídica y con este acto se cerró la discusión. Este conflicto no es un conflicto entre privados” y agregó que “la personería jurídica es el DNI colectivo de una comunidad mapuche, algo que viene negando sistemáticamente el juez Bonorino y la terrateniente Cristina Broers a través de su abogado Guillermo Hensel”.


“No necesitábamos estos papeles para demostrar nuestra existencia colectiva como comunidad, pero sabemos que en este sistema era la evidencia con la que podíamos tirar por la borda esa persistente postura negacionista”, explicó.


Los seis consejos zonales de la Confederación Mapuche en Neuquén presentaron una nota a Rolando Figueroa, gobernador de la provincia y al ministro Jorge Tobares, solicitando la personería jurídica no sólo a la comunidad Melo sino también a otras comunidades que la vienen reclamando hace bastante tiempo: “Instamos al gobierno de la provincia del Neuquén el otorgamiento inmediato de personerías jurídicas a todas las comunidades mapuche que la están demandando”.


Además solicitaban la intervención urgente del gobierno de Neuquén ante el fallo injusto del juez Bonorino que mantiene bajo grave amenaza a la comunidad Melo: “La situación de un inminente desalojo no ha cesado, generando una carga emocional sobre mi comunidad. Nos llevará mucho tiempo reparar todo el daño ya causado, por eso el acompañamiento que estamos teniendo hace mucho más llevadera esta situación”.


“Sabemos que si el juez Bonorino mantiene esta postura negacionista y racista hacia nuestra lof y pretende llevar adelante este desalojo, estos acompañamientos se van a multiplicar por todo el territorio”, agregó.

author: CNT Villaverde Alto - Comarcal Sur de Madrid
title: Defendamos La Casika: contra el desalojo del próximo 6 de octubre
content:
La Casika, no es sólo un centro social, es mucho más que el edificio que habita.


La Casika es un proyecto de autoorganización popular, es un referente como herramienta para la expansión de la 

cultura militante y de lucha,

 

con

 una agenda cultural propia y reivindicativa y que ha tejido redes sociales y políticas en estos casi 30 años. Es una escuela política y de intervención social, un espacio de reflexión y debate.


Durante casi tres décadas ha sido un lugar abierto a iniciativas sociales, políticas y culturales para 

el encuentro, para la organización desde abajo, construida desde abajo para las de abajo

, estrechamente vinculado al territorio, a la clase trabajadora, a quienes construyen contrapoder y comunidad contra la mercantilización de la vida.


Desde CNT Comarcal Sur apoyamos y apoyaremos siempre proyectos construidos colectivamente desde abajo para transformar la sociedad en todos y cada uno de los aspectos que nos oprimen como personas.


Por eso hacemos un llamamiento a la defensa de este histórico espacio. Porque 29 años de historia política social y cultural en Móstoles no la pueden borrar de un plumazo los aparatos del Estado. Animamos a consultar las 

redes sociales

 de la Casika para estar al tanto de todas las iniciativas programadas en el marco del posible desalojo, como la manifestación convocada el 3 de octubre o la llamada a resistir en la fecha prevista, el próximo martes 6.


Defendamos nuestros espacios, defendamos la Casika.

author: Unknown
title: Diyadin'de siyanürlü altın aramaya tepki: "Murat Nehri'nden siyanür değil, yaşam aksın
content:
Mış – Muş Demokratik Kurumlar Platformu, Ağrı’nın Diyadin ilçesinde siyanürle altın çıkarılması planlanan altın madeni projesine karşı, Atatürk Parkı önünde basın açıklaması gerçekleştirdi. “Topraklarımıza sahip çıkıyoruz. Madenleri istemiyoruz. Şirketlerin kârı için halkın geleceği yok edilemez. Mollakarada maden istemiyoruz” pankartının açıldığı açıklamaya, çok sayıda siyasi parti ve sivil toplum örgütü temsilcisi katıldı. Basın metnini Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti) Muş İl Eş Başkanı Çiçek Tutuş okudu.

Murat Nehri'nin bölge için önemine dikkat çeken Çiçek Tutuş, nehirde meydana gelecek bir kirliliğin geleceğe büyük bir tehdit oluşturacağını vurguladı. Siyanür kullanımının ciddi çevresel tehditler yarattığını kaydeden Çiçek Tutuş, "Bugün bize ekonomik kazançtan, istihdamdan ve yatırım değerinden söz edilebilir. Ancak biz soruyoruz: Bir madenin ekonomik getirisi, kirlenme riski altındaki su kaynaklarımızdan daha mı değerlidir? Bir şirketin elde edeceği kazanç, çiftçinin toprağından, hayvancılıkla geçinen yurttaşın merasından ve çocuklarımızın temiz su hakkından daha mı önemlidir? Hiçbir ekonomik faaliyet, yaşam hakkının ve doğanın üzerinde değildir. Altın yer altında kalabilir. Ancak su kaynaklarımızın kirlenmesi, tarım alanlarımızın zarar görmesi ve doğal yaşamın yok olması durumunda kayıplarımızı geri getirmek kolay olmayacaktır. Bu nedenle suyu ve toprağı yalnızca ekonomik bir kaynak olarak gören anlayışı kabul etmiyoruz. Su, toprağın ve yaşamın ortak varlığıdır. Kamu yararı, şirketlerin kârından önce gelmelidir" ifadelerini kullandı.

Murat Nehri havzasında siyanürlü altın çıkarma faaliyeti istemediklerini vurgulayan Çiçek Tutuş, "Murat Nehri’ni savunmak; Muş Ovası’nı, Diyadin’in meralarını, bölgenin tarımını ve bütün havzanın geleceğini savunmaktır. Bizler, doğayı şirketlerin kâr hesabına teslim eden anlayışa karşı; emeği, yaşamı, ortak varlıkları ve ekolojik dengeyi savunan bir çizgide duruyoruz. Suyun sahibi şirketler değil, halktır. Topraklarımız sermayenin sınırsız kullanım alanı değildir. Yaşam alanlarımız hiçbir ekonomik kazanç uğruna feda edilemez. Buradan bir kez daha açıkça ifade ediyoruz: Murat Nehri havzasında siyanürlü altın madenciliği istemiyoruz. Bu faaliyetin sona erdirilmesini ve maden sahasının kapatılmasını istiyoruz. Çünkü bizler, çocuklarımıza kirli sular, zehirlenmiş topraklar ve yok edilmiş meralar bırakmak istemiyoruz. Bizler, yaşanabilir bir gelecek istiyoruz. Murat Nehri’nden siyanür değil, yaşam aksın" dedi.

Çiçek Tutuş, 26 Eylül'de (Cumartesi) Diyadin'de düzenlenecek olan ekoloji mitingine çağrı yaparak sözlerini bitirdi. Basın açıklaması, alkışlarla sona erdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Mobilisation for the Kurdish language
content:
The demand for mother-tongue education has long been one of the central issues in discussions surrounding the Kurdish question and democratisation in Turkey. As the Peace and Democratic Society Process is being debated, the right to mother-tongue education and official status for Kurdish are seen not only as matters of education policy but also as fundamental conditions for social peace.


Heval Dilbahar, Co-Spokesperson of the Language, Culture and Arts Commission of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), said Kurdish-language education from preschool to university is possible and that, if the state demonstrates the necessary political will, existing shortcomings could be addressed within two to three years and Kurdish-language education introduced in schools.


In a report by Lütfi Pala of Mezopotamya Agency, Dilbahar said the republic was founded on a monist understanding: “A century ago, the Republic was established on a monist understanding. As a result, many languages, particularly Kurdish, were banned. The Kurdish language was subjected to severe pressure, coercion and restrictions. However, as a result of the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom, policies of denial, assimilation, prohibition and eradication were broken. In other words, it is no longer possible to deny or completely eradicate the Kurdish language through conventional methods.”


Kurdish remains under siege


Dilbahar said it would be wrong to assume that the pressure and restrictions imposed on Kurdish have been substantially lifted in recent years, stressing that the language remains under siege. Dilbahar also said: “Kurdish is still under siege and remains restricted in many areas. Kurdish still has no official or legal status, while its exclusion from the constitution and official institutions continues. In practice, pressure, obstruction and restrictions continue against many institutions, organisations and groups working on the Kurdish language. The aim is to gradually erode the Kurdish language under these conditions and distance it from society. Consider that today there are thousands of schools providing education in Turkish across Northern Kurdistan (Bakur), yet there is not a single school providing education entirely in Kurdish. Kurdish-language education remains prohibited. There is no right to education in Kurdish from primary school through university. Turkish-language schools and institutions are being opened in cities, districts, neighbourhoods, streets, villages and even hamlets, with the aim of extending and entrenching the dominance of Turkish throughout Kurdistan. Although the Kurdish people are struggling to protect, develop and expand the use of their language, under these conditions the existing efforts are unfortunately insufficient.”


Why should it not be possible?


Asked whether Kurdish-language education from preschool to university is possible and how it could be implemented, Dilbahar replied: “Education is provided in more than one language in many countries around the world. Multilingual education models are implemented from primary school through university in countries such as Switzerland and Sweden. If this is possible in those countries, why should it not be possible in Northern Kurdistan and Turkey? If the state demonstrates the necessary will and intent, the infrastructure for Kurdish-language education could easily be established within two to three years. It is not accurate to claim that this is technically impossible or that the necessary resources do not exist. What matters is establishing the political will and recognising that the Kurdish people have the right to receive education in Kurdish.”


Legal barriers must be removed


Dilbahar added that, in keeping with the spirit of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the state must remove the legal barriers facing the Kurdish language. Dilbahar said:  “The constitution must guarantee freedoms for both Kurdish and all other languages, and Kurdish must be granted a recognised status. The form this status takes can be discussed, but Kurdish, the language of millions of Kurds, must have official status. Kurdish must become a language of education if it is to preserve itself and be carried into the future. All place names and terms that were originally Kurdish and later Turkified must also be restored to Kurdish. Barriers to the use of Kurdish in official institutions and every sphere of social life must be removed. All the financial …

author: Mag
title: Proteste, Blockaden und unbefristeter Generalstreik in Bolivien gegen die Erhöhung der Kraftstoffpreise und andere Angriffe auf die Kaufkraft der Löhne
content:
Dossier


„

Die neue Regierung unter Rodrigo Paz hat ein Dekret erlassen, das die Subventionen für Kraftstoffe abschafft. Diese Maßnahme, die die Kaufkraft der Löhne beeinträchtigt, hat direkte Auswirkungen auf die Lebenshaltungskosten von Millionen Menschen und hat bereits zu Protesten geführt. Das am Mittwochabend von der neuen Regierung unter Rodrigo Paz in Bolivien unterzeichnete Dekret Nr. 5503 hat bereits Proteste ausgelöst. Die Streichung der Subventionen für Kraftstoffe bedeutet einen direkten Angriff auf die Kaufkraft der Löhne der Arbeitnehmer und der bolivianischen Bevölkerung. Am Freitag standen mehrere Städte des Landes aufgrund von Streiks und Blockaden ohne öffentliche Verkehrsmittel da. Bereits seit Donnerstag gibt es Blockaden auf der Autobahn La Paz-El Alto, um gegen die „de facto”-Erhöhung der Fahrpreise im öffentlichen Nahverkehr zu protestieren

…“ span.

Meldung der Redaktion LID Bolivien vom 19. Dezember in La Izquierda Diario


 (maschinenübersetzt) mit Fotos – siehe mehr Informationen zur weiteren Entwicklung:


Nach der Annahme eines IWF-Kredites und der Abschaffung der Dieselsubvention verlängert Bolivien aus Angst vor neuen Blockaden den Ausnahmezustand um 90 Tage


„Die Regierung in Bolivien hat mit der Begründung eines weiterhin hohen Konfliktpotenzials im Land den Ausnahmezustand verlängert. Kurz nach dem Beschluss wurde mit der Annahme eines Kredites des Internationalen Währungsfonds (IWF) und der damit einhergehenden Abschaffung der Dieselsubvention eine wirtschaftspolitische Maßnahme umgesetzt, die das Konfliktpotenzial im Land erneut anheizen könnte (…).100 der 158 anwesenden Abgeordneten stimmten am vergangenen Donnerstag nach neunstündiger Debatte für die Verlängerung des Ausnahmezustands. Damit bleibt der am 20. Juni von Präsident Rodrigo Paz verhängte Ausnahmezustand nun bis zum 17. Dezember in Kraft. (…) Der Ausnahmezustand geht auf die schwere politische und soziale Krise im Mai und Juni zurück (…). Über sieben Wochen hinweg blockierten unterschiedliche gesellschaftliche Akteure zahlreiche Straßen im ganzen Land. Besonders La Paz und El Alto waren von Engpässen bei Lebensmitteln, Medikamenten und Treibstoff betroffen. Die Proteste forderten mindestens 16 Todesopfer, davon 13 infolge fehlender medizinischer Versorgung aufgrund der Blockaden. Die wirtschaftlichen Schäden wurden auf mehr als drei Milliarden US-Dollar geschätzt. Der Zeitpunkt der Maßnahme wirkt strategisch gewählt, denn bereits am Freitag kündigte Präsident Paz die sofortige und vollständige Abschaffung der staatlichen Dieselsubventionen an, nachdem der Kongress einen Kredit in Höhe von 1,9 Milliarden US-Dollar des IWF zur Stabilisierung der Wirtschaft bewilligt hatte. (…) Kurz nach der Bekanntgabe der Verlängerung wurden am Wochenende bereits die Hauptverkehrsstrecken zwischen Cochabamba, Oruro und La Paz von 500 Sicherheitsbeamten gesichert, die im Mai und Juni Epizentrum der Blockaden waren. Gegen die Abschaffung der Subventionen hatten sich bereits im Vorfeld mehrere produktive Sektoren, darunter Landwirte und Fahrer, ausgesprochen. Es überrascht daher nicht, dass der Verkehrssektor wegen der Verdopplung des Dieselpreises auf nun 17,95 Bolivianos (1,59 Euro) für Montag bereits zu einem unbefristeten Streik aufgerufen hat. Auch der Gewerkschaftsdachverband COB lehnte in einer öffentlichen Erklärung die vollständige Abschaffung der Dieselsubventionen ab und berief eine Dringlichkeitssitzung auf, um die aktuelle Situation zu beurteilen und gegebenenfalls Gegenmaßnahmen umzusetzen.“


Beitrag von Lia Helguero Kandt vom 21. September 2026 in amerika21


 („Bolivien verlängert den Ausnahmezustand um 90 Tage“)


Bolivien: Haftbefehl gegen Morales und andere Protestführer der 53-tägigen Proteste von Mai bis Juni


„Staatsanwalt Brayan Melgar hat in Bolivien einen weiteren Haftbefehl gegen den bolivianischen Expräsidenten Evo Morales angeordnet. (…) Während der 53-tägigen Proteste, die von Mai bis Juni andauerten, wurden rund 100 Straßen blockiert, wodurch ganze Landesteile von der Versorgung mit Lebensmitteln, Medikamenten und Trebstoff abgeschnitten wurden. title: Mass Protest Planned Against Netanyahu’s UN Speech in NYC Thursday
content:
Netanyahu is attempting to “insult and demean the international system” with his visit, one activist said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is set to arrive in New York City on Thursday for the UN General Assembly – where he is expected to defend his warmongering in Iran and Gaza in a speech during the afternoon.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, has presided over the nearly three-year-long genocide in Gaza – which has killed at least 75,000 Palestinians, according to conservative estimates – while pursuing permanent war on states across the region and full annexation of the occupied West Bank.

The prime minister had originally planned to visit the U.S. for several days, but he has decided to cut his visit short by staying in New York City only for a few hours before flying out Thursday evening after his speech at the UN.

Activist organizations across New York City – led by the Palestinian Youth Movement, Jewish Voice for Peace, and the Democratic Socialists of America, among others – have planned a mass demonstration to confront Netanyahu on Thursday outside of the UN headquarters.

Taher Dahleh, an organizer from the Palestinian Youth Movement (PYM), told Truthout that Netanyahu is attempting to “insult and demean the international system and the rest of the states of the world” through his visit, while demonstrating that Israel can leverage forums like the UN’s General Assembly for its own interests and remain welcomed by the U.S.

But it cannot be ignored that Netanyahu has presided over “three years of genocide and spiraling regional war which has hit countries from Lebanon to Iran, Yemen to Iraq, in addition to devastating the Palestinian people, particularly in Gaza,” Dahleh stated.

In November 2024, the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu, charging him with war crimes, including “starvation as a method of warfare” and crimes against humanity committed during the war on Gaza since October 2023.

The 125 member states of the ICC are expected to abide by the arrest warrant and hand Netanyahu over to the ICC if he arrives in their territory.

But the Trump administration has ridiculed the ICC as “illegitimate” and “politicized,” and has worked to undermine the court. As far back as 2020, Trump began to target ICC members with sanctions, freezing their assets and threatening their livelihoods. According to a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday, the Trump administration is currently looking to announce sanctions against the ICC as a whole.

Others, however, have stated that the ICC has not gone far enough. In response to the 2024 sanctions, Palestinian legal organization Al-Haq emphasized that Netanyahu and Israel’s crimes “did not begin on 8 October 2023” but have continued for much longer – with the expansion of settlements in the West Bank having taken place over decades, and the siege of Gaza beginning in 2007, to name only a few examples.

Netanyahu has also directly overseen numerous war crimes in his nearly 20-year tenure as Israeli prime minister, including the 2012 war on Gaza (“Operation Pillar of Defense”), which killed at least 150 Palestinians; the 2014 war on Gaza (“Operation Protective Edge”), which killed over 2,250 Palestinians in the course of 50 days; and the 2021 war on Gaza, which killed over 250 Palestinians. The current genocide, with a death toll of 75,000 in Gaza and nearly 9,000 in Lebanon since 2023, surpasses these numbers, but is nonetheless a continuation of these crimes.

The Israeli prime minister is currently in the middle of an election campaign where he has deployed anti-Arab fearmongering and repeatedly referenced his 2024 pager attacks on Lebanon – which witnessed mass casualties and has been deemed a war crime – as a key example of his military and security prowess.

In his policy of permanent war, Netanyahu has pursued war with Iran for decades, before finally gaining US approval and launching the 2025 war on Iran and the joint 2026 US-Israeli war on Iran that has lasted the better part of this year.

author: David Swanson
title: International Day of Peace Demonstrations Demand Australia Scrap AUKUS, Cut Weapons Ties with Israel
content:
By Kerry Smith,

green left

, September 22, 2026


Protesters took to the streets on September 21 to demand the Labor government breaks its military ties with the United States and Israel.


The protests, on the eve of the United Nations Day of Peace, highlighted how the federal government’s decision to support the Coalition-orchestrated AUKUS binds it to support the Israeli state’s genocide in Gaza.


From

Kaurna Yerta/Adelaide

, Markela Panegyres reports that there was a festive atmosphere for the rally at Yartapuulti (Port Adelaide). Speakers called for an end to AUKUS and militarism and demanded the Australian government support Palestine by cutting ties with Israel. The protest was organised by

Port Adelaide Community Opposing AUKUS

.


Two choirs, a giant inflatable submarine, kayakers, drums, music and street theatre were highlights. Another was the arrival of the Peacewalkers Against AUKUS, who had walked more than 400 kilometres from Port Augusta to Port Adelaide to say “No to AUKUS”.


Western Australians gathered at the Rockingham War Memorial, marched to Churchill Park and on to Rockingham Jetty opposite Stirling, Garden Island. It was organised by a number of groups, including

Reject AUKUS Rockingham

, 

Stop AUKUS WA

 and Independent and Peaceful Australia Network. Speakers and attendees called for AUKUS to be cancelled and the Australia-US war alliance to be cancelled.


People were informed that as of 2027 up to four US and one British nuclear-powered submarine will be on rotation at HMAS Stirling. It is now feared that Stirling will, in effect, become a US base and that future US “rotating” nuclear powered submarines could also be nuclear armed.


Speakers said it is increasingly clear that AUKUS will not keep us safe and that US submarines and defence assets in Cockburn Sound risks making WA a military target.


Susan Price reports that Amnesty International organised an event at Southport on

Kombumerri Country/Gold Coast.

 Speakers included Helen O’Sullivan, a Gaza Flotilla activist, Halikl Keretas from Amnesty and Ofure Agbon, a high school student, who spoke about the war in Sudan.


Sydney Anti-AUKUS Coalition (SAAC) and Stop the War on Palestine (SWOP) co-organised the protest which drew up to 300 people to Sydney Town Hall, on

Gadigal Country

, reports Pip Hinman.


As the US and Israel continue their war on Palestine, with Australia’s full support, Palestinian-Australian Saffa called for an end to the two-war arms trade and to cut ties with Israel. She described the campaign against Bisalloy which has been awarded another contract to make armoured steel for Israel’s F35 jet fighters.


Australia is also deeply implicated in the genocide because it supplies intelligence through the Pine Gap spy base in central Australia that can be used by Israel to pinpoint targets. Cathy Eatock, Co-Chair of the Indigenous Peoples Organisation of Australia, drew the connection between the AUKUS war pact and Australia’s policy towards Israel, pointing to Australia’s refusal to join some European countries’ mild condemnation of Israeli settlers occupation on the West Bank.


Professor Jocelyn Chey, a China specialist, put the case for a foreign policy that “does not take sides” between the US and China.


NSW Greens Senator David Shoebridge said it was frightening how lock-step the major parties are on AUKUS. Arthur Rorris, Secretary, South Coast Labour Council, said the South Coast is united in opposing a submarine base on Port Kembla on the basis of the nuclear threat, the lack of sustainable jobs associated with AUKUS.


Tilly Fay from SWOP called on people to keep protesting for Palestine, and defending those who do and are penalised for doing so. She said

a teacher had been stood down

 for his pro-Palestine views.


Peter Murphy from SAAC appealed to attendees to get involved in building a bigger political force against AUKUS, to force Labor to rethink this disastrous alliance which is escalating tension with China, plunging money into submarines that could be spent on essential services and threatening communities including First Nations peoples with nuclear waste dumps on their land.

International Day of Peace Demonstrations Demand Australia Scrap AUKUS, Cut Weapons Ties with Israel

World BEYOND War

title: Hakan Tosun cinayeti: Sanık avukatları gelmedi, mahkeme karar açıklamadı
content:
İstanbul Esenyurt’ta 10 Ekim 2025 gecesi sokak ortasında bir grup erkeğin saldırısı sonucu hayatını kaybeden gazeteci ve belgeselci Hakan Tosun’un ölümüne ilişkin dava bugün üçüncü duruşmayla devam etti.


Bakırköy 17. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’ndeki duruşmada Tosun’un ailesi ve avukatları Hakan Bozyurt ile Cemal Yücel hazır bulundu.


Sanıklar Abdurrahman Murat ve Adnan Şahin tutuldukları cezaevlerinden Ses ve Görüntü Bilişim Sistemi (SEGBİS) aracılığıyla duruşmaya katıldı.


Duruşmayı takip etmek isteyen basın mensupları ve yurttaşlar ana salona alınmadı. Ek salondaki ekranlar üzerinden davayı takip etti. Salonda yer bulamayan çok sayıda izleyici de duruşmayı adliye koridorundan takip etti.


Duruşmada söz alan Hakan Tosun’un avukatı Cemal Yücel, sanıkların ve tanıkların iddialarının kamera görüntüleriyle tamamen çürütüldüğünü belirterek şunları kaydetti:


"Yalancı tanıkların iddia ettiği uyduruk şeylerin hiçbirinin olmadığı kamera kayıtlarında açıkça görülmektedir. Dört tekme vurulmuştur; tekmelerin şiddeti o kadar fazladır ki Hakan Tosun her darbeden sonra geriye doğru kaymak zorunda kalmıştır. Kamera görüntülerinde Hakan’ın sanıklara yönelik herhangi bir saldırısı veya sözü yoktur. Sanık Abdurrahman bununla da yetinmemiş, 7 dakika önce diğer sokağın başına arabasıyla gelip bekleyen diğer sanık Adnan’la birleşerek tekmeler atmış, ardından aynı araçla uzaklaşmışlardır."


Yücel, sanıkların olay yerinden ayrıldıktan sonra tekrar dönerek yarım bıraktıkları işi tamamladıklarını söyledi:


"BMW araçla yeniden aynı sokağa dönüp Hakan Tosun'un önünden geçmişler. 50 metre gittikten sonra davada sanık olması gerekirken tanık yapılan Yusuf Özakdağ motoruyla aracın yanına gitmiş, bir şeyler söylemiştir. Bunun üzerine Abdurrahman tekrar gelip yumruklamış ve tekmelemiştir. 'Hiç vurmadım' diyen Adnan araçla gelip tekme atmış, yerde yatan Hakan'ı sertçe silkeleyip bırakmıştır. Tanıklardan biri 'Sarsıp bıraktıktan sonra sesi kesildi' diyor. Sanıklar öldürme kastıyla hareket etmeselerdi ilk olaydaki şiddetli tekmelerden sonra tekrar geri dönüp yarım bıraktıkları eylemi sürdürmezlerdi."


Tosun’un itibarsızlaştırılmaya çalışıldığını da ekleyen Yücel şöyle devam etti.


"Metrobüsteki taciz iddiasıyla Hakan'ı itibarsızlaştırmaya ve bu ölümü hak etmiş gibi göstermeye çalışıyorlar. Bunlar tamamen iftiradır; ezberden söylemiyoruz, görüntüler mahkemenin önündedir. Hakan’ın bir kadına temasının olmadığı, temastan kaçınmak için tutunmaya çalıştığı sabittir. Ayrıca raporda geçen 1 mg fentanil maddesi uyuşturucu değil, hastanede yoğun bakımda tedavi görürken ağrılarını kesmek için verilen tıbbi bir ilaçtır. Haksız tahrik indirimi uygulanmaksızın sanıkların iştirak halinde 'kasten öldürme' suçundan cezalandırılmasını istiyoruz."


Bozyurt: "Motosikletli şahıs hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunulsun"


Tosun ailesinin avukatlarından Hakan Bozyurt ise olayda organize bir eylem olduğuna dikkat çekerek motosikletli 3. şahıs Yusuf Özakdağ’ın sanık olarak yargılanması gerektiğini belirtti:


"Geçen celse sunduğumuz videolarda 3. şahsın rolü açıkça görülüyor. Yusuf Özakdağ adlı kişi Abdurrahman ve Adnan ile birlikte hareket ediyor; Hakan darp edilirken orada bekliyor, araç uzaklaşırken tekrar yanlarına gidip iletişim kuruyor. Bu eylem üçünün organize şekilde gerçekleştirdiği bir saldırıdır. Yusuf Özakdağ hakkında mahkemenizin suç duyurusunda bulunmasını talep ediyoruz."


Bozyurt ayrıca, Hakan Tosun’un mesleki mirası ve ailesi açısından simgesel değeri yüksek olan fotoğraf kamerası ve dijital materyallerinin tarafına teslim edilmesini talep etti.


Söz verilen tutuklu sanıklar Abdurrahman Murat ve Adnan Şahin eski ifadelerini tekrarlayarak tahliyelerini talep etti. Sanık avukatları mahkemeye gelmediği için mahkeme heyeti hüküm kurmadı.


Tutuklu sanıklar Murat ve Şahin’in tutukluluk hallerinin devamına karar verdi. Taraf avukatlarının son savunmalarını yapması ve karar celsesi için duruşmayı 7 Ekim 2026 Çarşamba günü saat 10.30’a bıraktı.

La manifestación, que comenzó en la Plaza Congreso y avanzó a lo largo de la Avenida de Mayo, tuvo su eje en el rechazo a las políticas económicas y de ajuste implementadas por el gobierno de ultraderecha de Javier Milei.


Estuvo impulsada principalmente por el Frente de Izquierda y de los Trabajadores Unidad (FIT-U) y contó con la adhesión de un amplio arco de organizaciones.


En el discurso de cierre, se sostuvo: “Esta es la bronca de quienes trabajamos y estamos lejos de llegar a fin de mes. La bronca de las y los jubilados que trabajaron toda la vida y hoy tienen que elegir entre comer o comprar sus remedios”.


El economista y militante Eduardo Lucita, integrante de Economistas de Izquierda (EDI), escribió un análisis sobre la jornada que compartimos a continuación:


Apuntes rápidos sobre la Marcha de la Bronca


“Para que nadie se quede peleando solo” MB.


Este sábado 19 de septiembre en horas de la tarde se llevó a delante la Marcha de la Bronca. Convocada hace poco más de dos meses atrás por la diputada nacional Myriam Bregman, la principal figura de la izquierda anticapitalista en el país, que desde hace 4 meses está a la cabeza de los políticos con mayor imagen positiva y que las encuestas le asignan una intención de votos del orden del 10%.


Desde aquella primera convocatoria a hoy fueron más de 350 organizaciones sociales, sindicales, políticas, y muchos grupos con distintas identidades (jubilados, ambientalistas, feministas, en defensa de las libertades democráticas, originarios, artistas y científicos…), que se sumaron a la convocatoria, cuya organización tuvo dos puntos culminantes. Una primera reunión, transformada en Asamblea, que se definió como Autoconvocatoria y luego una Asamblea a cielo abierto en Parque Lezama que definió el itinerario de la marcha, de Plaza Congreso a Plaza de Mayo, y sus objetivos. Entre esas reuniones hubo dos virtuales que conectaron organizaciones de todo el país. Así la Autoconvocatoria rápidamente se federalizó y tuvo sus réplicas (desiguales en cuanto a la cantidad de participantes pero importantes en términos políticos) en más de 50 ciudades de casi todas las provincias del país.

title: Auftakt Protestwelle gegen die Animal Messe Stuttgart
content:
Ende November findet jährlich die Animal Messe in Stuttgart statt. Dort werden Kamele, Vogelspinnen, Fische und viele weitere Tiere ausgestellt. Kaninchen müssen über Hindernisse springen, Hunde werden zu Tanzshows genötigt und Schlangen müssen sich vom Publikum anfassen lassen. Gemeinsam mit anderen Gruppen des Netzwerk Tierrechte Stuttgart startet unsere OG Stuttgart nun in die zuvor im offenen Brief angekündigte Protestphase.

Das Kollektiv Tierbefreiung Stuttgart demonstrierte am Samstag, den 19.09.2026 vor dem Eingang der Messe Stuttgart. Die Demo war der Beginn einer Protestwelle des Netzwerk Tierrechte Stuttgart, welches ein Zusammenschluss mehrerer Tierrechtsorganisationen ist. Die Aktionen werden bis zum eigentlichen Termin der Animal Messe anhalten und dort ihren Höhepunkt finden [1].

Weitere Protesttermine sind: – Samstag, 10. Oktober 2026 – Samstag, 17. Oktober 2026 – Samstag, 24. Oktober 2026 – Dienstag, 10. November 2026 – Protestwochenende vom 20. November bis 22. November 2026.

Seit Juli finden in Stuttgart verschiedene Aktionen für die Abschaffung der Animal Messe statt, getragen von mehreren aktivistischen Tierrechtsgruppen. Am Wochenende der Messe (20. bis 22. November 2026) ist eine große Demo und Programm geplant.

„Seit 1995 findet die Animal Messe statt, dort werden Kamele, Vogelspinnen, Fische und viele weitere Tiere unter grausamsten Bedingungen ausgestellt. Kaninchen müssen über Hindernisse springen, Hunde werden zu Tanzshows genötigt und Schlangen müssen sich vom Publikum anfassen lassen.“ so Emilia Schüler, Pressesprecherin des Kollektivs Tierbefreiung Stuttgart. „Es wird Zeit, dass die Landesmesse im aktuellen Jahrzehnt ankommt und dieser unnötigen Tierquälerei ein Ende setzt.“

Das Kollektiv Tierbefreiung hat die Landesmesse GmbH mit einem offenen Brief im Mai 2026 aufgefordert, dem Weltweihnachtscircus zu folgen und keine Tierschauen, Wettkämpfe und generell keine Tiere als Teil von Messen in Ihren Hallen mehr zuzulassen [2, 3]. Daraufhin gab es ein Gespräch zwischen Mitgliedern der Geschäftsleitung der Messe und Aktivist:innen des Kollektivs Tierbefreiung. Die Messe zeigte sich vorerst uneinsichtig und verweist auf deren „Animal Kodex“ [4]. Dieser widerspricht sich selbst da das „Wohl der Tiere“ nicht im „Mittelpunkt“ stehen kann, solange dort Vogelspinnen in winzigen Boxen gezwängt werden und Fluchttiere wie Pferde und Alpakas in lauten Hallen ausharren müssen. Das hier offiziellen Leitlinien gefolgt wird, ist kein Argument, sondern ein Armutszeugnis.

Außerdem verleiten Veranstaltungen wie diese Menschen dazu, zu glauben, dass Tiere und auch Wildtiere wie Reptilien Konsumgüter sind. Es verleitet sie weiterhin dazu Tiere bei Züchtern zu kaufen, während allein in deutschen Tierheimen Tausende Tiere auf ein neues Zuhause warten.

Die Pressemitteilung und weitere Fotos sind hier zu finden.

[1] https://tierbefreiung-stuttgart.org/animal-messe/

[2] https://www.stuttgarter-zeitung.de/lokales/stuttgart/weltweihnachtscircus-in-stuttgart-keine-tiere-mehr-zirkuslegende-will-auf-den-willen-des-publikums-hoeren-78978083.html

[3] https://tierbefreiung-stuttgart.org/Presse/2026/offener-brief-animal-messe/

[4] https://www.messe-stuttgart.de/animal/messe/unser-kodex/animal-kodex/
