title: Suspected death in Eskişehir prison
content:
According to information provided by Çiçek’s family, Şiyar Çiçek, who was being held in Eskişehir Prison, died under suspicious circumstances. Çiçek had been in prison since 2014, and had been held in Eskişehir Prison for approximately two years. He was allegedly kept in a cell for the past 10 days.


According to a report published by Ajansa Welat, Çiçek’s family said that his health was good and that he only had diabetes. Çiçek’s father, Menduh Çiçek, said that his son had died in prison, and added: “On Monday they called us and said ‘Your son is sick, we are taking him to the hospital.’ My son only had diabetes, he was in very good condition, but he died.”


We don't know what happened to my son


Çiçek's father said that he had seen his son’s body and found no signs of torture, but that they had suspicions about the cause of death. He added: “We think they poisoned my son or did something else to him.”


Çiçek said that his son had spoken to his mother by phone about a week before his death and told her that he had been placed in a cell. He continued: “My son had been in a cell for 10 days. If he had been in the ward, we could have found out what happened. But because he was in a cell, we don’t know what happened to him.”


Çiçek said that his son had wanted to go to the hospital with his brother but was not allowed to do so, and added: “They had blindfolded my son. The prosecutor’s office knew that my son had died. But they did this to shift the responsibility onto the hospital. They recorded my son’s death as having occurred at the hospital, whereas he died in prison.”

author: EDRi
title: Serbia’s spyware scandal is also the EU’s problem
content:
At least 14 people in Serbia have been targeted with spyware since the beginning of 2026, according to new findings by EDRi member SHARE Foundation. The targets include members of the student movement, activists, a member of parliament from the opposition party and a local councillor. These findings comecame to light amid growing pressure on Serbia’s pro-democracy movement. The EU’s failure to address spyware at home undermines its credibility in demanding accountability from Serbia.

By EDRi, SHARE Foundation (guest author) · September 23, 2026

On 15 September, thousands of people joined Serbia’s student movement in Belgrade for what organisers called the “Victors’ March”, as the movement formally registered to participate in the country’s upcoming parliamentary elections scheduled for late October. The march marked a new phase in the mobilisation that has brought students to the centre of Serbia’s political opposition after months of protests demanding accountability, democratic reforms and early elections.

After almost two years of protests in the streets, the students are now moving into institutional politics, and polls show that they stand a chance against the current ruling party, Aleksandar Vucic’s SNS. However, two weeks before the elections were called, a scandal shook the public opinion in the country and abroad: many members from the student movement had been targeted by Serbian authorities with spyware.

In August 2026, 12 people contacted SHARE Foundation’s digital forensics experts after receiving Apple threat notifications warning that they had been targeted with “mercenary spyware”, that is, spyware developed by private companies. SHARE’s forensic analysis later confirmed two additional infections with a new version of NoviSpy, the Android spyware first identified in Serbia in 2024. Citizen Lab and Amnesty International’s Security Lab independently confirmed SHARE’s findings.

Citizen Lab confirmed that the phone of a student movement activist was infected with Pegasus, a spyware developed by NSO Group. The device was compromised through a zero-click exploit targeting iMessage, meaning that the victim did not need to click a link or take any action for the attack to succeed.

Amnesty International confirmed another infection with the new version of NoviSpy. In this case, the phone had previously been confiscated when its owner was brought in for police questioning. The spyware was installed while the device was in the hands of Serbian authorities.

In another case demonstrating the clear connection of Serbian authorities to the targeting, the same spyware was detected on a different device after private Viber messages from the phone were disclosed live on Serbian state-aligned television channel “Informer”. Further forensic analysis is ongoing.

These cases add to evidence of the use of spyware against journalists, activists and members of civil society in Serbia. In late 2024, Amnesty International and SHARE Foundation documented NoviSpy on devices belonging to people who had been subjected to police questioning. Researchers found that the spyware was configured to send data extracted from infected phones to a server whose IP address belonged to Serbia’s Security Information Agency (BIA). The spyware had been installed after devices were confiscated, using Cellebrite, a digital forensics tool available to Serbian authorities. In March 2025, Amnesty International also documented that two journalists had been targeted with Pegasus.

At the time, EDRi and 60 other civil society organisations called on EU institutions to demand an investigation into the cases, ensure remedies for victims and address the use of spyware by Serbian authorities.

Two years later, the same concerns remain, while the number of documented targets has increased and new spyware has been identified.

The Serbian case is a clear example of how spyware does not operate in a vacuum. The timing of an attack and the people targeted are essential to understanding the reason behind it, and it usually fits a wider pattern of authoritarianism and repression against political opponents or civic space. Spyware is one more tool in the authorities’ arsenal for undermining democratic life, but a particularly powerful one.

The targets identified by SHARE include students, activists and opposition politicians, most of them actively involved in the local elections in May 2026. Access to their phones can expose their communications, contacts …

author: Unknown
title: 5e Assemblée Anticarcérale Paname & Environs : 27 septembre au DOC !
content:
La cinquième Assemblée Anticarcérale Paname & Environs aura lieu le dimanche 27 Septembre au

DOC

 (26 Rue du Docteur Potain à Paris). Le lieu sera ouvert dès 14h pour s'installer, écrire ensemble des lettres à des prisonnier·es ou parcourir l'infokiosque, et l'assemblée même commencera à 14h30. On conseille d'essayer autant que possible de venir sans téléphone (ou au pire, de l'éteindre en avance) pour réduire la surveillance que l'on s'impose à travers l'omniprésence des mouchards technologiques dans nos milieux. Il y aura aussi un coin et des activités pour les enfants, pour permettre aux personnes qui ont des enfants de pouvoir participer à l'assemblée.


L'assemblée anti carcérale paris & environs a pour vocation d'être un espace d'organisation ouvert se réunissant mensuellement afin d'agir collectivement en solidarité avec les mouvements des prisonnier.es et tisser des liens avec les prisonnier.es et leurs proches sans passer par des cadres partisans ou syndicaux.


Lors des dernières grosses révoltes qui ont eu lieu, la réalité sociale de la répression nous a laissé-es face à un constat amer : nous sommes bien loin d'avoir les outils nécessaires pour réagir correctement face à l'appareil d'État, ainsi qu'amplifier la voix des prisonnier·ères et de celleux qui font les frais du système carcéral.


Pourtant, les mouvements ne manquent pas d'inventivité pour s'opposer de front aux prisons, que ce soit par des actions telles que l'attaque de la prison de Fresnes lors des révoltes de 2023, les attaques répétées de comicos dans cette même révolte comme lors des gilets jaunes, ou encore les attaques et intimidations de matons à domicile comme lors de

DDPF

.


Nous voulons nous en inspirer pour pousser nos luttes anti-carcérales plus loin, à la fois pour dépasser nos milieux anarchistes et adopter une position qui ne soit pas simplement défensive, en simple réaction à la répression.


La prison est — et sera toujours — l'un des symbole les plus éloquents de la puissance de l'État, de sa capacité à réprimer, enfermer et isoler l'ensemble des individu·es qui menacent son existence. La prison est au centre même de l'appareil colonial qui constitue l'État français : elle sert à mater et punir les révoltes des colonies comme récemment en Kanaky, Guadeloupe ou Martinique, à intensifier le tri aux frontières comme à Mayotte, et à tracer des frontières intérieures en incarcérant massivement les populations racisées, colonisées et les plus pauvres.


Attaquer les lieux d'incarcération - par les mots, la solidarité, le feu ou la bombe - c'est alors s'attaquer à ses outils privilégiés.


Rompre l'isolement des/avec les détenu·es est alors devenu rapidement pour les mouvements anticarcéraux un moyen d'affaiblir l'appareil carcéral et l'État colonial. En exposant la voix des personnes enfermé·es, on se donne le moyen de penser «

 

la prison

 

» (son fonctionnement, ses outils, etc.), mais aussi de la rendre moins «

 

extérieure à nos vies

 

». Des surgissements tels que

DDPF

 ou les révoltes pour Nahel parviennent à la remettre au centre de l'attention en s'y attaquant ouvertement, créant des fissures dans lesquelles nous désirons nous engouffrer pour mettre fin à la trop commune realité de l'incarcération et des assassinats policiers.


Une des prouesse des États dits «

 

démocratiques

 

», est d'avoir réussi à faire de la notion d'enfermement un impensé pour toute une partie de la population. Une situation si lointaine que l'on ne prend même pas la peine de l'envisager, alors que c'est pourtant le quotidien de beaucoup de personnes...


Cette nécessité de destruction est d'autant plus présente dans une région parisienne qui concentre à elle seule une densité collossale d'institutions d'enfermements : que ce soit les taules, tribunaux, comicos, ou prisons pour sans-papiers, mineur-es, enfants, fols, tox, handi-es, animaux non-humains...


Pour nous, s'organiser signifie construire des nouvelles formes de lutte, de solidarité et de décision, par notre capacité collective à rompre avec l'ordre existant, à expérimenter, à créer, à inventer...


Depuis le début du 20

e

 siècle, les Anarchist Black Cross (

ABC

) et leurs réseaux ont cet avantage de se présenter sous une forme autonome et souple, fondée sur un internationalisme radicalement anti-carcéral, d'où notre envie de nous réaproprier cette forme et de s'inscrire dans un réseau pour abattre les prisons proches de chez nous comme à l'autre bout du monde …

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Impunity persists 54 years after martial law imposition
content:
Symbolic paper cranes were attached in a steel frame, holding the calls for the freedom of all political prisoners. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

“More than five decades have passed yet the painful legacy of martial law—human rights violations, injustice and lack of accountability—remains deeply entrenched.”

Fifty-four years after the declaration of martial law under the Marcos Sr. dictatorship, political prisoners stressed that abuses continue through corruption and the use of state institutions and laws against dissent.

The warning came from political prisoners detained at the Metro Manila District Jail Annex 4 in Bicutan. They issued a statement through KAPATID ahead of the September 21 commemoration of martial law.

Their statement came days after the Supreme Court overturned former First Lady Imelda Marcos’ 2018 Sandiganbayan conviction on seven counts of graft involving her alleged financial interests in private foundations in Switzerland.

The Supreme Court, in a decision dated June 10 but made public on September 9, acquitted Marcos after finding that prosecutors failed to establish her guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The court cited, among other issues, the failure to properly authenticate key Swiss documents and to establish that the foundations were “businesses” covered by the anti-graft law.

The ruling reversed the Sandiganbayan’s 2018 decision which sentenced Marcos from six to 11 years in prison for each of the seven graft counts. The Supreme Court clarified that its decision concerned her criminal liability and did not determine whether assets involved in separate civil forfeiture cases constituted ill-gotten wealth.

For the political prisoners, the development underscores the continuing struggle over accountability and the historical legacy of martial law. “More than five decades have passed yet the painful legacy of martial law—human rights violations, injustice and lack of accountability—remains deeply entrenched.”

Some of those detained in Bicutan are veteran activists already involved in political struggles before martial law was declared on September 21, 1972.

They said that commemorating martial law should not be limited to remembering the abuses committed during the dictatorship. It should also involve examining the conditions that allowed authoritarian rule to emerge and the conditions that, they said, continue to enable corruption and impunity.

In their analysis, political and economic power remains concentrated among entrenched interests, allowing state institutions to be used to protect political and economic power. “As long as the three scourges of imperialism, feudalism, and bureaucrat capitalism remain as leeches clinging to the country’s political and social institutions, the danger of the reemergence of an even more ferocious fascist dictatorship and martial law will persist.”

The statement also linked the return of the Marcos family to national political power with the continuing contest over the historical narrative of martial law.

The Marcos Jr. administration has faced criticism from activist and human rights groups over its handling of human rights issues and its approach to historical narratives surrounding the Marcos dictatorship. Meanwhile, Marcos Jr. welcomed the Supreme Court ruling acquitting his mother. He said that he was happy that the decades-old case had been resolved.

For the political prisoners, repression cannot be understood only through the existence of an openly authoritarian government.

They said that institutions associated with democratic governance, including Congress, courts, laws, prisons, police and the military can also be used to suppress dissent. “We, political prisoners, are victims of political persecution. We are living witnesses to how laws and courts are weaponized and wielded to suppress our rights and imprison us on the basis of fabricated charges.”

They said that political prisoners face multiple criminal cases, violations of civil and political rights, and prolonged detention while awaiting trial. They pointed to the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020 and the Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act of 2012 which they said have been used against activists and progressive organizations critical of the government.

The government, however, has claimed that anti-terrorism measures are intended to address threats to national security and terrorism even if the Anti-Terrorism Act was challenged before the Supreme Court over …

author: anonerror
title: [Huelga de presxs EEUU] Diez años de #PrisonStrike: la visión de Industrial Worker
content:
En septiembre de 2016, decenas de miles de personas presas participaron o se vieron afectadas por una movilización que alcanzó al menos 46 centros penitenciarios de Estados Unidos. Diez años después, sus protagonistas recuerdan una experiencia de organización que consiguió atravesar divisiones raciales, territoriales y entre diferentes grupos dentro de las prisiones, y que puso sobre la mesa una cuestión todavía abierta: el trabajo penitenciario y la explotación de la población encarcelada.


9 de septiembre de 2016


En la Institución Correccional Franklin, situada en Carrabelle, Florida, aquel día comenzó de una manera poco habitual. Las personas presas se negaron a acudir al trabajo. Tampoco fueron al comedor ni al economato. Robert Powell, que se encontraba encarcelado allí y participó en la organización de la protesta, recuerda que la dirección de la prisión había preparado para aquel día un menú extraordinario, con alimentos que los presos no habían visto anteriormente y que tampoco volverían a encontrar después. Powell interpretó aquella decisión como un intento de romper el paro y convencer a los presos para que acudieran al comedor. Pero los organizadores se habían preparado. Una semana antes habían comprado suficientes alimentos en el economato para repartirlos entre toda su sección de la prisión. De esa forma podían mantener el boicot sin depender de la comida ofrecida por la institución. Aunque habían tenido poco tiempo para organizarse, la acción consiguió alterar seriamente el funcionamiento habitual de Franklin. Lo que estaba sucediendo allí, sin embargo, era solamente una pequeña parte de algo mucho mayor.


Una movilización que atravesó las cárceles estadounidenses


La protesta del

9 de septiembre de 2016

 se convirtió en la primera huelga penitenciaria coordinada a escala nacional en Estados Unidos. Las estimaciones recopiladas posteriormente sitúan entre

20.000 y 60.000

 el número de personas presas que participaron directamente o resultaron afectadas por las movilizaciones, que alcanzaron

al menos 46 instituciones penitenciarias

. La fecha había sido escogida deliberadamente. El 9 de septiembre de 1971 había comenzado la rebelión de la prisión de Attica, en el estado de Nueva York, uno de los acontecimientos fundamentales de la historia de las luchas penitenciarias estadounidenses. Cuarenta y cinco años después, presos de diferentes estados recuperaban aquella fecha para lanzar una nueva movilización. El planteamiento era sencillo y al mismo tiempo difícil de ejecutar: detener el trabajo y alterar el funcionamiento de las prisiones.


Contra la «esclavitud penitenciaria»


Kevin «Rashid» Johnson fue uno de los presos que contribuyeron a organizar y difundir la movilización desde la William P. Clements Unit, en Amarillo, Texas. Johnson definió aquella protesta como una huelga contra lo que los activistas denominaban

«esclavitud penitenciaria»

. Para sus organizadores, la cuestión no podía reducirse únicamente a los salarios extremadamente bajos —o directamente inexistentes— que reciben muchas personas encarceladas. Establecían una relación histórica entre el actual sistema penitenciario estadounidense y las estructuras de explotación surgidas después de la abolición formal de la esclavitud tras la Guerra Civil. Jason Renard Walker, también encarcelado en Clements en 2016, plantea una interpretación todavía más amplia: hablar de esclavitud penitenciaria significa hablar del trabajo involuntario, pero también de las condiciones de vida, la ausencia de derechos, los mecanismos disciplinarios y el enorme poder que las instituciones penitenciarias ejercen sobre quienes se encuentran bajo su control. La huelga pretendía utilizar uno de los pocos instrumentos colectivos disponibles dentro de las prisiones:

retirar el trabajo necesario para mantenerlas funcionando

.


Parar una prisión


Una huelga laboral puede conseguir rápidamente la atención de una administración penitenciaria, pero existe un problema evidente: no todas las personas presas tienen un empleo. Además, en algunas instituciones la respuesta ante una movilización consiste precisamente en decretar el confinamiento de la población reclusa. Eso ocurrió en Clements. El cierre de la prisión impidió desarrollar algunas de las acciones previstas, como el boicot al economato. De aquella experiencia surgieron debates sobre otras formas de resistencia, desde las huelgas de hambre hasta los boicots colectivos o la creación de redes de …

author: Access Now
title: From surveillance to governance: recentering human rights in the UN AI agenda
content:
September 21


				 @


				9:00 am


					 –


					10:30 am


EDT


Hybrid side event during UNGA81 High-Level Week


In-person attendance available upon request: email

un@accessnow.org


join the livestream


 Add to Calendar


 Google


 Apple


 Outlook 365


 Outlook Live


Panelists:


Louise Lund Henneberg

, Acting Director/Techplomacy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Denmark


Wafa Ben Hassine

, Chief, Digital Technology and Human Rights Section, Rule of Law, Accountability and Civic Space, Oﬀice of the High Commissioner for Human Rights


Beatriz Busaniche

, Executive Director, Fundación Vía Libre


Luda Svystunova

, Head of Social Research, Amundi


Welcoming remarks:

Irina Schoulgin-Nyoni, Ambassador for Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Sweden

Moderator:

 Alejandro Mayoral Baños, Co-Executive Director, Access Now


During the first session of the Global Dialogue on AI Governance, governments and stakeholders convened to have open, transparent and inclusive discussions on artificial intelligence governance. We now gather experts across the spectrum of stakeholders during UNGA81 to reaffirm that human rights should be the stepping stone of this process, instead of an afterthought.


None of this is irreversible, but the security issues associated with advanced AI tools are the consequences of deliberately prioritizing profit and competitiveness over the security and safety of at-risk communities, and they will not resolve on their own. Unbridled AI adoption combined with unacceptably lax corporate security practices demands urgent intervention at all levels, starting from putting human rights back at the center of digital governance mechanisms.


This discussion has the objective to explore concrete, actionable ways in which each stakeholder can contribute to oppose the normalization of surveillance. Experts will also discuss how to chart a way forward to reaffirm digital rights as the natural first line of defense against the abuses of AI technologies.

From surveillance to governance: recentering human rights in the UN AI agenda

content:

author: rezgar2
title: The silent bomb: AI and the dismantling of the human mind
content:
Rezgar Akrawi: What confronts us today is not a technological fate written in advance. It is the product of political and economic choices that serve the interests of capital. It can be confronted, difficult though that may be. Bringing AI under control, regulating algorithms and subjecting them to democratic oversight is a collective responsibility. It will require left, progressive and rights-based work and organisation on a global scale to make digital applications auxiliary tools serving the human mind rather than a substitute for it. This must be combined with advancing communal and participatory digital alternatives that restore people's capacity for independent thought and collective action.

To achieve this, work is needed to place data infrastructure under public interest, democratic administration and social accountability. To turn algorithms from closed "black boxes" into open-source software open to collective review and independent audit. To impose transparency in the design of models and in the sources of the data on which they are trained. And to support cooperative digital alternatives owned by their users and creators. This technology should be directed toward serving the needs of society, and contribute to the distribution of wealth, the organisation of production, the treatment of disease, the fight against poverty and the achievement of social justice.

Without such mechanisms, calls for laws, oversight and regulation remain general and inadequate, and technology stays hostage to a handful of capitalist monopoly corporations and major powers. Through social ownership, accountability and cooperative alternatives, it becomes possible to wrest AI from the logic of monopoly and profit and turn it into a common good where AI serves humanity's liberation, rather than being an instrument for humanity's enslavement.

We are not witnessing a takeover by robots of the kind imagined in countless films. We face a different model of digital control, built on automation and the deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) and algorithms to manage ever larger parts of daily life, leaving societies further subject to systems, corporations and intelligent machines.

Losing control of these systems, however, is just the tip of the iceberg in terms of the danger. That tip is developing fast under the pressure of competition between major powers and capitalist monopoly corporations — faster than laws, societies and educational institutions can keep up with. But the danger does not stop there, as these systems are being developed inside relations of ownership and fierce capitalist competition. That graver danger is harder to see. Under capitalism, AI is used to shape the consciousness of billions, steering their attention and behaviour to serve the capitalist model's logic. Competition between digital capitalist monopolies and major powers, in the absence of effective constraints and laws, may inflict the gravest damage on the human mind, turning AI into a weapon of mass destruction if its development and deployment continues at this excessive pace and without adequate safeguards.

These concerns no longer come from critics alone. On several occasions — among them the case revealed by TIME — AI systems have slipped out of control and attacked other systems. In response, about 1400 engineers at major AI companies signed a petition calling for technical tools and international governance mechanisms to regulate the pace of AI development. That petition was no isolated case. The International AI Safety Report, prepared by more than 100 experts with the backing of more than 30 states and international organisations, warned models have begun to distinguish between the testing environment and real-world use, and to circumvent evaluation mechanisms, allowing dangerous capabilities to pass undetected. It warned AI agents raise the level of risk because they act independently, which makes human intervention difficult before harm occurs. There are serious risks that AI systems will develop themselves, slip out of control and come to play a larger part in managing and controlling human beings than planned.

Tens of thousands of people, among them leading scientists, have signed an international statement demanding a ban on the development of "superintelligence" until there is scientific consensus it can be achieved safely and under control. Researchers at major digital corporations have resigned in protest at the course of AI …

author: Alexandra Martinez
title: A New Campaign Is Pushing Ulta Beauty to Drop Flock Cameras From Its Stores
content:
A petition demanding the removal of the surveillance cameras has more than 15,000 signatories.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A national gender justice organization is escalating a campaign against Ulta Beauty over the cosmetics retailer’s use of automated license-plate reader (ALPR) cameras made by the surveillance company Flock Safety, arguing that it threatens customer privacy and could disproportionately harm women and gender-expansive people.

UltraViolet, a women-led gender justice organization, launched its “Drop Flock” campaign this month, calling on Ulta Beauty to terminate contracts with Flock Safety and other mass surveillance companies. The organization said its petition had surpassed 15,000 signatures as of Sept. 8.

“Ulta Beauty has built a multibillion-dollar business on women’s trust,” UltraViolet Campaign Director Jenna Sherman said in a statement accompanying the campaign’s launch. “Putting Flock, an invasive mass surveillance system, right outside its stores without customer knowledge or consent is a direct violation of that trust.”

When asked about the campaign’s privacy and gender justice concerns, a Flock spokesperson pointed to the company’s public media FAQ page outlining its data retention policies and security safeguards. According to the FAQ page, cameras collect vehicle and license-plate data for law enforcement investigations with access and retention controlled by the agencies that use the system. Flock’s website says the company does not sell the data or use facial recognition. Ulta Beauty did not respond to Prism’s request for comment.

The campaign grew out of UltraViolet’s broader work examining the intersection of technology, privacy, and gender-based violence. Sherman said the organization has spent years tracking technologies that can be used to surveil, stalk, or harass women and gender-expansive people, including facial recognition, connected vehicles, location tracking, and other emerging technologies.

UltraViolet became more directly involved in the campaign against Flock Safety after working with Fight for the Future, a digital rights organization that has organized campaigns against Flock’s contracts with major retailers and local governments.

Flock Safety manufactures ALPR cameras that capture license-plate information and other visual details around vehicles. The company has built a large network of cameras used by law enforcement agencies and private organizations. Flock told Axios in August that its network had grown to more than 120,000 cameras across the country.

UltraViolet’s campaign is part of a national backlash against Flock and other ALPR providers. Local governments across the country have faced pressure to reject or end contracts with surveillance companies, while digital rights and civil liberties groups have increasingly turned their attention toward private companies using similar technology. In Florida, for example, state officials recently moved to restrict ALPR cameras on state roads amid concerns about privacy and misuse.

UltraViolet argues that corporations should face the same scrutiny as government agencies when they deploy surveillance technologies capable of collecting sensitive information about the public.

Sherman said UltraViolet was surprised to discover that Ulta was identified by Flock as a retail partner in the company’s public materials. The organization had already seen strong public engagement around campaigns targeting Flock cameras at Lowe’s hardware stores and decided to bring the issue to Ulta.

“We knew that we owed it to them to campaign specifically about Ulta because it is a company with a majority-women shopper base,” Sherman told Prism.

Ulta’s privacy policy contains a dedicated section on “Automated License Plate Recognition Usage and Privacy Policy.”

The policy states that Ulta uses ALPR systems where they are not prohibited by law and that the systems are used for the security of its premises, employees, guests, and assets. It also says information from those systems can be disclosed to third parties, including law enforcement, for specified purposes such as safety, protecting property, and complying with the law.

Sherman argued that the larger concern is the normalization of surveillance technology in everyday spaces. Unlike conventional security cameras, ALPR systems can automatically collect …

author: Unknown
title: LGBTİ+ hesaplarıyla başlayan sansür dalgası Evrensel, Af Örgütü, MLSA ve Barış Akademisyenleri’ne uzandı
content:
Hafta sonu LGBTİ+ örgütleri, aktivistler ve hak savunucularının sosyal medya hesaplarına yönelik erişim engellerinin ardından bugün çok sayıda X ve Instagram hesabı hakkında yeni erişim engeli kararları alındı.


Evrensel Gazetesi, Uluslararası Af Örgütü Türkiye, Barış Akademisyenleri ve Medya ve Hukuk Çalışmaları Derneği (MLSA) de engellenen hesaplar arasında.


İfade Özgürlüğü Derneği’nin (İFÖD) EngelliWeb projesi, bugün yaptığı açıklamada çok sayıda X ve Instagram hesabına erişim engeli getirildiğini duyurdu.


EngelliWeb, “Bugün de aralarında Evrensel Gazetesi, Uluslararası Af Örgütü Türkiye, Barış Akademisyenleri ve Medya ve Hukuk Çalışmaları Derneği'nin (MLSA) hesaplarının da bulunduğu çok sayıda X ve Instagram hesabı erişime engellendi. Hesapların bazıları Türkiye'den görünmez kılındı” açıklamasını yaptı.


X, MLSA, Af Örgütü ve Barış Akademisyenleri hesaplarını görünmez kıldı


İFÖD kurucularından Prof. Dr. Yaman Akdeniz de erişim engellerinin uygulanmaya başladığını belirterek MLSA ve Uluslararası Af Örgütü Türkiye’nin X hesaplarının Türkiye’den görünmez kılındığını açıkladı.


Akdeniz, daha sonra Barış Akademisyenleri hesabının da aynı şekilde engellendiğini duyurdu:


“Evrensel Gazetesi, Uluslararası Af Örgütü Türkiye, Barış Akademisyenleri ve Medya ve Hukuk Çalışmaları Derneği'nin (MLSA) hesapları erişime engellendi. MLSA ve Af Örgütü hesapları jet hızıyla X tarafından Türkiye'den görünmez kılındı. Sansür ve susturma operasyonu genişleyerek devam ediyor. An itibarıyla Barış Akademisyenleri’nin hesabı da Türkiye'den görünmez kılındı.”


Evrensel: Erişim şimdilik sürüyor


Evrensel Gazetesi Genel Yayın Yönetmeni Hakkı Özdal ise Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığının gazetenin X hesabının erişime engellenmesini istediğini, bu talebin X tarafından gazeteye bildirildiğini açıkladı.


Özdal, hesabın henüz Türkiye’den erişime kapatılmadığını belirterek şunları söyledi:


“Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığının, gazetemizin X/Twitter hesabının erişime engellenmesini istediğini, ilgili şirket bize de bildirdi. Şimdilik Evrensel hesabına yurt içinden erişim sürüyor. Ancak sansürün fiilen de hayata geçmesi durumunda yeni hesaplarımızı duyuracağız.”


Hafta sonu LGBTİ+ örgütleri ve aktivistlerin hesapları engellendi


Yeni kararlar, hafta sonu LGBTİ+ örgütleri, aktivistler ve hak savunucularına yönelik operasyonlarla eş zamanlı uygulanan internet sansürünün ardından geldi.


İstanbul 7. Sulh Ceza Hâkimliği, 12 Eylül tarihli ve 2026/9559 sayılı kararıyla KaosGL Derneği’nin “kaosgldernegi.org” ve Velvele’nin “velvele.net” internet siteleri ile çok sayıda LGBTİ+ örgütü ve aktivistin sosyal medya hesaplarına erişim engeli getirdi.


Karar kapsamında aralarında KaosGL, Velvele, Özgür Renkler Derneği, Queer Adana, Cinsel Şiddetle Mücadele Derneği, İnter Dayanışma, İzmir LGBTİ+ Onur Haftası ve LİSTAG’ın da bulunduğu hesapların yanı sıra aktivistlerin kişisel hesapları hedef alındı.


Toplam 14 X hesabı platform tarafından Türkiye’den görünmez kılındı. Seyhan Arman, SPoD, Pembe Hayat Derneği, Boğaziçi Üniversitesi LGBTİA+ Kulübü, 17 Mayıs Derneği, Yıldız Tar, Hacettepe Kuir Araştırmaları, Enes Hocaoğulları, HEVİ LGBTİ+ Derneği, Bilkent Üniversitesi LGBTİQA+ Öğrenci Topluluğu ve İÜ Radar’a ait 11 Instagram hesabı hakkında da erişim engeli kararı verildi. Bu hesaplara yönelik karar ise açıklamanın yapıldığı sırada Instagram tarafından uygulanmamıştı.


(HA)

Πρόκειται για μια αντιφασιστική, αντιρατσιστική, αντισεξιστική και αντιμιλιταριστική οργάνωση που αντιτίθεται στον καπιταλισμό και τον αυταρχισμό και φιλοξενεί μόνο όσους συμμερίζονται αυτές τις αρχές και που φιλοξενεί 16.000 mails, 1.500 ιστότοπους, 5.500 λίστες αλληλογραφίας και 10.000 ιστολόγια.

Το δηλωμένο μοντέλο είναι ριζικά διαφορετικό από αυτό των μεγάλων εμπορικών πλατφορμών. Καμία διαφήμιση, καμία πώληση προσωπικών δεδομένων, καμία αποζημίωση για εθελοντές. ιλοξενεί

author: Jian Zharese Joies Sanz
title: Tech professionals warn of privacy risks in proposed ID rule for Meta users
content:
MANILA – The Computer Professionals’ Union (CPU) sounded the alarm over the Department of Information and Communications Technology’s (DICT) proposal to require social media users to have the Philippine National ID.

The DICT claimed that the proposal would be the ‘safest’ way of verifying age of social media users, following the government’s statement blaming social media and online games for the series of school shootings in the country.

The CPU, however, maintained that the proposal is alarming and profoundly intrusive to Filipino citizens’ digital rights. “Rather than fostering a safe online environment, this draconian measure represents a clear and direct attack on the basic human right to privacy without any legitimate grounds that it will protect us from crime, or protect our youth from the culture of violence,” the union said.

Beyond possible violations of citizens’ privacy, the CPU said the rule strips away the right to anonymity, threatens free expression, and can become a dangerous tool for mass surveillance.

The group pointed out that the SIM Registration Law did not address the incidence of cybercrime after it was enacted into law under Ferdinand Marcos Jr’ s administration.

Despite the law’s promise to stop cybercrime and scams, reports of digital crimes have reportedly tripled in 2024, according to the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC). In an online article, the CICC recorded more than 10,004 cybercrime complaints in 2024 and P198 million ($3.16 million) in monetary losses from these incidents.

The CPU asserted that the proposal will also not solve the issues of online exploitation or youth violence. According to them, the real solution is a better system—accessible mental health services, comprehensive digital literacy programs integrated into educational systems, and stricter gun control measures to prevent real-world violence. (AMU, RVO)

author: C4SS
title: An Attack on Tech Freedom, an Assault on Dissent
content:
We live in a world of

surveillance states

,

militarized police

, and

crackdowns


on


dissent

. Meanwhile, corporate behemoths will often ally with the state to

shut down dissident speech

 or aid and abet

surveillance

. 


In this context, it’s important for independent groups to develop and maintain encrypted communications platforms and independent web hosting.


But the Trump administration recently

declared

 that an Italian tech collective is a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist” for doing exactly this. That Italian tech collective is Autistici/Inventati, which operates the independent web hosting service

NoBlogs

 along with other digital infrastructure projects for activists.


The State Department

claims

 that “Autistici/Inventati (A/I Collective) is an Italy-based extremist group that builds and operates the digital infrastructure for violent Antifa cells and other far-left militants across the world.”


That emphasis on

Antifa cells

 reflects the Trump administration’s ongoing attempt to crack down on dissent by demonizing “Antifa.” This has been the explicit aim of

NSPM-7

, and it has been central to prosecutions of anti-ICE activists, including the

Minneapolis 15

 and the

Prairieland defendants

.


In their obsessive desire to tie all leftist and anarchist dissent to “Antifa,” the Trump administration has made blatantly false claims. The State Department asserts: 


Oregon-based Rose City Antifa has relied on A/I Collective tools and services to organize and incite violent and criminal acts domestically, including an attack on Customs and Border Patrol helicopters that led to a federal indictment. Rose City Antifa also used A/I Collective tools and services to disseminate doxing lists and release illegally obtained personal information of Federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement, along with calls for targeted attacks on ICE agents in the streets and “in their homes.” 


However, as Torch Antifa Network

points out

, Rose City Antifa does not use A/I services and did not carry out these actions. Federal officials are instead referring to communications by Rose City Counter-Info, an entirely different group that does use A/I services. “Rose City” is a common nickname for Portland, Oregon. Not all groups that use this phrase in their name are identical. These outright falsehoods were credulously amplified by reporters at

Fox News

 and the

National Review

. 


Yet despite the incompetence this shows, designating A/I Collective as a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist” poses a very serious threat. As C4SS’s Technical Coordinator William Gillis

put it

, “This is a HUGE attack on basic free speech. Words completely fail me when addressing the potential loss to the anarchist movement of — as the US names it — 5,500 mailing lists, and 10,000 blogs.”


The State Department emphasizes users of the A/I Collective’s services that have allegedly committed crimes, including sabotage and terrorism. But many users are engaged in clearly First Amendment protected activities. These include anarchist bookfairs, antifascist researchers who study and expose far-right groups, the blog of a peer-reviewed academic journal, and an anarchist podcast and radio show. 


The “Specially Designated Global Terrorist” classification subjects Autistici/Inventati to sanctions. This means that purely based on a decree from the U.S. executive branch, anyone who engages in transactions with the A/I Collective becomes vulnerable to legal reprisal. As a result, the collective’s website has been

taken down

,

PayPal

 has blocked their account, and the Italian bank

Banca Etica

 plans to close their account. 


These sanctions have had a devastating effect on the A/I Collective. As

Sabot Media

reports

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Rights groups assail military-led symposium redtagging progressives in Tacloban university
content:
Photo taken by an attendee during the symposium (name withheld for security reasons).

By Veronika Barbosa TACLOBAN CITY – Progressive groups in Eastern Visayas raised alarm over a red-tagging incident that happened last September 12, 2026 in a symposium led by the 8th Civil Military Operations “Dangpanan (CMO) Battalion inside the Leyte Normal University in Tacloban.

The attendees of the said symposium were students enrolled in the National Service Training Program (NSTP) course mostly composed of first-year students.

According to the accounts of some student attendees, an officer of the Armed Forces of the Philippines discouraged them from joining protest actions. “At first, he [the CMO officer] was only talking about the West Philippine Sea, then we were shocked that they started talking about terror grooming and how it is not necessary to criticize the government through mass mobilizations,” said Aya (name withheld for security reasons), an attendee of the symposium. Aya added that the military officer dissuaded them from joining progressive organizations as it is a form of “terrorist recruitment.” “He said that joining rallies and educational discussions talking about socio-political issues are forms of indoctrination which will eventually lead students to being recruited into the communist rebellion,” Aya told Bulatlat in an interview.

“We were shocked and traumatized when they showed us pictures of dead bodies of rebels who they said were recruited by the New People’s Army by joining rallies,” shared Aya. Aya added that the military officer flashed pictures of University of the Philippines students “terror-groomed” by mass organizations. “I was alarmed and disappointed [by the redtagging remarks], especially coming from a military officer who is supposed to serve and protect the people,” she said.

The Association of Political Science Students (APSS) of LNU challenged the university administration to look into the reported incident. “We call for the protection of spaces where students can engage in peaceful political discussion, organization, and mobilization without intimidation and unwarranted labeling,” the group said.

In a statement, Pulso han Mag-aaram Paterno, a political organization in LNU, also expressed their condemnation of the incident. “The AFP is actively endangering the lives of student protesters through this blatant redtagging.” Pulso Paterno argued that even the Supreme Court itself ruled that redtagging directly threatens one’s life, liberty, and security. “Our universities must remain safe havens for critical thought, learning, and the free exchange of ideas, completely insulated from intimidation and harassment,” the group said. Katungod Sinirangan Bisayas, the local chapter of Karapatan, described the incident as a reflection of a “deeply alarming pattern in which state forces militarize education spaces to advance its counterinsurgency narrative, vilify dissent, and instill fear among young people who dare to question corruption, poverty, and injustice.” “The AFP’s presence inside schools must not be normalized…the AFP is not a neutral institution, as it wields enormous power and has supported the interests of those who hold political and economic power in the country,” expounded Katungod.

Last year, youth activist Axell Bergula of Kabataan Partylist and former student of LNU was redtagged and visited by two uniformed police officers inside the university premises.

Read: Tacloban Youth activist harassed after November 30 protest

Read: Youth activist, family harassed anew after filing CHR case vs cops

Last January, the 8th CMO posted a video redtagging journalist Frenchie Mae Cumpio, layworker Marielle Domequil, and Alexander “Chakoy” Abinguna of Tacloban 5.

“The video [of the 8th CMO] maliciously juxtaposes the Tacloban 5 activists with armed rebels and shamelessly instrumentalizes the trumped-up cases that they are facing to “warn” students about the legal consequences of activism,” Katungod SB said.

The Tacloban 5 refers to the five human rights defenders arrested on February 7, 2020 in simultaneous raids in Tacloban City. They have been slapped with fabricated charges. Two of the five have been temporarily released after posting bail. Cumpio and Domequil were acquitted of illegal possession of firearms and explosives but were wrongfully convicted of terror financing charges. Abinguna is facing trumped-up charges of illegal possession of firearms and explosives and murder …

author: Redazione_web
title: Questa non è una guerra
content:
Crosetto annuncia l’invio di navi da guerra nello stretto di Bab El Mandeb, e l’Italia è sempre più coinvolta nella guerra globale. È urgente dare una risposta chiara alle politiche di guerra, contro nuove spedizioni militari e per il ritiro di tutte le missioni all’estero. È difficile in questo momento prevedere cosa succederà nei prossimi giorni e quali fatti effettivamente seguiranno alle dichiarazioni del Ministro della Difesa Crosetto. Certo l’avanzata delle truppe del Consiglio politico supremo Huthi in Yemen ha mutato rapidamente la situazione, facendo emergere le difficoltà e le vulnerabilità dell’Arabia Saudita e dei suoi alleati, tra cui l’Italia.


Non è facile inquadrare la vicenda. Per capire cosa sta succedendo in queste settimane può essere utile riassumere alcuni fatti. In Yemen è in corso una guerra civile dal 2014 quando il Consiglio politico supremo degli Huthi, una forza sciita zaydita che negli anni è stata legata all’Iran, ha conquistato la capitale Sana’a iniziando un lungo conflitto prima contro le forze leali al regime del presidente Hādī, sostenuto da USA e Arabia Saudita, e poi dal 2022 – dopo il fallimento delle trattative di pace in seguito al ritiro di Hādī – contro il Consiglio di Leadership Presidenziale, ancora unico governo yementa riconosciuto dalla cosiddetta comunità internazionale. Nel contesto della guerra di Israele a Gaza dal 2023 e poi nel quadro della guerra con l’Iran condotta da Stati Uniti e Israele a partire dal marzo scorso, gli Huthi sono più volte intervenuti a sostegno dei propri alleati. Negli ultimi mesi lo scontro tra USA e Iran per il controllo dello stretto di Hormuz ha dato una nuova centralità strategica al Mar Rosso e allo stretto di Bab El Mandeb. Dallo scorso marzo infatti l’Arabia Saudita ha deciso di trasferire gran parte del traffico di petrolio sull’oleodotto est-ovest Petroline, che dai giacimenti di Aqbaiq nel Golfo Persico arriva fino al porto di Yanbu sul Mar Rosso, fino ad allora sottoutilizzato, iniziando ad impiegarlo al massimo della sua capacità. Da allora si sono intensificati gli attacchi lungo il tracciato di 1201 km che taglia in due la penisola arabica e ha 13 stazioni di pompaggio. La vulnerabilità dell’infrastruttura a sabotaggi ed attacchi militari si inserisce in un contesto già complesso, infatti, per limiti degli impianti, anche in una situazione di pace questa soluzione non avrebbe comunque reso l’Arabia Saudita in grado di fornire la stessa quantità e qualità di oli che potevano passare via nave attraverso Hormuz, mettendo in discussione il suo ruolo di fornitore globale di petrolio. A partire dal 3 settembre, gli Huthi hanno lanciato un’offensiva assumendo il controllo di quasi tutta la costa occidentale dello Yemen, e quindi di fatto anche dello stretto di Bab El Mandeb, occupando le principali isole di questo strategico braccio di mare. In seguito ad attacchi con droni all’oleodotto, l’Arabia Saudita ha chiuso lo scorso 11 settembre l’intera conduttura per motivi di sicurezza. Nei giorni successivi le forze Huthi sono avanzate ulteriormente in Yemen, mentre sono proseguiti i bombardamenti con droni verso l’Arabia Saudita. In questo contesto si colloca l’annuncio sull’invio di navi da guerra nello stretto di Bab El Mandeb, fatto nel pomeriggio del 17 settembre da Crosetto al Forum Risorsa Mare di La Spezia che ha visto la partecipazione di numerosi esponenti del Governo, delle Forze Armate e delle imprese armatoriali, spedizioniere e portuali. Crosetto ha affermato che l’Italia era pronta ad inviare le navi anche da sola e che la “burocrazia” italiana non si sarebbe sovrapposta a quella europea, facendo chiaramente riferimento a problemi interni alla missione europea Aspides. Poche ore dopo, nella notte tra il 17 e il 18 settembre, le forze armate Houthi hanno colpito la base aerea Re Fahd a Taif, in Arabia Saudita vicino a La Mecca. Uno dei quattro Eurofighter italiani schierati nella base, nel quadro della missione Task Force Air Arabia, è stato distrutto nell’attacco. Stando alle notizie diffuse dalle agenzie, nella base, oltre a militari sauditi, statunitensi e di altri paesi, sarebbero presenti 300 militari italiani. Le truppe italiane sono presenti nell’area da tempo, ma è dalla seconda metà di marzo che è in corso questa missione, che nel complesso prevede lo schieramento di 300 militari, 4 eurofighter, un aereo radar e due aerei da trasporto C-130J. Una missione passata sotto traccia anche grazie alle nuove procedure di …

author: Unknown
title: Iraqi military delegation holds talks in Shengal
content:
A high-ranking Iraqi military delegation led by Chief of Staff Abdul Amir Rashid Yarallah traveled to Shengal on Tuesday. The delegation is expected to meet with representatives of the Yazidi community and military forces present in the region to discuss the security situation and the restructuring of security arrangements.


According to the Iraqi Ministry of Defense, the visit is intended to assess the security situation in Shengal and review the operational readiness of the forces stationed there. Yarallah also heads the high-level security commission established by the government.


The delegation also includes members of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (Hashd al-Shaabi). According to multiple reports, meetings are planned with the military formations active in Shengal, including the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the Shengal Women’s Units (YJŞ). The talks will focus on the future security structure, the handover of weapons, and the integration of members of the units into state institutions.


The visit follows a decision by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi. Following a meeting with Yazidi organizations on September 11, he announced that the resistance units would hand over their weapons to the state. At the same time, he said that eligible members of the YBŞ and YJŞ could be integrated into Iraq’s official security institutions.


Al-Zaidi also ordered the formation of a high-level commission tasked with examining the security and humanitarian situation in Shengal, assessing the needs of the population, and developing proposals for further measures. Its mandate also includes determining the status of members of the resistance units, reconstruction, and creating the conditions necessary for displaced people to return.

title: DEM Parti'den silahsızlanma açıklaması: “Elimizde bir tarih yok”
content:
DEM Parti Sözcüsü Ayşegül Doğan, partisinin haftalık bilgilendirme toplantısında gündeme ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. Doğan, toplantının ardından gazetecilerin sorularını da yanıtladı.

DEM Parti’nin 5’inci Olağan Büyük Kongresi sonrasında gerçekleştirilen Merkez Yürütme Kurulu (MYK) toplantısında ele alınan başlıkları aktaran Doğan, “Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci” olarak ifade ettiği sürece ilişkin de açıklamalarda bulundu.

PKK’nın silah bırakma sürecine ilişkin soruları yanıtlayan Doğan, temasların ve saha çalışmalarının sürdüğünü söyledi.

Doğan, silahsızlanmaya ilişkin karşılıklı çalışmalar yürütüldüğünü ve bunun için oluşturulan mekanizmaların çalıştığını belirterek, “Önümüzdeki günlerde silahsızlanmaya dair önemli gelişmelerin olmasını bekliyoruz.” dedi.

Kamuoyuyla paylaşılabilecek somut gelişmeler ortaya çıktığında bunların açıklanacağını belirten Doğan, silahsızlanmaya ilişkin şu aşamada belirlenmiş bir tarih olmadığını ifade etti.

Doğan, “Silahsızlanmaya dair şu an elimizde bulunan bir tarih yok. Yalnızca basın toplantısında ifade ettiğim gibi tarafların açıklamaları ve sahada pratik çalışmalar var.” diye konuştu.

Dışişleri Bakanı Hakan Fidan’ın silahsızlanma sürecinde gecikme yaşandığı yönündeki açıklamalarının hatırlatılması üzerine Doğan, Fidan’ın değerlendirmesine katıldığını söyledi.

Doğan, “Gönül isterdi ki silahsızlanma açıklamanın hemen ardında yaşansaydı. Ancak biz başından beri söyledik ki yasal çerçeve hızla çıkmalı, silahsızlaşmanın takvimi geciktirilmemeli.” dedi.

Sürecin daha hızlı ilerlemesi gerektiğini belirten Doğan, silahsızlanmanın takviminin oluşturulması gerektiğini ancak bunun gerçekleşmediğini söyledi.

Doğan, gazetecilerin partisinin anayasa ve cumhurbaşkanlığı adaylığı konusundaki tutumuna ilişkin sorularını da yanıtladı.

Cumhurbaşkanlığı adaylığı konusunda parti içerisinde bir tartışma yürütülmediğini belirten Doğan, Türkiye’nin demokratik bir anayasaya ihtiyacı olduğunu söyledi.

Doğan, anayasanın hazırlanma sürecinin demokratik ve kapsayıcı olması gerektiğini belirterek, “Biz bu tartışmanın öznesiyiz. Bizim anayasa konusunda pazarlığımız yok.” ifadelerini kullandı.

title: Ferdinand Domela Nieuwenhuis - Staten och militarismen
content:
Författare

: Ferdinand Domela Nieuwenhuis

Titel

: Staten och militarismen

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #3 1917


 Staten kan icke existera utan militarismen. De som förklara sig mot militarismen men för staten ha därför icke allvarligt nog begrundat problemet. Dessa tvenne faktorer komplettera varandra.


 Vad är egentligen staten?


 Staten är, under alla sina olika former, ett instrument till förtryck, som den besittande klassen använder sig av för att hålla de besittningslösa i fattigdom och beroende.


 Ju mer man utvidgar statens makt, desto starkare är dess förtryck. Och under den senare tiden har statens makt betydligt ökats, trots alla sociala reformer. Den börda som pressar industriarbetarna (producenterna) har blivit betydligt tyngre. Och det är på dem det hela vilar. Om man tar ett samhälle på 5,000 personer, varav 1,000 producera, så underhålla dessa 1,000 arbetare de 5,000, vilket blir en producent på fem konsumenter.


 Man beräkner att i de europeiska staterna finns femton millioner män som äta ur statens krubba. De äro icke blott parasiter, men de hålla dessutom staternas öden i sina händer.


 Till denna klass hör kungarna, ministrarna, diplomaterna och generalerna, adeln och militärbefälet, alla funktionärer, de som sitta inne med de höga platserna inom industrien etc. För dessa äro kriget, även när det leder till ett nederlag, profitabelt, såväl materiellt som socialt.


 Man säger: det är just därför, som vi måste erövra statsmaskineriet för att göra det nyttigt för de besittningslösa. Tror ni på det?


 En maskin som gjorts för ett visst ändamål, kan icke benyttas till ett fullständigt motsatt ändamål. Allt det där pratet är därför bluff! Staten är en regeringsmaskin, en maktmaskin, och förutsätter alltid ett medel med vilket man kan böja de motvilliga. Den är således ett tvångsinstrument. Kalla det vad ni vill: polis, militarism, - det är sak samma, det är alltid makten som uppträder med våld. Staten är mänsklighetens mest öppna, mest skamliga och mest kompletta negation. Den bryter människornas internationella solidaritet och ersätter den med en begränsad, nationell sammanhållning, och detta just i syfte att förstöra, att erövra och underlägga sig den övriga delen.


 Det finns icke den grymhet, den våldsgärning, det helgerån, den falskhet, det bedrägeri, den nedriga sammansvärjning, den skamliga banditism, det fräcka tjuveri, det förräderi som icke har begåtts och fortfarande dagligen begås under täckmanteln av

statens intresse

.


 Machiavelli erkände det öppet.


 Ty hur betraktade staterna alltid folken? Som en livlös massa, som en för staten avlad köttmassa, tvungen att underkasta sig och betala, bestämd till en evig lydnad.


 Därför har staten behov av militarismen. Den kan icke leva och blomstra utan den. Det är således ett oförnuftigt företag, att bekämpa resultatet, utan att röra vid orsaken.


 Människorna ha blivit utestängda från sin naturliga egendom (jorden) vare sig medelst våld eller list. Och berövade alla arbetsmedel måste de sälja sina krafter och utlämna sig på nåd och onåd till de besittande. Därav kommer slaveriet för den stora massan. Ty vad är det karaktäristiska för slaveriet? Att man

arbetar för andra.

 Nå väl, den stora massan arbetar för andra. Den befinner sig i slaveri.


 Och vem beskyddar och upprätthåller detta tillstånd?


 Staten!


 Staten tjänar således kapitalismens intresse, ty från den får den liv och tillvaro.


 Militarismen utgör en integrerande beståndsdel i staten; man kan således icke klara sig utan den.


 Läs Krapotkins bok:

Den modärna staten

. Där skall man se: "Det är alltid en livlig önskan att få avsättningsmarknad för sina produkter och strävan efter att exploatera de efterblivna folken, som är orsaken till de modärna krigen. I Europa slåss man icke längre för monarkernas ära. Man kastar den ena arméen mot den andra för att skydda de mäktiga herrarna Rotchilds och Schneiders, det mycket aktade aktiebolaget d'Anzin, eller den mycket heliga katolska bankens i Rom inkomster. Kungarna räknas icke längre. Alla krig som förts i Europa sedan hundrafemtio år tillbaka ha varit krig för handelsintressen, för rätten till exploatering." I varje stat finns det en klick, en klass av män, ännu mäktigare än fabrikanterna, som söka nya avsättningsområden, nya källor till rikedom, och som tillskynda krigen. author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als Huhn in der Fleischindustrie leben zu müssen
content:
Die Hühnermast ist ein grausames System, das auf maximale Schnelligkeit, Wachstum und Profit ausgelegt ist und mit einem gewaltvollen Tod für die Tiere endet.


Wie fühlt es sich an, als „Masthuhn“ geboren zu werden

, ohne die Möglichkeit, der leidvollen Industrie zu entkommen

?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Du sollst so schnell wie möglich so schwer wie möglich werden – und wirst dann getötet.


Du kommst in einem Hühnerschlupfbetrieb mit tausenden anderen Küken zur Welt. Um dich herum piepsen sie verzweifelt. Und auch du suchst nach Nähe und Wärme. Aber da ist keine Mutter, in deren Gefieder du dich kuscheln kannst – und du wirst sie auch niemals kennenlernen.

Noch am ersten Tag deines Lebens wirst du über Förderbänder geschleudert und in eine Kiste gepackt. Dann beginnt die oftmals stundenlange Fahrt zum Mastbetrieb – eingepfercht mit Dutzenden anderen Küken, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Du kommst in einer riesigen Halle an. Hier wirst du die nächsten rund 5 Wochen verbringen – die einzigen Wochen deines Lebens.


Um dich herum Tausende andere Küken. Du teilst dir einen Quadratmeter mit bis zu 23 anderen Tieren. Jetzt seid ihr noch klein, doch das wird sich schnell ändern.


Du wächst. Unnatürlich schnell. Das Futter steht dir Tag und Nacht zur Verfügung – hochkalorisch, proteinreich, entwickelt für maximales Wachstum in kürzester Zeit.


Du hast keinen Platz, um dich natürlich zu bewegen, es gibt nichts zum Erkunden. Keinerlei Möglichkeiten, deine natürlichen Verhaltensweisen auszuleben. Es ist trist und laut. Da ist nur diese Enge.


Die Luft ist stickig. Der Ammoniakgeruch von den Ausscheidungen Tausender Tiere brennt in deinen Augen, in deinen Lungen. Du bekommst Atemwegserkrankungen. Jeder Atemzug tut weh.


Dein Körper wurde durch jahrzehntelange Züchtung so manipuliert, dass du in wenigen Wochen das Gewicht erreichst, für das ein Huhn unter natürlichen Bedingungen Monate bräuchte.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Deine Brustmuskeln wachsen so schnell und werden so schwer, dass deine Knochen dein Gewicht nicht mehr tragen können. Deine Beine verformen sich. Dein Herz ist zu klein für deinen massiven Körper, es hat Probleme, deine Organe mit ausreichend Blut zu versorgen. Du hast Schmerzen beim Gehen und deine Gelenke sind entzündet.


Um dich herum sind Hühner, die gar nicht mehr aufstehen können. Sie liegen in ihrem eigenen Kot und leiden unter extremen Schmerzen. Sie verdursten und verhungern.


Andere Hühner werden aufgrund der Enge von ihren Artgenossen versehentlich totgetrampelt und erdrückt – ihre Körper verwesen zwischen dir und den tausenden anderen Tieren. Auch du hast keine Chance, den anderen Hühnern auszuweichen.


Dann ist es soweit. Menschen kommen und packen dich. An deinen Beinen, kopfüber, werden du und deine Artgenossen gegriffen und in enge Transportkisten geworfen. Deine ohnehin schon schmerzenden Beine brechen unter der groben Behandlung. Du hast Schmerzen und Todesangst.


Zusammengepfercht, ohne Wasser, ohne Futter, geht es zum Schlachthof. Die Fahrt kann Stunden dauern. Manche Hühner sterben bereits im Transporter – vor Stress, vor Erschöpfung, erdrückt von anderen Tieren.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Im Schlachthof riechst du Blut. Du hörst die Schreie anderer Hühner. Dann bist du selbst an der Reihe. Unter grausamen Bedingungen wirst du betäubt und getötet. Du bist gerade einmal 35 bis 42 Tage alt geworden.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Hühner in der Fleischindustrie erleiden müssen.


Die Wahrheit hinter „Hähnchenfleisch“


Wie grausam das kurze Leben von sogenannten Masthühnern ist, haben wir schon mehrfach bei Undercover-Recherchen aufgedeckt, beispielsweise in einem (jetzt ehemaligen) Zuliefererbetrieb der großen Marke Wiesenhof. Hier erfährst du mehr über unsere Aufdeckungen und kannst unsere Petition für strengere Tierschutzvorgaben, -kontrollen und -strafen unterzeichnen:


Jetzt für Hühner unterschreiben 


In Deutschland wird mehr Fleisch von Hühnern konsumiert als produziert – und die Nachfrage ist in den vergangenen Jahren stetig gestiegen. Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht: Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel.


In den meisten Supermärkten findest du mittlerweile eine Vielfalt tierfreundlicher Alternativen, die hervorragende Proteinquellen sind – probiere sie aus. Oder koche unsere zahlreichen pflanzlichen Rezepte von Love Veg nach, wie unsere

knusprigen Tofu-Nuggets

.

title: ‘AUTUMN’ HUNTING IS ABOUT AS REAL AS ‘TRAIL’ HUNTING
content:
Cub hunting or ‘autumn hunting’ as it is referred to by hunts, has been underway for a few weeks now and already we are seeing overwhelming reports of foxes running for their lives and aggressive behaviour from hunts whose illegal activity is being exposed.


On the 15

th

 of September the North Cotswold Hunt descended on Wormington in Gloucestershire. A

young fox

 was seen fleeing for its life but this wasn’t the only wildlife disturbed and distressed by the hunts presence, as deer were also seen running towards the very busy B4632.


This young fox was witnessed running for its life.

© Three Counties Hunt Sabs


The Hursley Hambledon Hunt have also been caught demonstrating blatant cub hunting tactics. On the 09

th

 of September while hunting in Meonstoke hounds were entered into a covert and remained there, being encouraged on by the huntsman, for over twenty minutes. Riders and foot supporters lined the covert in an attempt to turn foxes back, but they were unsuccessful as no less than three foxes were seen fleeing the area.


1 of 3 foxes fleeing from the Hursley Hambledon Hunt.

© South Hampshire Hunt Sabs


Meanwhile on the same day over two hours north, the Ledbury Hunt were causing chaos in Berrow. Again, cub hunting tactics were on display for all to see as riders surrounded a covert, saddle slapping and using sticks and voice calls to try and scare foxes back towards hounds. One fox is believed to have been cornered in an area of brambles and unfortunately their fate is unknown.


A short while later another fox was hunted and was thankfully seen to safety by a sab, who reminded the huntsman Sam Jones that he is soon due in court for charges under the Hunting Act while he was huntsman at the criminal Cottesmore Hunt.


This young fox makes its escape from the Ledbury hounds and huntsman Sam Jones.

© Three Counties Hunt Sabs


Grange Farm in Grandborough, a certified Camping and Caravanning site, played host to the Warwickshire Hunt on the 10

th

 of September. The hunt encouraged hounds along a brook just south of the meet and it wasn’t long before a fox was seen running for its life.


A rider attempted to catch up to the fox and turn it back as it fled to safety in a covert. Thankfully sabs were on hand to intervene, battling hollers from the whipper in Jacob Martin, who was actively encouraging hounds on.


This fox was hunted by the Warwickshire Hunt who met at a certified Camping & Caravanning site.

© West Midlands Hunt Sabs


While all of the foxes mentioned above were helped to safety, we are reminded of the sickening and cruel reality of “trail” hunting when sabs are faced with the aftermath of a fox being killed.


Unfortunately, on the 18

th

 of September, Three Counties Hunt Sabs witnessed the Heythrop Hunt kill a fox on land near Swell Wold Farm in Gloucestershire. The fox was surrounded, and the lasting result was blood smeared on a wooden fence while the fox’s innards were left strewn across the floor.


This is the sickening reality of “trail” hunting.

© Three Counties Hunt Sabs


As hunts charge through the countryside in search of innocent lives to take, all manner of wildlife is disturbed, as Cirencester Hunt Sabs reported on the 5

th

 of September while at

the bin bag Beaufort Hunt

. The hunt were on the Badminton Estate, and two quads were seen in a woodland whilst hunt riders circled the perimeter for at least an hour with hounds inside. 

This is not ‘trail’ hunting this is blatant cub hunting.


The hunt eventually moved on from here but disturbed a herd of deer, one of which fled into the road and was hit by a passing car. The couple in the car were left devastated by what had happened as the deer died by the roadside. As is to be expected, the hunt continued on with absolutely no regard for the trauma they had caused and the danger they had put people in.


After running from the Beaufort Hunt this deer was hit by a passing car.

Sabs stayed with them until they passed away.

© Cirencester Hunt Sabs


The Beaufort Hunt continue to terrorise the countryside, and on the 19

th

 of September five foxes were witnessed fleeing from the hunt and were helped safely on their way by Wiltshire Hunt Sabs. On this partiular day the Beaufort focused on hunting three coverts, and again as we are seeing all over the country, cub hunting tactics were employed to encourage younger inexperienced hounds to work a fox’s scent and ultimately kill them.

title: Woman Walks Free From Pig Farrowing Crate After 21 Days And Nights In Trafalgar Square
content:
Animal Rising vows further factory farm exposés as group says three-week action marks beginning of long-term campaign to end factory farming.

Animal Rising campaign lead Michelle Farnham has today (22 September) walked free from a pig farrowing crate in Trafalgar Square after spending 21 consecutive days and nights confined inside it, without leaving once.

Michelle emerged from the crate at 11am, after first entering it at 7am on 1 September, completing an extraordinary physical and psychological challenge designed to bring the reality of factory farming into public view.

She greeted a crowd of approximately 100 supporters and was joined by her partner and family following the three weeks of intense isolation.

Thousands of passersby encountered the installation during its three weeks in one of London’s busiest public spaces, with many stopping to speak with Michelle about the action and the conditions faced by animals in factory farms.

The action attracted national and international media attention, with high-profile visitors including former RSPCA president Chris Packham and Green MP Adrian Ramsay. [1]

Animal Rising said at the event that the end of Michelle’s confinement marks only the beginning of a long-term campaign against factory farming. The group is calling on the government to commit to ending factory farming by 2040 and says further investigations and exposés of conditions inside British farms will follow.

Michelle’s action was inspired by Luna, a mother pig whose life Animal Rising documented for a month on a Suffolk factory farm. [2] Michelle was confined in similar farrowing crate, of the type used in around 90% of indoor British pig farming systems to confine mother pigs around giving birth and nursing their piglets. [3]

Around 200,000 mother pigs are confined in farrowing crates in the UK each year. Sows can spend four to five weeks at a time inside the crates, unable even to turn around. [4]

A petition to free Luna is now approaching 30,000 signatures. [5]

Michelle is available for interview about her experience of spending 21 days and nights inside the crate, the physical and psychological impact of this time, and why she believes the UK must move away from factory farming.

To arrange interviews or follow-up coverage, please contact press@animalrising.org or +44 1225 29 6691

High-quality pictures and videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

[1] https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-16123123/Chris-Packham-woman-pig-crate-Trafalgar-Square.html

[2] Luna investigation and footage: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=efbUsgUYUCA

[3] https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/animal-welfare-strategy-for-england/animal-welfare-strategy-for-england

[4] RSPCA information on farrowing crates: https://www.rspca.org.uk/getinvolved/campaign/farmcages

[5] Free Luna petition: https://act.animalrising.org/free_luna_pet

Le Pig Minimum Standards (PMS) est un référentiel comprenant 9 critères liés aux conditions d’élevage et d’abattage des cochons. Il est soutenu par plusieurs associations de défense des animaux en France et en Europe.

L214 a fait un pas vers E.Leclerc en demandant à la chaîne de supermarchés de s’engager sur un nombre limité de critères du Pig Minimum Standards, dont la faisabilité ne peut être contestée. Il s’agit de s’approvisionner, d’ici 2030, uniquement auprès d’élevages :

ne recourant plus aux cages pour les truies.

Ces critères constituent aujourd’hui le strict minimum pour réduire les souffrances des cochons dans les élevages intensifs. De nombreuses entreprises se sont déjà engagées, comme Pizza Cosy, Boulangerie Ange, Best Western, Marie Blachère, Big Fernand ou encore Columbus Café & Co.

title: Kutschpferde ohne Schutz: Vorstösse in Stadt, Kanton und Bund
content:
Anwohner:innen dokumentierten diesen Sommer in Interlaken

Kutschpferde im Dauereinsatz

: dasselbe Pferd um 14 und um 21 Uhr desselben Tages, bei 31 Grad. Das kantonale Veterinäramt erklärte zu einer Temperaturlimite, die Tierschutzgesetzgebung biete

«keine Grundlage für derartige Anordnungen»

. An dieser Lücke setzen die drei Vorstösse an.


Die

Tierschutzverordnung

 regelt, wie viel Bewegung ein Pferd mindestens braucht – nicht, wie lange es vor der Kutsche arbeiten darf. Hitzeschutz schreibt sie für Wasserbüffel, Yaks und Schweine vor, für Pferde im Geschirr fehlt jede Bestimmung. Die Motion von Nationalrätin Meret Schneider (Grüne) beauftragt den Bundesrat deshalb, die Verordnung zu ergänzen: mit einer Höchstdauer des täglichen Einsatzes und Ruhezeiten, Einsatzgrenzen bei Hitze und einem Fachkundenachweis für das gewerbliche Kutschieren.


«Die Tierschutzverordnung kennt Hitzeschutz für Wasserbüffel, Yaks und Schweine – nur für Pferde, die bei grosser Hitze Kutschen über den Asphalt ziehen, fehlt jede Regel», sagt Meret Schneider. «Diese Lücke kann der Bundesrat auf dem Verordnungsweg schliessen, ohne Gesetzesänderung.»


Wie gross die Risiken auch für Menschen sind, zeigte der

Unfall im Val Roseg

 vom 16. August: Die Bremsleistung einer Kutsche reichte nicht mehr aus, ein Pferd stürzte, das Fuhrwerk prallte gegen einen Baum. Eine 73-jährige Frau starb, zwölf Mitfahrende wurden verletzt. Wer ein Tierfuhrwerk lenkt, braucht nach Bundesrecht einzig das vollendete vierzehnte Altersjahr, eine Prüfung besteht nicht.


Im Grossen Rat verlangt Susanne Clauss (SP) mit der Interpellation «Hitzefrei für Kutschpferde?» Auskunft darüber, wie viele Pferde im Kanton Bern für gewerbliche Kutschfahrten eingesetzt werden, wie der Kanton kontrolliert und was aus den Meldungen aus der Bevölkerung wird.


«Verbindliche Regeln nehmen den sorgfältigen Betrieben nichts weg», sagt Susanne Clauss. «Sie stoppen die Betriebe, die ihr Pferd von Mittag bis Mitternacht durcharbeiten lassen.»


In der Stadt Bern fragt Tobias Sennhauser, Stadtrat von Tier im Fokus (TIF), welche Bewilligungen die Stadt für Kutschenbetriebe erteilt, welche Vorgaben für die Kutschenfahrten des städtischen Tierparks gelten und wie weit ihr Handlungsspielraum reicht – bis hin zu einem Verbot.


«Die Kutsche ist Unterhaltung auf Kosten der Tiere», sagt Tobias Sennhauser. «Wir wollen von der Stadt wissen, ob sie im 21. Jahrhundert daran festhalten will, Pferde zwischen Tram, Bussen und Menschenmengen einzuspannen.»


Andere Städte sind weiter:

Berlin

 lässt seit 2019 ab 30 Grad im Schatten keine Kutschfahrten mehr zu, Barcelona, Madrid und Málaga haben den gewerblichen Kutschenbetrieb ganz beendet.


Der Beitrag

Kutschpferde ohne Schutz: Vorstösse in Stadt, Kanton und Bund

 erschien zuerst auf

Tier im Fokus (TIF)

.
