author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Admin Boots 760K Individuals From ACA Exchanges, Citing Alleged Fraud
content:
One critic decried the move as “a political stunt designed to throw even more people off their coverage.”

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Vice President J.D. Vance and Mehmet Oz, the head of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, jointly announced on Tuesday a plan by the Trump administration to cancel coverage for hundreds of thousands of individuals and families currently enrolled in insurance exchanges within the Affordable Care Act (ACA).

The administration will cancel around 315,000 ACA health plans, which provide health insurance coverage for approximately 760,000 people in the U.S. Both Vance and Oz allege that the plan targets people whose applications neglected to include required information on their applications. Some enrollees may have been added to the ACA — sometimes known as Obamacare — without their knowledge, the pair also alleged.

Yet, many people may face removal simply because their insurance brokers, who helped them enroll, mistakenly did not place their Social Security numbers on submitted documents when they applied.

In response to that action, Vance and Oz announced that over 500 brokers have been warned they could be blocked from taking part in enrolling future participants. CMS also announced a moratorium on new brokers helping people to enroll.

“A blanket moratorium on new agent and broker registrations would punish legitimate professionals instead of targeting the bad actors responsible for fraud,” said Mychal Walker, president of the National Association of Benefits ​and Insurance Professionals.

The bulk removal of individuals enrolled in the ACA exchanges is part of a so-called anti-fraud task force that Vance is leading.

“This is what the fraud task force is all about,” the vice president said at a press conference for the plan, claiming that billions of dollars will be saved by removing these individuals.

“If you care about the ACA, then you’ll want us to take the fraud out,” Oz also stated.

Asked by a reporter whether some eligible individuals could be removed from the ACA rolls, Vance dismissed those concerns, claiming the White House had attempted to reach out to people by mail to prevent that outcome, stating that, “we send them FedEx letters, we go to their house.”

But the flippant attitude of the duo may cause some to question whether they are sincere. At one point, the image of a person alleged to have engaged in fraud was displayed during the presser. “He’s got a very punchable face,” Oz said.

In addition to the 760,000 who were announced to be removed from the ACA health coverage, the duo also said they were examining an additional 400,000 individuals they suspect are part of a larger fraud scheme.

The advocates of social programs have criticized the administration’s purported focus on rooting out fraud as a ruse for cutting benefits and programs that help Americans with lower incomes.

“Families need coverage they can afford and count on when they get sick. Vance’s task force won’t accomplish that,” said Brad Woodhouse, president of Protect Our Care, adding that the vice president’s actions are “nothing more than a bullshit distraction — a political stunt designed to throw even more people off their coverage while pretending to save taxpayers’ money.”

In an op-ed for Truthout in May, Amy K. Matsui, vice president for child care and income security at the National Women’s Law Center, wrote, “These efforts are less about ensuring that public dollars are spent for their intended purpose and more about cutting basic needs programs altogether”:

It’s hard to seriously argue that this administration is concerned with rooting out fraud, considering the president has pardoned wealthy donors convicted of tax fraud, forgoing millions of dollars in restitution. So, I repeat: This is not really about responsible stewardship of public resources or making life more affordable for struggling families.

The announcement of the plan by the Trump administration on Tuesday comes as over 5 million Americans have already dropped their ACA enrollment this year after being unable to afford coverage. Prices have soared after the White House refused to renew subsidies for the program that were introduced during the coronavirus pandemic to help more people gain access to health care.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Threatens Iran With Genocide in Address to UN General Assembly
content:
“Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he said.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump made his most openly genocidal threat yet to Iran on Tuesday, threatening to “annihilate” the country and its 92 million people with “no hope of survival.”

In his opening address to the UN General Assembly in New York City, Trump asserted again that he is facing a choice on Iran about whether to make a deal “that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country.”

“Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” Trump said in his UN speech.

Trump has repeatedly made genocidal threats against Iran, prompting calls for impeachment and war crimes inquiries. These arresting remarks are especially alarming considering that Trump felt emboldened to make them at the highest-level gathering of world leaders, under the flag of an organization created after World War II with the mission of preventing global atrocities.

Human rights experts have previously said that Trump’s threats to wipe out Iran are genocidal. The UN’s Genocide Convention defines genocide as acts carried out “with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.”

Over the nearly seven months of his war on Iran, Trump’s genocidal threats have become commonplace. He has previously said that “a whole civilization will die tonight”; claimed numerous times that there “won’t be anything left” after he strikes the country; and, most recently, pontificated about “if and when do I blow the entire nation up?”

During his remarks at the UN, Trump said that Iran’s air force, navy, nuclear program, and defense equipment have been totally destroyed by the U.S – a dubious claim that he’s made since the first week of the war. He said that Iran’s government “slaughtered 72,000 of its citizens this year,” adding that “recently 10,000 were killed for protesting.”

It’s unclear what events Trump is referencing. Iranian human rights activists have recorded roughly 6,500 protesters killed in mass protests in December and January, far lower than Trump’s 72,000 figure. Many mass gatherings in Iran since then have cheered the government against the U.S. and Israel’s war of aggression.

A UN fact-finding mission also recently found that two U.S. strikes on Iran during the first day of the war were likely war crimes in violation of international laws of civilian protection.

After making his genocidal threat at the UN, Trump claimed “we will make a deal right after the election. It doesn’t make sense for them not to. They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election, what they don’t realize is I am not running.” He said that, once the war is over, oil prices “will come plummeting down even lower than they were at the start of the conflict.”

Analysts have said this claim attempts to manipulate voters amid the president’s record low approval ratings, driven in large part by the war and the affordability crisis that it’s worsened.

In his speech, Trump also threatened Cuba, saying that his administration is “seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba,” where he said left-wing leaders have “spent decades coordinating with the left-wing radicals and communist networks here in the United States.”

author: Renée Feltz
title: Tennessee Is Days Away From Executing a Sexual Assault Victim
content:
Christa Pike’s lethal injection is booked for September 30. She may be the first woman Tennessee executes in 200 years.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Christa Pike was sexually abused and raped from the time when she was a toddler until almost a year to the day before she was arrested in 1995 at age 18 for murdering fellow teenager Colleen Slemmer when the two attended a job training program for troubled youth in Knoxville.

Tennessee officials do not dispute these facts. “I think everybody in this courtroom wishes that those things had never happened to Ms. Pike,” Tennessee Attorney General’s Office lawyer Will Ayers acknowledged in his closing argument to a grueling three-day hearing last month about challenges to Pike’s execution scheduled for September 30. “I think we all wish that we were not here today and that she was not on death row.”

In a new approach, the state’s Supreme Court appointed Shelby County Senior Judge Mark Ward as a “special master” to hear the arguments by Pike’s defense team, including that lethal injection would be cruel and unusual because it could trigger traumatic memories, among other reasons.

“We’ve all heard of flashbacks,” said clinical psychologist Dr. Bethany Brand, who testified that such memories can “intrude so intensively that the person loses all awareness of where they actually are, and what’s happening, and they instead are reliving what they lived through already.” Brand interviewed Pike in 2023 and found the “level of trauma she was subjected to … is almost impossible to grasp because it is so severe.”

Experts in the field of trauma and sexual violence filed an amicus brief in the case arguing there is “substantial risk” that the execution would cause Pike to re-experience what she endured as a girl and teenager and “it will be as horrific for her now as it was then.”

“Once she is restrained and immobilized, a man will try to find a vein in Ms. Pike’s arm through which he will inject the poison that will kill her,” notes the brief. “If he cannot find a vein in her arm, the expectation is that he will attempt to inject the poison near her groin.”

But a week after the hearing, Ward concluded Pike’s team had “failed” to prove she would face “needless suffering,” or could “avoid mental suffering” if the state used any other method besides lethal injection.

If the justices agree with Ward’s “findings,” then Pike’s lawyers say they will appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court. They have also submitted a clemency petition to Republican Gov. Bill Lee, asking him to commute her sentence to life in prison without parole, noting that Pike’s life of abuse went unad­dressed by the adults and state sys­tems meant to pro­tect her, and she has accepted responsibility for her crime and expressed deep remorse. Otherwise, she will be the first woman Tennessee executes in over 200 years, and the last person sentenced to death in the state for a crime committed at such a young age, the petition states.

author: Kourosh Ziabari
title: No English Test for You: Trump’s Campaign Against Iran Now Targets Education
content:
By restricting access to standardized tests, the US is effectively blocking Iranians from applying to schools abroad.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

As U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration tightens its repressive measures against Iran, Iranian students and applicants of English proficiency tests have become the latest targets of a campaign by the White House to severely constrain Iran’s connections with the rest of the world.

With the war on Iran nearing the end of its seventh month, the U.S.-Israeli bombing operations have been supplanted by new tactics, including a package of sweeping sanctions rolled out on August 24, which the Department of the Treasury has labeled as “Economic D-Day,” calling it an “unprecedented, whole-of-government, economic campaign” that will continue until “Tehran stands alone.”

As part of this economic offensive, the Office of Foreign Assets Control has revoked several sanctions regulations licenses, including Iran General License G, which previously allowed academic exchanges and authorized certain educational services in Iran, such as tests of English proficiency that are administered worldwide.

Now, young Iranians seeking educational opportunities overseas are saying their prospects are being undermined: International companies conducting credentialed tests in Iran have ceased their local operations, and third countries where Iranian students could travel to take the tests are also turning them away.

The Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), Pearson Test of English (PTE), and International English Language Testing System (IELTS) are among the standardized tests that academic institutions in English-speaking and some other countries expect international applicants to pass as a requirement of enrollment in their programs.

Other additional tests are often required by higher education institutions during the admission process, including the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE). For years, these tests have enabled cohorts of young Iranians to follow their educational aspirations in places like the U.K., Canada, and the United States, where they remain some of the largest populations of international students despite stringent visa policies.

This slow but steady trickle of opportunity may now be halted as the U.S. blocks Iranians from satisfying the basic conditions of applying to schools. There are also concerns that overcompliance may add arbitrary prohibitions to the existing rules, worsening discrimination against people of Iranian heritage based on their country of origin or perceived nationality, even if they’re residents of other countries.

“I had one student who had taken the PTE exam in Van and wanted to retake two skill sections, but unfortunately, she was told that because of the new restrictions, she couldn’t participate using an Iranian passport,” said Mona Poorverdi, a 41-year-old English teacher in northern Iran, referring to an applicant she knew who was barred from sitting for the exam in Turkey earlier this summer.

Administered by the London-based Pearson plc, the test includes multiple modules, including PTE Academic, which is accepted by universities in Britain, Australia, and New Zealand. The multinational company, whose chair is the Iranian American businessman and Google’s former Chief Business Officer Omid Kordestani, has now announced that it will comply with the U.S. sanctions and will not schedule or deliver exams for candidates who are residents of Iran.

Shortly after the Treasury’s campaign was set in motion, the New Jersey-headquartered Educational Testing Service (ETS) announced the indefinite suspension of TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran. The private educational assessment organization, which administers a range of language proficiency and certification exams, said the action was “required to comply with U.S. sanctions law.”

Pearson plc and ETS didn’t respond to Truthout’s request for comment.

Other private companies have also joined the U.S. government’s economic warfare targeting everyday life in Iran. Starting September, the Pennsylvania-headquartered educational technology company Duolingo has placed a moratorium on Iranian citizens taking its Duolingo English Test, citing the Trump administration’s sanctions.

Developed in 2016, the online language assessment test is accepted by hundreds of institutions in Anglophone countries, including Yale …

title: Doğan: We expect important developments in the coming days
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan spoke on current developments following her party’s first Central Executive Board (MYK) meeting after its 5th Ordinary Congress.


According to Doğan, the meeting addressed the party’s work for the new period, the new legislative term, the Peace and Democratic Society Process, as well as economic and social developments.


‘We expect important developments’


Commenting on the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Ayşegül Doğan said they viewed the framework law adopted by Parliament as the first step in the process.


She said efforts regarding disarmament were continuing through contacts between state officials, Abdullah Öcalan and the PKK leadership, adding that reciprocal efforts were also underway on the ground.


“We expect important developments regarding disarmament in the coming days,” Ayşegül Doğan said.


She added that an announcement would be made when there were concrete developments arising from these efforts that could be shared with the public, noting that no definite date had been set.


Öcalan’s role


Ayşegül Doğan said that Abdullah Öcalan’s role in the process should not be considered solely from a single perspective.


Disarmament on the one hand, political transition on the other


Ayşegül Doğan further stated the following:


“For the efforts being carried out on the ground to yield results and continue effectively, Mr. Öcalan needs to be part of the relevant committee. His formal involvement in the work as coordinator for disarmament and political transition would have an extremely positive impact. That is why we consider this important.


There will also be a need for certain working groups that can contribute to the efforts on disarmament and political transition. These developments will be important for identifying and establishing those groups and for enabling the work to move swiftly toward a conclusion.


Therefore, Mr. Öcalan’s role needs to be discussed not from a single perspective, but in all its various dimensions: disarmament on the one hand and political transition on the other. Because this process is about making a lasting transition from conflict to democratic politics. All mechanisms must operate accordingly.


Committees must work effectively and in coordination


Following the establishment of the Monitoring and Evaluation Committee after the law was enacted, we are now able to hold these discussions. The Monitoring and Evaluation Committee, as stipulated by the law, held its first meeting on August 24. At a press conference we held afterward, following discussions within our Central Executive Board, we emphasized the importance of the fact that this committee had been established quickly, had convened, had begun its work, and was carrying out activities on the ground.


A committee was established and subcommittees were formed. However, no public statement has yet been made regarding who will serve on these four subcommittees or how they will operate. Nor has any information been provided on the matter.


As the DEM Party, we have previously stated that it is very important for these committees to work effectively, in coordination and in close cooperation with one another. We reiterate this.


The new term beginning on October 1 will be very important


We emphasize that the new term beginning on October 1 will be a very important period for peace and democracy. Parliament has major responsibilities in permanently ending the conflict, strengthening democratic politics, and removing obstacles to political participation. All political parties, and of course the Speaker of Parliament in particular, have crucial roles to play. Parliament Speaker Mr. Kurtulmuş periodically informs the public about this issue and makes statements regarding the steps that need to be taken.


Fair representation must be ensured


We are also working to complete our preparations for the new legislative term. It will be an intense period. The process of establishing this committee should be completed immediately after Parliament reconvenes. title: PJAK member remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after arrest by Iranian intelligence
content:
Sirwan Habibi, a member of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested him in Kamyaran, Kurdistan Province.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that Habibi’s family has repeatedly visited Ministry of Intelligence offices and courts in Kamyaran and Sanandaj in recent days, seeking information about his situation. However, the authorities have continued to deny any knowledge of his arrest.


Habibi, from Sanandaj, is known within PJAK by the organisational name Aram Sine. The continued lack of information about his fate, together with the absence of any judicial case registered in his name at the courts in either city, has heightened concerns about his condition and whereabouts.


KHRN has spoken to several residents of Kamyaran’s Besat neighbourhood who witnessed his arrest, obtaining further details about the circumstances.


According to witnesses, dozens of civilian vehicles with tinted windows used by the Ministry of Intelligence agents surrounded several streets in the neighbourhood on the evening of 8 September. At about 01:00 local time on 9 September, agents began pursuing Habibi as he rode a motorcycle.


Witnesses said one of the vehicles struck his motorcycle at high speed, causing it to overturn, before agents used violence to arrest him.


Bystanders called the police emergency number, 110, and approached to help him after the motorcycle overturned. Plainclothes forces fired into the air to disperse them.


One witness said: “A few minutes later, a police patrol responding to the 110 call arrived, unaware of what was happening. But security forces blocked its path, said it was a security matter and forced the officers to leave.”


The witnesses said Habibi resisted arrest, but agents beat him, covered his face with a cloth and put him in a Samand car before taking him away.


In a statement issued on 14 September, PJAK said Habibi had been carrying out an organisational mission and was unarmed when Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested him. The party said his fate remained unknown.


KHRN’s findings show that, before the US-Israeli war with Iran, most people arrested by the Ministry of Intelligence and the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in Kurdistan Province were taken to the two agencies’ detention facilities in Sanandaj, where they were held and interrogated.


Following US and Israeli air strikes on those facilities, security agents have been holding detainees in secret detention facilities operated by the Ministry of Intelligence and in solitary confinement in prisons in the cities concerned.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Compares AI Warnings to Past Climate Fears He Wrongly Says Were a “Hoax”
content:
Millions of people have died as a direct result of the climate crisis.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump has dismissed legitimate concerns about the growth of artificial intelligence (AI), comparing them to the “hoax” of the climate crisis.

“The same people that said, ‘We’ll all be dead in twelve years because of Global Warming’ … are the people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us, that robots are going to attack us, and everything is a DISASTER,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

The president’s comments came a week after reports about the U.S. military nearly starting a war with China after relying on false information from AI, and after the world experienced its hottest month on record in August.

Trump also claimed that “nobody was dead” due to climate change, and compared AI concerns to the investigation into election interference by Russia during his first term in office, and his impeachment over withholding aid from Ukraine in order to get political “dirt” on Joe Biden, wrongly describing both of those situations as “a Hoax.”

In dismissing worries over the expansion of AI — which tech experts and developers themselves have said should be slowed down until proper safeguards are instituted — Trump made a false claim about the climate crisis: that no one has died from it.

In fact, millions of people around the world have lost their lives due to its impacts.

According to a Lancet Countdown report published last fall, which was authored by 128 experts from 71 different academic institutions, 546,000 deaths have occurred from heat exposure on average each year over the past decade. It also found that 84 percent of heatwave days in the past five years of data wouldn’t have happened without the effects of the climate crisis, and that droughts induced by the climate crisis have also led to 123.7 million more people experiencing food insecurity around the world than observed between 1981 and 2010.

“We’re seeing millions of deaths that are occurring needlessly every year because of our persistent fossil fuel dependence, because of our delay in mitigating climate change, and our delays in adaptation to the climate change that cannot be avoided,” said Marina Romanello, executive director of the Lancet Countdown at University College London.

Extreme weather events, which are becoming more numerous and severe due to climate change, have caused at least hundreds of thousands of deaths over the past 20 years.

“From 1995 to 2024, more than 832,000 lives were lost … driven by more than 9,700 extreme weather events,” reads an explainer from GermanWatch’s Climate Risk Index. “The frequency and intensity of climate-related disasters continue to rise, and these figures underscore the urgent need for climate action.”

A University of Wisconsin-Madison study published in 2022 found that eliminating air pollution from energy-related activities could reduce premature deaths in the U.S. by more than 53,000 annually. Put another way, by ending the country’s dependence on fossil fuels and shifting to renewable energy sources, the U.S. could save a number of lives nearly equivalent to the population of Madison every five years.

AI data centers will also worsen the climate crisis.

According to a 2015 analysis from Cornell University researchers, by 2030, the current rate of AI growth will add 24 to 44 million metric tons of carbon dioxide to the atmosphere every year. That amount is equal to 5 to 10 million cars added to U.S. roads annually. Water usage to cool these data centers would also equal the annual household usage of 6 to 10 million Americans per year.

author: Daron Letts
title: From ‘Fore!’ to ‘Play ball!’: Golf event makes Iqaluit minor softball league reality
content:
Minor league softball is coming to Iqaluit in summer 2027, thanks to more than $220,000 raised by the Iqaluit Charity Golf Tournament in Gatineau, Que.


“This support will give more young people a chance to be active, learn new skills and take part in organized recreation,” said Iqaluit Mayor Solomon Awa Monday in a news release.


Organized by Outcrop Communications, more than 130 golfers took part in the Sept. 17 event, which also attracted approximately 30 corporate sponsors.


The donations are destined for the Ikajuqtiit Community Association, a non profit, Iqaluit-based organization that enhances recreational opportunities for local youth, including improvements to the Iqaluit ball diamond.


The funds will cover uniforms and equipment for the new league, said association chair Tom Fitzgerald Tuesday in a phone interview.

The money will also pay for the installation of artificial turf in the outfield.


Those materials are scheduled to arrive next July on the first sealift of 2026, at no charge by Nunavut Sealink and Supply Inc., he said.


It is the first time the association has been the beneficiary in the charitable event’s 19-year history.


 Habitat for Humanity Iqaluit usually receives the funds that the event raises.


However, because Habitat for Humanity had no projects planned for Iqaluit this year, organizers chose to support Ikajuqtiit, said Outcrop Communications CEO Jen Hayward Monday in a phone interview.


The city’s recreation department will organize and administer the league, Fitzgerald said.

Reprise du séminaire «

 

Comprendre et agir dans la complexité : pour une théorie de la situation

 

»


 |&nbsp7 septembre 2025


Le séminaire du collectif Malgré Tout « Penser et agir dans la complexité » fait sa rentrée pour nouvelle saison 2025/26 ! L' objectif de ce séminaire peut se résumer ainsi : chercher une nouvelle « terre ferme » (…)


Nous poursuivrons cette année notre étude théorique et pratique de la situation, comprise comme socle organique minimal de l'agir.


Premier séminaire de cette année :


Séminaire


Présentation des axes de la saison 2026/2027


Avec la fin de l'époque de l'homme - sujet autoproclamé face à un monde réduit au statut d'objet - se pose une question centrale : quelle instance multiple peut encore penser, sentir et agir dans le chaos contemporain

 

?


La crise actuelle produit un vécu quotidien marqué par la dispersion, l'impuissance et l'angoisse devant un monde qui échappe à nos grilles de lecture. Le travail que nous proposons repose sur un pari : faire de la situation le dispositif à partir duquel il devient possible d'affronter cette dispersion sans céder à la tentation d'un nouvel ordre disciplinaire.


autres dates


Une telle exigence suppose de rompre avec l'imaginaire occidental de la fixité, qui n'a cessé de chercher l'être du côté de ce qui demeure, se conserve et résiste au devenir. Notre époque appelle au contraire une réconciliation avec le devenir, non comme abandon à la dispersion, mais comme condition d'une éthique situationnelle du présent.


Comme nous l'avons précédemment montré, la complexité ne relève ni d'une théorie ni d'une simple interprétation. Elle constitue un mode objectif et concret du monde qui exige un changement de paradigme, capable de renouer avec la puissance d'agir.

author: Luan Matheus Santana
title: “Usem muito Gemini”: Educação vira porta de entrada das Big Techs no Piauí
content:
Zona leste de Teresina. A sala de aula de uma escola estadual tem estrutura similar às demais instituições de ensino do Piauí: é ampla, tem paredes claras e as mesas estão organizadas para atividades em grupo. Alguns elementos, porém, chamam atenção. A sala é equipada com Chromebooks. No centro, uma poltrona reproduz as cores e o formato do logotipo do Google. As mesas e cadeiras também seguem a paleta da multinacional: azul, vermelho, amarelo e verde. Ao fundo, ocupando praticamente toda a parede, um grande painel visual exibe a outra logomarca, a do Google for Education. 


“Gostaram dessa sala? Mais uma sala tecnológica, de inovação, padrão Google, viu?”, disse o então secretário estadual de educação do Piauí, Washington Bandeira, em vídeo compartilhado nas redes sociais na época. Depois, ele conta aos alunos com orgulho que o pessoal do Liceu paraibano visitou a sede do Google nos Estados Unidos.

“Usem muito o Gemini, porque o Google é nosso parceiro no ensino de IA”, completou, referindo-se à inteligência artificial.  


Publicação de Washington Bandeira sobre a parceria do estado do Piauí com o Google na área da educação


A “sala Google” no Centro de Educação Tecnológica Professor Darcy Ribeiro foi a primeira inaugurada pelo governo estadual, em 20 de março de 2025. À época, o espaço foi apresentado como um marco da modernização da educação pública. Além de Teresina, outras duas cidades do Piauí, Regeneração e Amarante, também instalaram “salas Google” em escolas da rede pública. Estes ambientes coloridos, porém, são apenas um símbolo da proximidade do governo do Piauí com o Google e demais Big Techs.


Pelo menos desde 2022, o governo do Piauí tem firmado contratos milionários com multinacionais de tecnologia. O governador do estado, Rafael Fontelles (PT), é candidato à reeleição e tem aparecido como favorito nas pesquisas de intenção de voto. 


Um levantamento realizado pela

Agência Pública

 identificou R$ 93,7 milhões em acordos diretos e indiretos firmados pelo governo do Piauí nos últimos quatro anos com empresas como Google, Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon Web Services (AWS), além de empresas locais que atuam como integradoras de serviços das multinacionais.

A maior parte destes contratos se referem a recursos para a área de educação. Foram R$ 36,4 milhões, mais de um terço do total. 


Os contratos destinam-se à compra de plataformas digitais, infraestrutura em nuvem, licenças de software, equipamentos, soluções de inteligência artificial e, em muitos casos, para contratação de revendedores e integradores nacionais. 


Parte desses recursos estão sendo investidos em tecnologia para o ensino de inteligência artificial nas escolas da rede pública. O estado foi o primeiro no Brasil a incluir a IA como disciplina obrigatória em 2024 – em algumas instituições, a ferramenta usada para o ensino de IA é a Teachable Machine, do Google. Em junho de 2026, o governo lançou um novo programa para levar o ensino de IA também às escolas municipais. Inicialmente, o projeto será implantado em 50 municípios, com previsão de alcançar todas as 224 cidades do Piauí até 2027. 


Pesquisadores, especialistas em educação digital e organizações de defesa de direitos digitais questionam o modelo adotado no Piauí e em outros estados da federação. Eles alertam para o risco de dependência tecnológica e para a ausência de mecanismos transparentes de governança, proteção de dados e avaliação do impacto dessas tecnologias. 


Inauguração da ‘sala Google’ em Teresina


“É evidente que tem uma assimetria de poder, um acúmulo de saberes e de tecnologia bastante desigual entre os países do Norte e do Sul global”, afirma Rodrigo Nejm, doutor em psicologia e especialista em direitos digitais e educação digital no Instituto Alana. Para ele, é completamente possível reconhecer as assimetrias de capacidade tecnológica sem, para isso, “legitimar uma dependência de submissão”. 


“O problema não é fazer uso de plataformas internacionais, mas é permitir que elas abusem e violem direitos dos estudantes no Brasil”, completa. Para Nejm, parte dos milhões de reais destinados à transformação digital da educação deveria ser utilizada para desenvolver “soluções livres, nacionais, se possível, mas que fossem auditáveis, transparentes, para que, por exemplo, o Tribunal de Contas ou um profissional da imprensa pudesse ter acesso integral a informações sobre o critério de funcionamento, ou as evidências das ciências da aprendizagem que fundamentam”, explica …

author: Katja Diehl
title: 2,5 Milliarden. Verbrennen.
content:
Es ist leider gar nicht so schwer, DIE Stimme zur intersektionalen Mobilitätstransformation zu sein, wenn Gesellschaft und Politik bis heute bei Mobilität Auto und am liebsten auch Verbrenner denken.


2,5 Milliarden Euro für fossile Kraftstoffe – was wäre damit möglich?


Bund und Länder haben sich auf einen erneuten Tankrabatt ab dem 1. Oktober 2026 geeinigt. Es ist bereits der dritte Versuch innerhalb weniger Jahre, steigende Spritpreise durch kurzfristige Steuersenkungen zu kompensieren. Während massiv in die Subventionierung von Benzin und Diesel investiert wird, bleiben die strukturellen Defizite im öffentlichen Nahverkehr ungelöst.


Aus Sicht der Mobilitätsgerechtigkeit stellt sich mir die Frage:


Wie lange wollen wir noch mit der Gießkanne Milliarden ausschütten, während für jede Wahlfreiheit in der Mobilität durch Busse, Bahnen, Radwege angeblich kein Geld da ist?


Menschen in Armut, die auf das Auto angewiesen sind, ein geringes Einkommen haben und oft in ländlichen Regionen leben, wo Alternativen fehlen.


Mit denselben 2,5 Milliarden Euro ließen sich Hunderte Kilometer neuer Radwege bauen, On-Demand-Rufbus-Systeme im ländlichen Raum etablieren oder kindgerechte, sichere Räume schaffen. Selbst ein flächendeckendes Sozialticket wäre finanzierbar.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Trump Administration Aims to “Asphyxiate” Cuba Into Submission, Diplomat Says
content:
Meanwhile, the CIA recently formed a new secret task force as part of a widening US effort to destabilize Cuba.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

As the United Nations General Assembly opens in New York, we speak with senior Cuban diplomat Carlos Fernández de Cossío, who says the Trump administration is seeking to “asphyxiate the people of Cuba into submission.” On Friday, millions in Cuba lost power in what was at least the sixth major blackout since President Trump cut off fuel shipments to the island in January. The fuel blockade comes on top of the six-decade-long U.S. economic embargo and countless attempts to topple the communist government.

“We will do all we can to stop any nation, the U.S. or any nation, from taking over Cuba,” says Fernández de Cossío, who has served as deputy Cuban foreign minister since 2022.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman in New York. Juan González is in Chicago.

As world leaders gather for the United Nations General Assembly here in New York, we turn now to look at Cuba, which is facing a growing humanitarian crisis amidst an escalating economic war waged by the Trump administration. On Friday, millions in Cuba lost power in what was at least the sixth major blackout since President Trump cut off fuel shipments to the island in January. The fuel blockade comes on top of the six-decade-long U.S. embargo. Residents of Havana say they have no water or electricity in their homes.

VALENTIN PARRA: [translated] It’s very bad for everyone, because everyone gets desperate in a house without water and without light. It’s a phenomenon that isn’t seen anywhere else in the world, only here. And when people don’t have water — look, I myself was without water for 15 days, without water or light for 15 days. The luck is that I could bathe over here and bathe on the other side. But tell me: What does someone do who doesn’t have that possibility?

AMY GOODMAN: Meanwhile, the CIA recently formed a new secret Cuba task force as part of a widening U.S. effort to pressure Cuba. According to the Times, the CIA is adding case officers who recruit and manage spies, as well as officers who conduct cyber operations and specialize in covert influence operations.

The U.S. has made many attempts to overthrow the Cuban government over the past 65 years, hundreds of attempts. In 1960, the CIA formed a Cuba task force that oversaw the failed Bay of Pigs invasion on April 17th, 1961. The Guardian recently reported allies of President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have already begun vying for control of Cuba’s assets if the Cuban government falls under the U.S. pressure. The Wall Street Journal just published an article headlined “The Backroom Meetings in Miami Where Cuba’s Future Is Being Plotted.”

To talk about all of this, we’re joined by Cuba’s Deputy Foreign Minister Carlos Fernández de Cossío.

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: It is an honor.

AMY GOODMAN: Thanks so much for being with us. I’m glad we’re within the 25-mile zone that you’re allowed to travel in in New York. Right? Twenty-five miles from Columbus Circle?

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: Columbus Circle, yes.

AMY GOODMAN: Number one, if you can talk about what is — as the foreign minister addresses the United Nations, what’s the Cuban government’s message to the Trump administration as it tightens the economic sanctions and embargo?

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: We will be speaking to the international community at the U.N., not necessarily to the U.S. government, but the U.S. belongs to the international community. We live in a world which has become very dangerous, where expansionism, the ambition of domination, the attempts to take over the natural resources of developing countries has come back to the stage. The U.N. was created precisely for that not to happen, and has developed precisely for not that to happen, yet as reality today as a result of a foreign policy that is conceptualized as peace through force, which implies imposing the will of the U.S. through intimidation, aggression, coercion and so on. So, that’s one point that we need to talk.

We need to talk about the plight of the people of Cuba, because the aggression of the United States against Cuba today has a very serious human face …

title: İki gündür kayıp olarak aranıyordu: Ormanda cansız bedeni bulundu
content:
Kütahya - Tavşanlı ilçesinde 2 gündür kayıp olarak aranan gece bekçisi Hikmet Uzuncan (42), ormanda otomobilinin içinde ölü olarak bulundu.

Devekayası mevkiindeki özel bir şirkette gece bekçisi olarak çalışan Hikmet Uzuncan, 2 gün önce otomobiliyle evinden çıktıktan sonra kendisine haber alınamadı. Yakınları çevrede yaptığı aramalarda Uzuncan’dan bir iz bulamayınca kayıp ihbarında bulundu.

Yapılan incelemede Uzuncan’ın otomobiliyle 2 gün önce Tavşanlı-Kütahya kara yolu üzerindeki bir akaryakıt istasyondan yakıt alıp ayrıldığı belirlendi. Arama çalışmalarını akaryakıt istasyonun çevresinde yoğunlaştırılan jandarma ekipleri, Şahmelek mevkiindeki ormanda otomobili tespit edildi.

Otomobilde yapılan aramada ise Uzuncan'ın cansız bedeni bulundu. Jandarma ve savcılık incelemesinin ardından Uzuncan’ın cansız bedeni, hastane morguna kaldırıldı. Uzuncan’ın ölüm nedeni, yapılacak olan otopsinin ardından netlik kazanacak.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Senator Says European Nations Must Sanction Trump, Rubio Before US Wrecks ICC
content:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen said that Trump and Rubio’s attacks on the ICC seek to obstruct investigations into Netanyahu.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A U.S. senator has called on foreign leaders to impose sanctions on top U.S. officials as the Trump administration wages a campaign to dismantle the International Criminal Court (ICC).

Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) said that, if they “have any self-respect,” nations party to the ICC would take steps to stop the Trump administration’s meddling. It is extraordinary for such a call to come from a sitting member of congress.

“If European countries & other signatories to the International Criminal Court have any self-respect, they’d sanction Rubio & Trump for obstructing investigations of [Israel Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu’s war crimes,” the senator said in a post on social media on Monday.

When the Trump administration first announced sanctions against the court last year, a group of 79 countries, including major European powers like the U.K., France, and Germany, signed a statement opposing the move. “Such measures increase the risk of impunity for the most serious crimes and threaten to erode the international rule of law, which is crucial for promoting global order and security,” they wrote.

But, despite such statements, many of those nations have not taken decisive action to rein in the Trump administration — and, even further, have continued to capitulate to the administration on many repressive requests throughout Trump’s second term.

Van Hollen’s post came in response to a Wall Street Journal report that the administration is preparing yet more sweeping sanctions against the ICC. These sanctions, which have not been finalized, “forbid most transactions with the ICC after a grace period of six to seven months,” the Journal reports. Such sanctions could have wide-ranging consequences due to the U.S.’s vast control over global financial systems.

The sanctions sought by the Trump administration mark an escalation in its campaign against the ICC, the end goal of which, as Rubio has stated, is to “dismantle” the court. The U.S. has previously sanctioned individual members of the court, including the current president of the ICC, Tomoko Akane, as well as the lead prosecutor in the case against Netanyahu for crimes against humanity in Gaza.

Sanctions on the entire court could make it even harder for the ICC to carry out prosecutions of Netanyahu and other global leaders accused of committing human rights violations. Adil Haque, a professor of international law at Rutgers University, also noted on Monday that “Congress could pass a law stripping presidential power to sanction international institutions and their staff.”

The Trump administration has claimed that the ICC is a threat to American sovereignty. Analysts have said that the administration’s true goal is not to protect sovereignty, but to shield the U.S. and other allies from facing consequences for past and future abuses.

In his speech before the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, President Donald Trump reiterated his attacks on the ICC. He said that the ICC is an “evil group of people,” and called on all 125 member countries to “resign” from the body.

“We will never allow U.S. service members to be investigated or anyone else to be investigated, or given show trials by an anti-American tribunal with no jurisdiction over us,” Trump said.

His remarks came days after two separate UN reports suggested that U.S. officials could be investigated and prosecuted for war crimes in Iran and military actions in central and South America.

title: İran’dan Hürmüz Boğazı açıklaması: Geçiş düzenlemelerine uymayan gemilerin yüklerinin yüzde 20'sine el konulacak
content:
Yarı resmi Tesnim Haber Ajansı'na göre, İran Meclisi Ulusal Güvenlik Komisyonu Sözcüsü Hasan Kaşkavi, Hürmüz Boğazı’na ilişkin oluşturulan “Hürmüz Boğazı'nın Güvenliğinin Sağlanmasına Dair Stratejik Eylem Planı” hakkında konuştu.

İran Meclisi Ulusal Güvenlik Komisyonu’nda Stratejik Eylem Planı’nın 13, 14 ve 15. maddelerinin onaylandığını söyleyen Kaşkavi, Ceza Kanunu’nun 5. maddesine göre, 13. madde ile Hürmüz Boğazı’nda oluşturulan geçiş düzenlemelerine uymayan gemilerin taşıdığı yükün yüzde 20’sine el konulacağını veya yüzde 20'lik yükün değeri ölçüsünde ceza kesileceğini belirterek, cezanın ödenmemesi halinde gemilere de el konulacağını kaydetti.

Kaşkavi ayrıca, 14. maddeye göre Hürmüz Boğazı ile ilgili iki ülke arasında oluşturulan belge veya çok taraflı uluslararası anlaşmaların İran Anayasası’nın 77, 125, 176 ve 57. maddeleri çerçevesinde olması gerektiğini söyledi.

Kaşkavi, İran Genelkurmay Başkanlığının ilgili kanunun uygulanmasını takip etmekle görevli olduğunu ve bu hususun 15. maddede yer aldığını hatırlattı.

İran Ceza Kanunu’nun 5. maddesinin A fıkrasına göre, İranlı olsun veya olmasın, İran’ın iç ve dış güvenliğine, toprak bütünlüğüne veya bağımsızlığına karşı girişimde bulunanlar, İran’ın egemenliği dışında kalan alanlarda olsa bile, işlediği bazı suçlardan dolayı İran kanunlarına göre yargılanabiliyor.

author: Amir Khafagy
title: NYC Announces Largest Food Delivery Worker Settlement Ever Reached in US
content:
DoorDash reached a $131.5 million settlement agreement for underpaying nearly 260,000 delivery workers.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Immigrant delivery workers have long alleged that DoorDash has shortchanged them out of their hard-earned wages. Now, the city has announced a historic settlement that aims to make them square — and then some.

On Tuesday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) Commissioner Samuel Levine announced a $131.5 million settlement agreement with DoorDash for underpaying nearly 260,000 delivery workers.

The settlement follows a years-long DCWP investigation that found DoorDash failed to pay thousands of workers for all the time they worked, and failed to pay thousands more workers on time. DCWP will contact the affected workers directly, and said they expect workers will receive compensation equivalent to approximately 200% of the amount they were initially underpaid.

Additionally, DCWP found that DoorDash violated the city’s delivery worker Minimum Pay Rate law, which is currently set at $22.13 per hour for time spent on active delivery, regardless of a worker’s immigration status. And although DoorDash increased hourly pay for its workers in December 2023, the company still found ways to exclude some delivery workers from receiving the minimum hourly wage.

As per the terms of the agreement, over $115 million will go directly into delivery workers’ pockets, and DoorDash will be forced to pay more than $16 million in additional civil penalties. The city estimates that since at least 2022, more than 260,000 workers were underpaid by DoorDash, including workers who were not paid at all or were paid late by days and, in some cases, weeks.

According to the city, this is the largest labor enforcement action in New York City history as well as the largest food delivery worker settlement ever reached in the entire country.

“When a worker earns a wage, they deserve to be paid that wage — not tomorrow, not after a lawsuit, but on time and in full,” said Mayor Mamdani in a statement shared with Documented. “No corporation is above the law, and this administration will keep fighting until every worker gets the pay and protections they deserve.”

DoorDash spokesperson Samantha Ramirez acknowledged that the company had failed to pay some workers, but stressed that it was not deliberate, but merely a mistake.

“Simply put, we screwed up,” she told Documented in a statement. “Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late. While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them okay. We pride ourselves on operational excellence at DoorDash, and this was not excellent, nor was it acceptable.”

Ramirez said less than 1% of all payments to delivery workers were affected, with around $6.6 million in wages withheld from workers. Another $5.7 million in wages arrived days or, in some cases, weeks late. Overall, Ramirez says, 65% of impacted workers were underpaid by $1 or less.

“We’re making things right by paying every impacted Dasher what they are owed and fixing what caused this so it doesn’t happen again,” said Ramirez.

The settlement goes beyond compensating for past violations. Going forward, as part of the settlement, DoorDash must submit detailed data reports to DCWP every month for three years, which the agency will use to monitor the company’s compliance with the law and the terms of the settlement.

The case was first brought to the city’s attention by The Workers’ Justice Project (WJP) in 2023 after they found that 200 DoorDash workers had had their wages stolen beginning in 2022. Since then, they have continued to put pressure on the city to act. Now the city has finally delivered.

“This historic settlement is a major victory for thousands of Deliveristas across New York City who have been organizing for basic rights and building their own union, Los Deliveristas Unidos,” said Ligia Guallpa, executive director of WJP, in a statement shared with Documented. “For too long, DoorDash treated workers as disposable, stealing their wages and deactivating them, leaving families without the income they rely on. This settlement puts money back in workers’ pockets and holds DoorDash accountable.”

For workers like Rosendo Tacam, who first brought this case to light in 2023, the settlement announcement is a vindication …

title: Eskişehir’de Eğitim Sen’den okul saldırısı tepkisi: Okullarda şiddeti sona erdirecek somut adımlar acilen atılmalıdır
content:
Eskişehir – Eğitim Sen Eskişehir Şubesi, Manisa’nın Turgutlu ilçesinde İnci Üzmez Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi önünde öğrencileri hedef alan silahlı saldırıya tepki göstermek amacıyla Köprübaşı’nda basın açıklaması yaptı. Açıklamayı Eğitim Sen Eskişehir Şube Başkanı Özkan Demirkol okudu.

Manisa’nın Turgutlu ilçesinde sabah saatlerinde okul önünde gerçekleşen silahlı saldırıda 11 öğrencinin yaralanmasına dikkat çeken Demirkol, okullarda her geçen gün tırmanan şiddet olaylarının ve öğrencilerin yaşam hakkını tehdit eden saldırıların münferit vakalarla geçiştirilemeyeceğini söyledi.

Okullarda yaşananların eğitim sisteminin içine sürüklendiği yapısal krizin, derinleşen toplumsal şiddet ikliminin ve öğrencilerin can güvenliğini yok sayan ihmaller zincirinin doğrudan sonucu olduğunu belirten Demirkol, “Okullarda şiddeti sona erdirecek somut adımlar acilen atılmalıdır” dedi.

Milli Eğitim Bakanlığının eğitim alanındaki temel sorunlara çözüm üretmek yerine “önlük” gibi şekilci dayatmalarla ve öğretmenlerin giyim kuşamıyla gündem oluşturduğunu söyleyen Demirkol, Bakanlığın bu yaklaşımından vazgeçmesi gerektiğini ifade etti.

Demirkol, “Okullarda ve okul çevrelerinde öğrenciler saldırıların hedefi olurken, eğitim emekçileri her gün şiddet riskiyle yüz yüze çalışırken, Bakanlığın eğitimin asıl ve hayati sorunu olan ‘güvenli okul, güvenli gelecek’ talebini görmezden gelmesi ve kamuoyunu tamamen şekilci meselelerle meşgul etmesi kabul edilemez” diye konuştu.

Öğrencilerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin yaşam hakkını ve güvenliğini tehdit eden sorunların görmezden gelindiğini belirten Demirkol, giderek derinleşen şiddet ikliminin halı altına süpürüldüğünü söyledi. Demirkol, bunun MEB’in eğitimin gerçek ihtiyaçlarından ve sahadaki yakıcı gerçeklerden ne kadar kopuk olduğunu gösterdiğini ifade etti.

Okulların aşırı güvenlikçi denetim alanlarına dönüştürülmesinin eğitim kurumlarının toplumsal ve demokratik dokusunu zedelediğini söyleyen Demirkol, öğrencilerin potansiyel birer “suç öznesi” olarak görülmesine dayanan yaklaşımların çözümsüzlüğü derinleştirdiğini belirtti.

Kalıcı çözümün okulları yalnızca güvenlikçi bir anlayışa teslim etmekten geçmediğini vurgulayan Demirkol, Psikolojik Danışmanlık ve Rehberlik (PDR) hizmetleri ile sosyal hizmet uzmanlarının eğitim sürecinin merkezine alınması gerektiğini söyledi.

Demirkol, “Okullarda psikolojik danışman, rehber öğretmen ve sosyal hizmet uzmanlarının görevlendirilmesi sıradan kontenjan hesaplarına ya da masa başında belirlenen sayılara göre değil; her okulun bulunduğu çevrenin sosyo-ekonomik koşulları, öğrencilerin ihtiyaçları ve somut riskler dikkate alınarak planlanmalıdır” dedi.

MEB’in eğitim ortamlarında yaşanan sorunlara şekilci ve polisiye yöntemlerle yaklaşmaktan vazgeçmesi gerektiğini belirten Demirkol, önleyici, koruyucu, pedagojik ve sosyal destek mekanizmalarının güçlendirilmesini istedi.

Eğitim sisteminin uzun süredir devam eden temel sorunlarından birinin kalabalık sınıflar olduğunu ifade eden Demirkol, sınıf mevcutlarının derhal azaltılması gerektiğini söyledi. Öğrenciler ve eğitim emekçileri açısından daha sağlıklı ve güvenli eğitim ortamlarının oluşturulması gerektiğini belirtti.

Müfredatın yalnızca sınava odaklı eleme ve yarıştırma mantığından çıkarılması gerektiğini söyleyen Demirkol, öfke kontrolü ve akran zorbalığıyla mücadele gibi konuların yanı sıra kültür, sanat ve sporla desteklenen güçlü bir pedagojik yapının oluşturulması gerektiğini ifade etti.

Demirkol, okulların güvenliğinin yalnızca polisiye yöntemlerle sağlanmaya çalışılmaması gerektiğini belirterek öğrencilerin sosyal, duygusal ve pedagojik ihtiyaçlarına yanıt verecek yeterli sayıda psikolojik danışman, rehber öğretmen ve sosyal hizmet uzmanının istihdam edilmesini istedi.

Eğitim Sen olarak Milli Eğitim Bakanlığına çağrıda bulunan Demirkol, öğrencilerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin can güvenliğinin sağlandığı, güçlü pedagojik bağların kurulduğu nitelikli ve demokratik bir okul ikliminin oluşturulması gerektiğini söyledi.

Demirkol, “Yeni saldırıların önüne geçilmesi için gereken önlemler vakit geçirmeksizin alınmalıdır” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Tony Blair Wants Governments to Embrace AI, Not Slow It Down
content:
Tony Blair’s think tank has called for governments to embrace AI and rebuild their states around the new technology despite the risks posed to workers, societies and security.


The former Labour prime minister, who has multiple ties to the tech sector, has backed a new paper arguing that countries risk being left behind if they do not adapt to the AI era.


Blair’s vision for AI-powered governance was set out in a

paper

 released by his think tank, the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI).


“Countries cannot protect themselves from AI by ignoring it,” the paper argues. “The only meaningful path is to engage with it, building institutions capable of operating at the speed and complexity of the world now emerging, and harness AI to transform how the state itself works.” 


The institute’s paper does not make reference to Blair’s own relationship with the tech industry, including the hundreds of millions of dollars in funding his institute has received from tech moguls. 


Larry Ellison, the billionaire founder of software company Oracle, which is heavily invested in infrastructure driving the AI boom, has given

around £257m in donations and pledges

 to Blair’s think tank since 2021.


In February, campaign group

Foxglove criticised the UK government

 for collaborating with Blair’s think tank on AI implementation, stating: “Ministers seem to be unable to spot a potential conflict of interest which is blindingly obvious to everyone else.”


Despite acknowledging the risks to labour markets, the dangers of concentrating technological power and increased exposure to biological threats, the answer is not to slow development but instead to “harness and control it”, he wrote.


“This AI revolution will be happening to you and you won’t be guiding it,”

Blair added in a video interview posted on X

.


Earlier this month, a handful of AI executives

called for a global slowdown

 in AI development in response to warnings about the existential threat posed by the new technology. However, other

tech leaders – including the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia – questioned

 if Silicon Valley bosses were motivated more by safety concerns or by their fears of increased competition.

author: Acratosaurio rex
title: ¿Conocer nuestro pasado impedirá cometer sus errores?
content:
Otro de los grandes mitos del anarquismo español (1), es que su auge a finales de los siglos XIX y principios del XX, proviene del hecho de que los anarquistas no se contentaron con hacer propaganda o actuar de forma individual o en pequeños grupos de afinidad. Nuestros antecesores en España, entraron en organizaciones obreras de carácter sindical, organizaciones que atraían a sus miembros por intereses: mejoras salariales, reducciones de jornada, seguros sociales, educación, ocio… De. Esta manera agruparon desde los sindicatos a cientos de miles de trabajadores que no eran anarquistas, y que entraron así en contacto con la cultura que podemos llamarla libertaria: autonomía de partidos, solidaridad, acción directa, rechazo de representantes parlamentarios, organizaciones confederadas, etc. A diferencia de lo que sucedía en otros países donde había jefes, dirigentes, líderes de origen burgués metidos en partidos a la conquista del Estado, en el mundo sindical libertario había militantes, portavoces y referentes que eran obreros sin excepción, y que miraban con indiferencia en general, la lucha de partidos.

En fin, que el mito de la CNT, nos muestra a anarquistas más o menos convencidos, que lejos de agruparse en pequeñas organizaciones, o como decía Malatesta, en partidos anarquistas compuestos solo por anarquistas, los anarquistas españoles se mezclaron con el mundo sindical, al que dotaron de impulso, creatividad y estatutos. Por supuesto, no fue una organización perfecta la CNT que surge de las sociedades de resistencia, de los sindicatos de oficio y del Sindicato Único. La mezcla de Anarquismo + sindicato de masas + acción directa + autonomía política dio lugar a una criatura portentosa, multifacética, mítica. Hay libros de historiadores que hablan de incompetencias de la CNT, y yo os digo que no: lo hicieron todo bien. Porque como te pongas a buscar errores y a creértelos, seguro que los acabas cometiendo. So pringao, que eres un pringao con ínfulas de historiador.

Los obreros y obreras del siglo XX, adoptaban una serie de consignas que les llenaban la imaginación de posibilidades. Nada de propaganda farragosa. Por ejemplo en el campo, la consigna era la Tierra, la Unión, el Trabajo y Cumplir. No me preguntes que significaba para ellos y ellas ese asunto, os dejo que os lo imaginéis. ¿Eran anarquistas? Tal como puedes serlo tú, no. De hecho en Andalucía la FAI en los años treinta llegó a tener 743 afiliados en toda la región. La CNT tenía más de 300.000. ¿Podían setecientas y pico de personas desperdigadas por un país enorme, sin teléfonos, sin internet, sin coches, sin dinero… Dominar, mandar o dirigir a cientos de miles? Pues en mi opinión, no podían.

Bueno, son esas cosas las que me llaman la atención de este 90 aniversario de la pelea del 36. Y me sorprende como los anarquistas de libro, los de verdad que leen cosas y le dan vueltas a la cabeza todo el puto día, han renunciado a dirigirse a los trabajadores actuales a través de la ventana que les proporciona las franquicias anarcosindicalistas, que no serán perfectas para los exigentes estándares de calidad libertaria que gasta la peña. Vale. Pero tampoco es para enfadarse con ella y echarle la cruz a un amado mito sindical y libertario, que ha resistido –modestamente– los últimos y complejos 90 años.

Recuerda: conocer los errores del pasado, permite repetirlos. Eso es muy cansao.

author: Unknown
title: Le nuove regole della Resistenza
content:
Gli Houthi – o più propriamente

Ansar Allah

 -, negli ultimi giorni hanno colpito e conquistato territori e isole fondamentali per il controllo dello stretto di Bab El-Mandeb, minacciando la chiusura alle petroliere saudite e paventando la possibilità di un inasprimento della crisi energetica globale, andando ad aggiungersi alle significative conseguenze del blocco di Hormuz.


Ricordiamo che a luglio scorso, gli Houthi – che già controllavano la regione della capitale Sana’a – sono riusciti a cacciare le forze filo-governative dalla costa sud-occidentale, prendendo il controllo della città portuale di Mokha, importante centro strategico, dell’isola di Mayyun e delle isole Hanish. Tutti territori già oggetto di contesa, poiché permettono un controllo potenzialmente totale sulla viabilità dello stretto. Tutto questo è avvenuto a seguito della crisi di Hormuz e alla scelta obbligata delle petromonarchie di spostare la circolazione sull’altro lato della penisola arabica (Bab el-Mandeb, appunto), permettendo di attenuare – seppure lievemente – la strozzatura sul mercato petrolifero. La guerra civile era scoppiata nel 2014, dopo l’inizio delle operazioni militari del gruppo sciita zaidita nelle regioni ovest del Paese. Le forze armate yemenite sono state sostenute negli ultimi dodici anni – durante i quali gli Houthi hanno mantenuto pressappoco gli stessi territori fino alla scorsa settimana -, da Arabia Saudita ed Emirati Arabi Uniti, finanziati e aiutati a loro volta dagli Stati Uniti. 


L’Arabia è il maggiore esportatore di petrolio dei paesi OPEC e la sua economia, nonostante i piani di diversificazione della produzione, è ancora basato sull’export di petrolio per il 45% del PIL. Colpire il suo commercio petrolifero significa quindi assestare un colpo durissimo tanto al paese quanto al mercato del petrolio su scala globale. Inoltre il blocco è avvenuto contestualmente al sabotaggio da parte di milizie filo-iraniane in Iraq dell’oleodotto East-West, che aveva permesso, insieme a Bab el-Mandeb, di far fronte alla chiusura di Hormuz. L’offerta di greggio saudita è scesa a circa 6 milioni di barili al giorno, raggiungendo il minimo storico dal 1990 ad oggi. Se poi l’oleodotto non verrà ripristinato in tempi brevi, provocando uno stop pressoché totale all’export saudita, vi è la possibilità di un crollo del 4% dell’intera offerta globale. Attualmente gli Houthi stanno tenendo in scacco, seppur precario, l’Arabia Saudita, tanto nella sua funzione di sostegno al governo Yemenita quanto nel suo ruolo di alleato USA fondamentale per la strategia di gestione del Medio Oriente.


La guerra si inserisce infatti nella spaccatura tra Iran, di cui gli Houthi sono alleati, e paesi arabi allineati alla strategia Israelo-americana di contrasto all’Asse della Resistenza. Strategia che appare sempre più fallimentare man mano che il tempo passa. Trump infatti, dopo le richieste saudite di intervenire in Yemen, ha risposto con un secco diniego: la prospettiva di un’ulteriore campagna fallimentare – utile solo a dimostrare l’inefficienza militare USA in contesti di guerra “ibrida” – sarebbe politicamente ed economicamente insostenibile. Decisione di certo comprensibile se si considerano le elezioni midterm alle porte, ma che ha come conseguenza un rinnovato e, per il momento, sicuro margine di manovra militare per le milizie di Ansar Allah. Il perdurare della crisi potrebbe però spingere gli USA ad intervenire nonostante le imminenti elezioni. Sul versante regionale appare invece evidente lo sfaldamento dell’alleanza Arabia – Emirati, o per lo meno un allontanamento dei loro obiettivi anche sul breve periodo. L’esercito yemenita si trova infatti praticamente spaccato in due parti, una sostenuta dal regno di Saud e l’altra dagli Emirati. Questa divisione, che ha origine dalle divergenze strategiche dei due paesi – come spiegato

qui

 -, si ripercuote sui risultati politici di Israele e degli USA ottenuti con gli accordi di Abramo. Non significa certo che le alleanze USA stiano per crollare definitivamente, ma il frazionamento causato dai conflitti in corso e la resistenza – e il contrattacco – dell’Iran ne mettono a dura prova la tenuta. Come d’altra parte non si parla di una vittoria immediata dell’Asse della Resistenza: sulla carta le possibilità tecniche di colpire gli Houthi ci sarebbero.

author: The Canadian Press
title: ‘Dooming the moose’: Manitoba Cree chief calls for voluntary stop to hunting
content:
The leader of a First Nation in Manitoba is urging all moose hunters to stop hunting in the community’s traditional territory due to what she calls dwindling population numbers.


Misipawistik Cree Nation Chief Heidi Cook is advocating for a “voluntary hunting closure” of an approved game hunting area that encompasses a large part of the community along the northwestern shores of Lake Winnipeg.


Cook is appealing to all hunters, including members of Misipawistik, to prioritize the long-term health of the moose population by halting harvesting in the area beginning Monday, when the season opens.


“At this moment in time, the moose population just cannot sustain that harvest. So we’re asking all Manitobans to stand with us in protecting moose and calling on our government to do better,” Cook said in an interview.


“We need to take action, all of us collectively, to protect that moose population so that it can be there for generations of hunters to come. This is our responsibility.”


Cook said information last year from the province, based on an aerial survey, estimated 64 bull moose were in the area.


The government has made 62 bull moose tags available for the same area this year, said the chief.


That doesn’t take into account community hunters, who have treaty rights to hunt on their traditional territory and don’t require government-issued licences or tags.


A provincial spokesperson said in an email Friday that the government’s survey found the moose population remained stable since the last survey in 2013.


While 62 tags were available this year, the spokesperson said fewer hunters applied and 37 licences were allocated. The government projects a harvest of nine bull moose.


The First Nation disputes the province’s position on the moose population, saying it has observed a sharp drop in the number harvested by members.


Cook said historically the community would harvest up to 19 moose in a season but that hasn’t happened for the past 10 to 15 years.


A government report detailing the 2013 survey recorded a historic low number of moose for the area. It attributed the low numbers to fires, forestry and mineral exploration, and suggested further disturbances to the animal’s habitat over the following 10 to 20 years.


The First Nation has been raising concerns with the province for years about the moose, said Cook, but it hasn’t seen much “meaningful change.”


“What our people have been experiencing for a number of years is that it’s almost an involuntary closure. We just don’t have the moose,” she said.


“This is something that is part of our responsibility. We have a right to moose, but we also have a responsibility to protect that moose and make sure that it can survive and be healthy.


“If we continue with the hunt as is, we’re dooming the moose to not being able to be available for future generations.”


Manitoba Keewatinowi Okimakanak, an advocacy group representing some northern First Nations, supports Cook’s call for a voluntary halt to hunting.


“When First Nations’ leaders raise concerns about the health of a population and the future sustainability of a resource, those concerns must be taken seriously by Manitoba,” Grand Chief Garrison Settee said in a statement.


Cook said areas south of the First Nation have seen total hunting closures because of the way the province has managed the moose population.


In 2024, Misipawistik warned the province its members couldn’t meaningfully hunt for moose in their territory and asked the government to put licences on hold.


The government reduced the number issued and committed to working with the community to determine moose population dynamics and the First Nation’s food needs, but Cook has said that didn’t happen.


The First Nation took the province to court last year in an attempt to halt moose harvesting in its territory, arguing it infringes on the community’s right to hunt for food and that moose are important for social and ceremonial purposes.


The importance of the animals affects the community in more ways than “just an empty freezer,” added Cook.


“It’s hard, because the moose is such an important cultural species. It’s tied to our relationship with the land, the sharing that happens between families, just the seasonal rhythms of being out and having those moose camps.”


In 2018, Misipawistik developed a land guardian program to track moose in the area.


Cook said the program has been successful in reducing poaching and animals …

author: William Turton
title: Trump’s FBI Scrapped Bribery Investigation Linked to Sen. Susan Collins
content:
A top donor told agents his company won millions in federal contracts by bankrolling campaigns of powerful politicians.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In the final weeks of 2019, a top fundraiser for Sen. Susan Collins walked into a perilous meeting at a Corner Bakery in Washington, D.C.

For the first time in her two-decade Senate career, the Republican lawmaker from Maine was in danger of losing her seat. President Donald Trump’s dismal approval ratings were dragging her down in the polls, and she was falling behind her likely 2020 Democratic challenger in fundraising.

Scott Reed, head of the Collins super PAC, was on a mission to close that gap. Reed was meeting that day with three executives from a Hawaiian defense contractor, Navatek. A year earlier, Collins had helped their company land a multimillion-dollar Navy research contract in Maine. Now, seated at a coffee shop not far from the U.S. Capitol, Reed asked them for a $500,000 donation.

Government contractors are banned from making political contributions. More consequentially, for the company to offer donations to Collins in exchange for an official action, or for Collins to accept, would constitute criminal bribery.

But the company did have such a proposal: Navatek was hungry for more government contracts in Maine. If they cut a big check, the CEO told Reed, Navatek wanted Collins to guarantee tens of millions of dollars in additional federal funding.

To skirt campaign finance laws and conceal the source of the funds, Navatek planned to funnel the donation through a shell company. The CEO wanted assurance that Collins would know where the money came from. Reed confirmed that she would, the executive said — and that Navatek would get its government contracts.

After the Corner Bakery meeting, Navatek’s CEO, Martin Kao, sent an initial $150,000 to the Collins super PAC using the shell company. Two months later, he told Navatek executives that Collins committed to getting the company $32 million in naval contracts, according to an internal company email reviewed by ProPublica.

Three years later, Kao holed up in a conference room to recount the Corner Bakery meeting to a group of four FBI agents and federal prosecutors. The FBI had seen through his shell company ruse, and in 2022 a grand jury indicted him for making illegal campaign contributions. No one working for Collins was charged.

Facing years in prison, Kao hoped to do less time by revealing the entire scheme.

What he told them has never before become public. The Corner Bakery meeting, he asserted, was just one episode in a sprawling pay-to-play operation that embroiled some of the most powerful figures in Congress.

Over three days at the U.S. attorney’s office in Honolulu, Kao laid out in devastating detail how his operation worked. He gave agents a 50-page document naming dozens of lobbyists, congressional staffers and members of Congress who he said helped him trade cash for contracts. Kao and his close associates had donated nearly $900,000 to dozens of politicians, allowing Navatek to establish operations in half a dozen states with over $40 million a year in government funding.

Most damningly, Kao told FBI agents and prosecutors, the company’s work for the government was of no real value. Navatek’s research under his stewardship never resulted in products the military wanted to buy, ProPublica found.

Kao’s tell-all interviews with the FBI lasted into late 2024. His confessions opened up an entirely new phase of the investigation. Agents sifted through hundreds of thousands of records seized during Kao’s arrest and found that many were consistent with his account of widespread influence peddling.

Kao had credibility issues. He was now a felon trying to avoid a lengthy prison sentence. And there were other challenges. Building a corruption case against elected officials requires extraordinary proof of a quid pro quo arrangement, in part because the Supreme Court has narrowed what counts as bribery.

Even so, by the end of 2024, the agents had enough evidence to pursue a sweeping bribery probe that could ensnare top lawmakers of both political parties. They asked their supervisors to approve a new investigation and contemplated using undercover operatives to gather more evidence. Although their effort was in its early stages, and it was unclear where it would lead, FBI agents asked Kao extensive questions …

Artikel von Anna Merlan vom 25. Februar 2025 in Mother Jones

Trump verbietet CNN, MS NOW und Politico den Zugang zum Weißen Haus – Klagen und Soli-Boykott großer US-Sender, dem sich sogar Fox News anschließt


Trumps Streit mit Medien eskaliert: Der US-Präsident stellt Medien als Müll dar – und verbannt sie aus seiner Regierungszentrale. Stattdessen gibt es jetzt »Trump TV«.


„

Nach dem Rauswurf des TV-Senders CNN aus dem Weißen Haus eskaliert die Fehde zwischen Präsident Donald Trump und mehreren US-Medien. Die Sender CNN und MS NOW sowie das ebenfalls vom Ausschluss betroffene Nachrichtenportal »Politico« ziehen vor Gericht, um ihre Plätze im Weißen Haus zurückzuerkämpfen. Und der Streit zieht noch weitere Kreise: Die engmaschige TV-Begleitung auf Terminen und Reisen Trumps, die über ein Rotationsprinzip großer Fernsehsender geregelt ist, wurde von diesen gestoppt – als Protestaktion, weil CNN Teil dieses sogenannten Pools ist.


Mitten in diesem Streit ging das Weiße Haus am Montagabend (Ortszeit) mit einem eigenen Online-Kanal auf Sendung. Der Stream namens »Trump TV« zeigte zunächst Reden des Präsidenten sowie Übungen der US-Streitkräfte, deren Schlagkraft gepriesen wurde. Laut dem Weißen Haus wird »Trump TV« täglich rund um die Uhr laufen – »mit den besten Momenten aus der Vergangenheit, Ankündigungen sowie den neuesten und wichtigsten Nachrichten aus der Regierung«. Eigene Produktionen oder journalistische Inhalte waren zunächst nicht zu sehen.


Selbst Trumps Lieblingssender Fox News protestiert…


In einer gemeinsamen Stellungnahme der TV-Sender hieß es, die Öffentlichkeit habe ein grundlegendes Interesse daran, unabhängige Informationen über ihre Regierung zu erhalten – und keine Regierung solle eine Nachrichtenorganisation einschränken, nur weil sie deren Berichterstattung missbillige. Bemerkenswert ist, dass das Statement von allen fünf TV-Sendern kam – und damit auch von Fox News. Das ist eigentlich Trumps Lieblingssender, der häufig wohlwollend über ihn berichtet und ihm sehr viel Platz im Programm einräumt.


Auch die »New York Times« solidarisierte sich mit den »ungerecht ins Visier genommenen« Medienhäusern. Die Zeitung war am Montag für den Pressepool eingeteilt, der für Fotos zuständig ist. Als Reaktion auf den Ausschluss von CNN und Co. kündigte sie an, die am Montag aufgenommen Bilder nicht weiterzugeben und auch selbst nicht zu veröffentlichen. Die »Washington Post« teilte ebenfalls mit, keine Fotos von Auftritten des Präsidenten am Montag zu veröffentlichen.


CNN, »Politico« und MS NOW reichten ihre Klage bei einem Gericht in der Hauptstadt Washington ein. Das Verbot sei eine »Bedrohung für die Pressefreiheit und das Recht der Öffentlichkeit auf unabhängigen Journalismus ohne Einmischung der Regierung«, erklärten die Medien in einer gemeinsamen Mitteilung. Die Klage der Medien wurde als Eilantrag eingereicht. Das heißt, dass sich ein Gericht zügig mit dem Fall befassen muss. Beantragt wurde, das Verbot unverzüglich zu kippen
